library(shiny)

### renderPlot replacement: Safari 27 (WebKit) cannot hold the call stack of
### shiny::renderPlot in webR ("Maximum call stack size exceeded"), so draw with
### renderImage instead, which nests about 45 fewer R calls
renderPlot <- function(expr, width = "auto", height = "auto", res = 72, ...,
                       env = parent.frame(), quoted = FALSE) {
    func <- shiny::exprToFunction(expr, env, quoted)
    shiny::renderImage({
        info <- shiny::getCurrentOutputInfo()
        w  <- if (is.numeric(width))  width  else info$width()
        h  <- if (is.numeric(height)) height else info$height()
        shiny::req(w > 0, h > 0)
        pr <- shiny::getDefaultReactiveDomain()$clientData$pixelratio
        if (is.null(pr)) pr <- 1
        f   <- tempfile(fileext = ".png")
        dev <- shiny:::startPNG(f, w * pr, h * pr, res = res * pr)
        on.exit(grDevices::dev.off(dev), add = TRUE)
        grDevices::dev.control(displaylist = "enable")
        v <- withVisible(func())
        if (v$visible) print(v$value)
        list(src = f, contentType = "image/png", width = w, height = h,
             coordmap = shiny:::getCoordmap(v$value, w * pr, h * pr, res * pr))
    }, deleteFile = TRUE)
}

### ---------- model functions -------------------------------------------------
### a mixture of K = 3 bivariate normals; theta = list(pi, mu (K x 2), S (2 x 2 x K))
K <- 3
COLS <- c("#E69F00", "#0072B2", "#009E73")       # one colour per component

## log density of N2(mu, S) at the rows of X
ldbvn <- function(X, mu, S) {
    det <- S[1, 1] * S[2, 2] - S[1, 2]^2
    Si  <- matrix(c(S[2, 2], -S[1, 2], -S[1, 2], S[1, 1]), 2) / det
    D   <- sweep(X, 2, mu)
    -log(2 * pi) - 0.5 * log(det) - 0.5 * rowSums((D %*% Si) * D)
}

## log of pi_k * phi(x | mu_k, S_k), one column per component
log_joint <- function(th, X)
    sapply(seq_len(K), function(k) log(th$pi[k]) + ldbvn(X, th$mu[k, ], th$S[, , k]))

row_lse <- function(L) { m <- apply(L, 1, max); m + log(rowSums(exp(L - m))) }

## E-step: responsibilities (n x K) and the observed log-likelihood
e_step <- function(th, X) {
    L <- log_joint(th, X); lse <- row_lse(L)
    list(R = exp(L - lse), loglik = sum(lse))
}

## M-step: weighted proportions, means and covariances
m_step <- function(R, X) {
    Nk <- colSums(R)
    mu <- t(sapply(seq_len(K), function(k) colSums(R[, k] * X) / Nk[k]))
    S  <- array(NA_real_, c(2, 2, K))
    for (k in seq_len(K)) {
        D <- sweep(X, 2, mu[k, ])
        S[, , k] <- crossprod(D * sqrt(R[, k])) / Nk[k] + diag(1e-6, 2)
    }
    list(pi = Nk / nrow(X), mu = mu, S = S)
}

## a component is "degenerate" if it has (almost) no points or a flat covariance
degenerate <- function(th)
    any(!is.finite(unlist(th))) || any(th$pi < 1e-8) ||
    any(apply(th$S, 3, function(S) S[1, 1] * S[2, 2] - S[1, 2]^2) < 1e-8)

em_path <- function(th0, X, no_iters) {
    TH <- list(th0); LL <- e_step(th0, X)$loglik
    th <- th0
    for (i in seq_len(no_iters)) {
        th <- m_step(e_step(th, X)$R, X)
        if (degenerate(th)) break
        TH[[i + 1]] <- th
        LL[i + 1] <- e_step(th, X)$loglik
    }
    list(TH = TH, LL = LL)
}

### ---------- data sets (true parameters) -------------------------------------
cv <- function(s1, s2, r) matrix(c(s1^2, r * s1 * s2, r * s1 * s2, s2^2), 2)
datasets <- list(
    "well separated, equal weights" = list(
        pi = rep(1/3, 3), mu = rbind(c(0, 0), c(4, 0), c(2, 3.5)),
        S = list(diag(2), diag(2), diag(2))),
    "overlapping, equal weights" = list(
        pi = rep(1/3, 3), mu = rbind(c(0, 0), c(2.2, 0), c(1.1, 1.9)),
        S = list(diag(2), diag(2), diag(2))),
    "correlated shapes, unequal weights" = list(
        pi = c(0.5, 0.3, 0.2), mu = rbind(c(0, 0), c(3, 3), c(4, -1)),
        S = list(cv(1, 1, 0.8), cv(1.2, 0.7, -0.6), cv(0.5, 1.2, 0))),
    "only two true clusters (K = 3 overfits)" = list(
        pi = c(0.5, 0.5), mu = rbind(c(0, 0), c(4, 1)),
        S = list(cv(1, 1, 0.3), cv(1, 1, -0.3)))
)

make_data <- function(spec, n, seed) {
    set.seed(seed)
    z <- sample(seq_along(spec$pi), n, replace = TRUE, prob = spec$pi)
    X <- t(sapply(z, function(j) spec$mu[j, ] + drop(t(chol(spec$S[[j]])) %*% rnorm(2))))
    colnames(X) <- c("x1", "x2")
    X
}

### ---------- starting values ---------------------------------------------------
starts <- c("random data points as means", "random labels",
            "means near the centre")

make_start <- function(how, X, seed) {
    set.seed(seed)
    S0 <- array(cov(X), c(2, 2, K))
    ctr <- colMeans(X)
    mu <- switch(how,
        "random data points as means" = X[sample(nrow(X), K), ],
        "random labels" = {
            lab <- sample(rep_len(seq_len(K), nrow(X)))
            t(sapply(seq_len(K), function(k) colMeans(X[lab == k, , drop = FALSE])))
        },
        "means near the centre" =
            matrix(ctr, K, 2, byrow = TRUE) + matrix(rnorm(2 * K, 0, 0.05), K))
    list(pi = rep(1 / K, K), mu = unname(mu), S = S0)
}

### ---------- UI ---------------------------------------------------------------
## an icon-only playback button; the title shows as a tooltip
ctrl_btn <- function(id, icon_name, title, class = "btn-default")
    actionButton(id, NULL, icon = icon(icon_name), title = title, class = class,
                 style = "flex: 1; padding: 6px 0;")

## a checkbox with a short label; the tooltip gives the full meaning
short_check <- function(id, label, tip, value)
    checkboxInput(id, tags$span(label, title = tip), value, width = "auto")

ui <- fluidPage(
    ## ---- control panel: two rows --------------------------------------------
    wellPanel(
        ## generate the data
        fluidRow(
            column(4, selectInput("dataset", "True mixture", choices = names(datasets),
                                  width = "100%")),
            column(4, sliderInput("n", "Sample size n", min = 60, max = 600,
                                  value = 300, step = 30, width = "100%")),
            column(3, div(style = "padding-top: 25px;",
                          actionButton("newdata", "Regenerate a dataset",
                                       class = "btn-warning", style = "width:100%;")))
        ),
        hr(style = "margin: 4px 0 8px;"),
        ## the starting value, the playback and the display options
        fluidRow(
            column(3, selectInput("start", "Start EM from", choices = starts,
                                  width = "100%")),
            column(2, sliderInput("maxit", "Iterations", min = 5, max = 200,
                                  value = 60, step = 5, width = "100%")),
            column(3, div(style = "display: flex; gap: 4px; padding-top: 25px;",
                          actionButton("newstart", "New start",
                                       title = "Draw a new starting value of the chosen kind",
                                       style = "flex: 1.8; padding: 6px 2px;"),
                          ctrl_btn("first", "backward-fast", "Back to the start"),
                          ctrl_btn("back",  "backward-step", "One iteration back"),
                          ctrl_btn("play",  "play",          "Play / pause",
                                   class = "btn-primary"),
                          ctrl_btn("step",  "forward-step",  "One iteration forward"),
                          ctrl_btn("toend", "forward-fast",  "To the end"))),
            column(4, div(style = "display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; column-gap: 14px; padding-top: 22px;",
                          short_check("uncertain", "Hollow if unsure",
                                      "Hollow points: largest responsibility below 0.9", TRUE),
                          short_check("truth", "True means",
                                      "Mark the true means with red crosses", FALSE),
                          short_check("autoplay", "Autoplay",
                                      "Start playing whenever the data or the start change",
                                      FALSE)))
        )
    ),
    ## ---- plots ----------------------------------------------------------------
    fluidRow(
        column(7, plotOutput("fit", height = "560px")),
        column(5, plotOutput("ll",  height = "280px"),
                  plotOutput("pis", height = "280px"))
    )
)

### ---------- server -----------------------------------------------------------
server <- function(input, output, session) {

    dseed <- reactiveVal(812); sseed <- reactiveVal(1)
    observeEvent(input$newdata,  dseed(dseed() + 1))
    observeEvent(input$newstart, sseed(sseed() + 1))

    X <- reactive(make_data(datasets[[input$dataset]], input$n, dseed()))

    path <- reactive(em_path(make_start(input$start, X(), sseed()), X(), input$maxit))
    nlast <- reactive(length(path()$TH) - 1L)     # last iteration reached

    ## ---- iteration state driven by the playback buttons ---------------------
    t_cur   <- reactiveVal(0L)
    playing <- reactiveVal(FALSE)

    ## any change to the data or the starting value restarts the display
    observeEvent(path(), {
        t_cur(0L)
        playing(isTRUE(input$autoplay) && nlast() > 0)
    })

    observeEvent(input$play, {
        if (isTRUE(playing())) playing(FALSE)
        else {
            if (t_cur() >= nlast()) t_cur(0L)    # replay from the start
            playing(TRUE)
        }
    })
    observeEvent(playing(), {
        updateActionButton(session, "play",
                           icon = icon(if (isTRUE(playing())) "pause" else "play"))
    })
    ## the timer: advances one iteration per tick while playing
    observe({
        if (!isTRUE(playing())) return()
        k <- isolate(t_cur()); kmax <- isolate(nlast())
        if (k >= kmax) { playing(FALSE); return() }
        invalidateLater(400, session)
        t_cur(k + 1L)
    })
    observeEvent(input$step,  { playing(FALSE); t_cur(min(t_cur() + 1L, nlast())) })
    observeEvent(input$back,  { playing(FALSE); t_cur(max(t_cur() - 1L, 0L)) })
    observeEvent(input$first, { playing(FALSE); t_cur(0L) })
    observeEvent(input$toend, { playing(FALSE); t_cur(nlast()) })

    ## ---- the scatter plot with E-step classes and weighted-density contours --
    output$fit <- renderPlot({
        x <- X(); P <- path(); t <- min(t_cur(), nlast())
        th <- P$TH[[t + 1]]
        E  <- e_step(th, x)
        cls  <- max.col(E$R, ties.method = "first")    # hard classification
        sure <- apply(E$R, 1, max) >= 0.9

        rx <- range(x[, 1]) + c(-1, 1); ry <- range(x[, 2]) + c(-1, 1)
        g1 <- seq(rx[1], rx[2], length.out = 120)
        g2 <- seq(ry[1], ry[2], length.out = 120)
        G  <- as.matrix(expand.grid(g1, g2))
        ## pi_k * phi_k on the grid, one column per component
        Dk <- exp(log_joint(th, G))
        ## shared, geometrically spaced levels: a component with a smaller
        ## weight reaches fewer of them, so it draws fewer rings
        lev <- max(Dk) * 4^-(0:3)

        par(mar = c(4, 4, 3, 1))
        plot(x, type = "n", asp = 1, xlim = rx, ylim = ry,
             xlab = expression(x[1]), ylab = expression(x[2]),
             main = sprintf("iteration %d:  log-likelihood = %.2f", t, E$loglik))
        for (k in seq_len(K))
            contour(g1, g2, matrix(Dk[, k], length(g1)), levels = lev,
                    drawlabels = FALSE, col = adjustcolor(COLS[k], alpha.f = 0.4),
                    lwd = 1, add = TRUE)
        pch <- if (isTRUE(input$uncertain)) ifelse(sure, 19, 1) else 19
        points(x, col = COLS[cls], pch = pch, cex = 0.8)
        ## each mean in its component's colour, on a white halo so it
        ## stands out from the points of the same colour
        points(th$mu, pch = 3, cex = 2.4, lwd = 6, col = "white")
        points(th$mu, pch = 3, cex = 2.2, lwd = 3, col = COLS)
        if (isTRUE(input$truth))
            points(datasets[[input$dataset]]$mu, pch = 4, cex = 2, lwd = 2, col = "red")
        legend("topleft", bty = "n", cex = 0.9, pch = 19, col = COLS,
               legend = sprintf("component %d:  pi = %.2f,  %d points",
                                seq_len(K), th$pi, tabulate(cls, K)))
        legend("bottomright", bty = "n", cex = 0.85,
               pch = c(3, if (isTRUE(input$truth)) 4),
               col = c("grey30", if (isTRUE(input$truth)) "red"),
               legend = c("current means", if (isTRUE(input$truth)) "true means"))
    })

    output$ll <- renderPlot({
        P <- path(); t <- min(t_cur(), nlast()); it <- seq_along(P$LL) - 1
        par(mar = c(4, 4.5, 3, 1))
        plot(it, P$LL, type = "n", xlab = "iteration",
             ylab = "observed log-likelihood", main = "must never decrease")
        lines(it[1:(t + 1)], P$LL[1:(t + 1)], type = "b", pch = 19, cex = 0.6,
              col = "firebrick")
        if (nlast() < input$maxit)
            mtext(sprintf("stopped at iteration %d: a component degenerated", nlast()),
                  side = 3, line = 0.1, cex = 0.8, col = "firebrick")
    })

    output$pis <- renderPlot({
        P <- path(); t <- min(t_cur(), nlast()); it <- seq_along(P$TH) - 1
        PI <- t(sapply(P$TH, `[[`, "pi"))
        par(mar = c(4, 4.5, 3, 1))
        matplot(it, PI, type = "n", ylim = c(0, 1), xlab = "iteration",
                ylab = "mixing weight", main = "mixing weights")
        for (k in seq_len(K))
            lines(it[1:(t + 1)], PI[1:(t + 1), k], type = "b", pch = 19, cex = 0.6,
                  col = COLS[k])
    })
}

title: The EM Algorithm for a Bivariate Normal Mixture
text:
About the app
Watch the EM algorithm fit a mixture of three bivariate normal distributions, each with its own mean vector and full covariance matrix: \[
f(x) = \sum_{k=1}^{3} \pi_k\, \phi(x \mid \mu_k, \Sigma_k), \qquad x \in \mathbb{R}^2 .
\] It is the two-dimensional, three-component version of the one-dimensional mixture app.
Pick a true mixture and a starting value, then step through the fit with the playback buttons, or press play to run it automatically. Regenerate a dataset draws a fresh sample from the same mixture. Starting draws a new starting value of the chosen kind. Changing the data or the start resets the display to iteration 0.
Left panel, at iteration \(t\):

Colours: the E-step as a hard classification. Each point is coloured by the component with the largest responsibility \(\hat r_{ik}^{(t)} \propto \hat\pi_k^{(t)}\, \phi(x_i \mid \hat\mu_k^{(t)}, \hat\Sigma_k^{(t)})\). EM itself uses the soft responsibilities. With Hollow if unsure ticked, points whose largest responsibility is below 0.9 are drawn hollow, so you can see where the classification is uncertain.
Contours: the weighted component densities \(\hat\pi_k^{(t)}\, \phi(x \mid \hat\mu_k^{(t)}, \hat\Sigma_k^{(t)})\), in the component’s colour. All three use the same four contour levels, each a quarter of the one above. A component with a smaller weight therefore reaches fewer of the levels and draws fewer rings. The crosses, in each component’s colour, are the current means.

Right panels: the observed log-likelihood, which must never decrease, and the paths of the three mixing weights.
Four behaviours are worth producing deliberately.
Fast convergence when the clusters are well separated. With the well-separated mixture, the responsibilities are almost all 0 or 1 after a few iterations. The hard classification then agrees with the soft one, and EM converges in a handful of steps.
Slow convergence when they overlap. With the overlapping mixture, many points stay hollow for a long time and the log-likelihood keeps creeping up for dozens of iterations. This is the slow linear convergence that comes with a large fraction of missing information.
Local maxima. With correlated shapes and unequal weights, try several random starts. Some runs end with one component stretched across two true clusters while another splits a single cluster. The final log-likelihood is then visibly lower. EM finds a local maximum, not necessarily the global one, which is why it is usually run from several starts.
Overfitting with K = 3. When the data have only two true clusters, the third component has no cluster of its own. It ends up either splitting one cluster or as a small, low-weight component. Its contours show only a ring or two, because its weight is small. The fitted log-likelihood still improves on the two-component fit, so the likelihood alone cannot tell you the number of components.

    list(pi = Nk / nrow(X), mu = mu, S = S)
}

## a component is "degenerate" if it has (almost) no points or a flat covariance
degenerate <- function(th)
    any(!is.finite(unlist(th))) || any(th$pi < 1e-8) ||
    any(apply(th$S, 3, function(S) S[1, 1] * S[2, 2] - S[1, 2]^2) < 1e-8)

em_path <- function(th0, X, no_iters) {
    TH <- list(th0); LL <- e_step(th0, X)$loglik
    th <- th0
    for (i in seq_len(no_iters)) {
        th <- m_step(e_step(th, X)$R, X)
        if (degenerate(th)) break
        TH[[i + 1]] <- th
        LL[i + 1] <- e_step(th, X)$loglik
    }
    list(TH = TH, LL = LL)
}

### ---------- data sets (true parameters) -------------------------------------
cv <- function(s1, s2, r) matrix(c(s1^2, r * s1 * s2, r * s1 * s2, s2^2), 2)
datasets <- list(
    "well separated, equal weights" = list(
        pi = rep(1/3, 3), mu = rbind(c(0, 0), c(4, 0), c(2, 3.5)),
        S = list(diag(2), diag(2), diag(2))),
    "overlapping, equal weights" = list(
        pi = rep(1/3, 3), mu = rbind(c(0, 0), c(2.2, 0), c(1.1, 1.9)),
        S = list(diag(2), diag(2), diag(2))),
    "correlated shapes, unequal weights" = list(
        pi = c(0.5, 0.3, 0.2), mu = rbind(c(0, 0), c(3, 3), c(4, -1)),
        S = list(cv(1, 1, 0.8), cv(1.2, 0.7, -0.6), cv(0.5, 1.2, 0))),
    "only two true clusters (K = 3 overfits)" = list(
        pi = c(0.5, 0.5), mu = rbind(c(0, 0), c(4, 1)),
        S = list(cv(1, 1, 0.3), cv(1, 1, -0.3)))
)

make_data <- function(spec, n, seed) {
    set.seed(seed)
    z <- sample(seq_along(spec$pi), n, replace = TRUE, prob = spec$pi)
    X <- t(sapply(z, function(j) spec$mu[j, ] + drop(t(chol(spec$S[[j]])) %*% rnorm(2))))
    colnames(X) <- c("x1", "x2")
    X
}

### ---------- starting values ---------------------------------------------------
starts <- c("random data points as means", "random labels",
            "means near the centre")

make_start <- function(how, X, seed) {
    set.seed(seed)
    S0 <- array(cov(X), c(2, 2, K))
    ctr <- colMeans(X)
    mu <- switch(how,
        "random data points as means" = X[sample(nrow(X), K), ],
        "random labels" = {
            lab <- sample(rep_len(seq_len(K), nrow(X)))
            t(sapply(seq_len(K), function(k) colMeans(X[lab == k, , drop = FALSE])))
        },
        "means near the centre" =
            matrix(ctr, K, 2, byrow = TRUE) + matrix(rnorm(2 * K, 0, 0.05), K))
    list(pi = rep(1 / K, K), mu = unname(mu), S = S0)
}

### ---------- UI ---------------------------------------------------------------
## an icon-only playback button; the title shows as a tooltip
ctrl_btn <- function(id, icon_name, title, class = "btn-default")
    actionButton(id, NULL, icon = icon(icon_name), title = title, class = class,
                 style = "flex: 1; padding: 6px 0;")

## a checkbox with a short label; the tooltip gives the full meaning
short_check <- function(id, label, tip, value)
    checkboxInput(id, tags$span(label, title = tip), value, width = "auto")

ui <- fluidPage(
    ## ---- control panel: two rows --------------------------------------------
    wellPanel(
        ## generate the data
        fluidRow(
            column(4, selectInput("dataset", "True mixture", choices = names(datasets),
                                  width = "100%")),
            column(4, sliderInput("n", "Sample size n", min = 60, max = 600,
                                  value = 300, step = 30, width = "100%")),
            column(3, div(style = "padding-top: 25px;",
                          actionButton("newdata", "Regenerate a dataset",
                                       class = "btn-warning", style = "width:100%;")))
        ),
        hr(style = "margin: 4px 0 8px;"),
        ## the starting value, the playback and the display options
        fluidRow(
            column(3, selectInput("start", "Start EM from", choices = starts,

            column(2, sliderInput("maxit", "Iterations", min = 5, max = 200,

            column(3, div(style = "display: flex; gap: 4px; padding-top: 25px;",
                          actionButton("newstart", "New start",
                                       title = "Draw a new starting value of the chosen kind",
                                       style = "flex: 1.8; padding: 6px 2px;"),
                          ctrl_btn("first", "backward-fast", "Back to the start"),
                          ctrl_btn("back",  "backward-step", "One iteration back"),
                          ctrl_btn("play",  "play",          "Play / pause",
                                   class = "btn-primary"),
                          ctrl_btn("step",  "forward-step",  "One iteration forward"),
                          ctrl_btn("toend", "forward-fast",  "To the end"))),
            column(4, div(style = "display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; column-gap: 14px; padding-top: 22px;",
                          short_check("uncertain", "Hollow if unsure",
                                      "Hollow points: largest responsibility below 0.9", TRUE),
                          short_check("truth", "True means",
                                      "Mark the true means with red crosses", FALSE),

    ## ---- plots ----------------------------------------------------------------

### ---------- server -----------------------------------------------------------
server <- function(input, output, session) {

    dseed <- reactiveVal(812); sseed <- reactiveVal(1)
    observeEvent(input$newdata,  dseed(dseed() + 1))
    observeEvent(input$newstart, sseed(sseed() + 1))

    X <- reactive(make_data(datasets[[input$dataset]], input$n, dseed()))

    path <- reactive(em_path(make_start(input$start, X(), sseed()), X(), input$maxit))
    nlast <- reactive(length(path()$TH) - 1L)     # last iteration reached

    ## ---- iteration state driven by the playback buttons ---------------------
    t_cur   <- reactiveVal(0L)
    playing <- reactiveVal(FALSE)

    ## any change to the data or the starting value restarts the display
    observeEvent(path(), {
        t_cur(0L)
        playing(isTRUE(input$autoplay) && nlast() > 0)
    })

    observeEvent(input$play, {
        if (isTRUE(playing())) playing(FALSE)
        else {
            if (t_cur() >= nlast()) t_cur(0L)    # replay from the start
            playing(TRUE)
        }
    })
    observeEvent(playing(), {
        updateActionButton(session, "play",
                           icon = icon(if (isTRUE(playing())) "pause" else "play"))
    })
    ## the timer: advances one iteration per tick while playing
    observe({
        if (!isTRUE(playing())) return()
        k <- isolate(t_cur()); kmax <- isolate(nlast())
        if (k >= kmax) { playing(FALSE); return() }
        invalidateLater(400, session)
        t_cur(k + 1L)
    })
    observeEvent(input$step,  { playing(FALSE); t_cur(min(t_cur() + 1L, nlast())) })
    observeEvent(input$back,  { playing(FALSE); t_cur(max(t_cur() - 1L, 0L)) })
    observeEvent(input$first, { playing(FALSE); t_cur(0L) })
    observeEvent(input$toend, { playing(FALSE); t_cur(nlast()) })

    ## ---- the scatter plot with E-step classes and weighted-density contours --
    output$fit <- renderPlot({
        x <- X(); P <- path(); t <- min(t_cur(), nlast())
        th <- P$TH[[t + 1]]
        E  <- e_step(th, x)
        cls  <- max.col(E$R, ties.method = "first")    # hard classification
        sure <- apply(E$R, 1, max) >= 0.9

        rx <- range(x[, 1]) + c(-1, 1); ry <- range(x[, 2]) + c(-1, 1)
        g1 <- seq(rx[1], rx[2], length.out = 120)
        g2 <- seq(ry[1], ry[2], length.out = 120)
        G  <- as.matrix(expand.grid(g1, g2))
        ## pi_k * phi_k on the grid, one column per component
        Dk <- exp(log_joint(th, G))
        ## shared, geometrically spaced levels: a component with a smaller
        ## weight reaches fewer of them, so it draws fewer rings
        lev <- max(Dk) * 4^-(0:3)

        par(mar = c(4, 4, 3, 1))
        plot(x, type = "n", asp = 1, xlim = rx, ylim = ry,
             xlab = expression(x[1]), ylab = expression(x[2]),
             main = sprintf("iteration %d:  log-likelihood = %.2f", t, E$loglik))
        for (k in seq_len(K))
            contour(g1, g2, matrix(Dk[, k], length(g1)), levels = lev,
                    drawlabels = FALSE, col = adjustcolor(COLS[k], alpha.f = 0.4),
                    lwd = 1, add = TRUE)
        pch <- if (isTRUE(input$uncertain)) ifelse(sure, 19, 1) else 19
        points(x, col = COLS[cls], pch = pch, cex = 0.8)
        ## each mean in its component's colour, on a white halo so it
        ## stands out from the points of the same colour
        points(th$mu, pch = 3, cex = 2.4, lwd = 6, col = "white")
        points(th$mu, pch = 3, cex = 2.2, lwd = 3, col = COLS)
        if (isTRUE(input$truth))
            points(datasets[[input$dataset]]$mu, pch = 4, cex = 2, lwd = 2, col = "red")
        legend("topleft", bty = "n", cex = 0.9, pch = 19, col = COLS,
               legend = sprintf("component %d:  pi = %.2f,  %d points",
                                seq_len(K), th$pi, tabulate(cls, K)))
        legend("bottomright", bty = "n", cex = 0.85,
               pch = c(3, if (isTRUE(input$truth)) 4),
               col = c("grey30", if (isTRUE(input$truth)) "red"),
               legend = c("current means", if (isTRUE(input$truth)) "true means"))
    })

    output$ll <- renderPlot({
        P <- path(); t <- min(t_cur(), nlast()); it <- seq_along(P$LL) - 1
        par(mar = c(4, 4.5, 3, 1))
        plot(it, P$LL, type = "n", xlab = "iteration",
             ylab = "observed log-likelihood", main = "must never decrease")
        lines(it[1:(t + 1)], P$LL[1:(t + 1)], type = "b", pch = 19, cex = 0.6,
              col = "firebrick")
        if (nlast() < input$maxit)
            mtext(sprintf("stopped at iteration %d: a component degenerated", nlast()),
                  side = 3, line = 0.1, cex = 0.8, col = "firebrick")
    })

    output$pis <- renderPlot({
        P <- path(); t <- min(t_cur(), nlast()); it <- seq_along(P$TH) - 1
        PI <- t(sapply(P$TH, `[[`, "pi"))
        par(mar = c(4, 4.5, 3, 1))
        matplot(it, PI, type = "n", ylim = c(0, 1), xlab = "iteration",
                ylab = "mixing weight", main = "mixing weights")
        for (k in seq_len(K))
            lines(it[1:(t + 1)], PI[1:(t + 1), k], type = "b", pch = 19, cex = 0.6,
                  col = COLS[k])
    })
}

shinyApp(ui, server)

library(shiny)

### renderPlot replacement: Safari 27 (WebKit) cannot hold the call stack of
### shiny::renderPlot in webR ("Maximum call stack size exceeded"), so draw with
### renderImage instead, which nests about 45 fewer R calls
renderPlot <- function(expr, width = "auto", height = "auto", res = 72, ...,
                       env = parent.frame(), quoted = FALSE) {
    func <- shiny::exprToFunction(expr, env, quoted)
    shiny::renderImage({
        info <- shiny::getCurrentOutputInfo()
        w  <- if (is.numeric(width))  width  else info$width()
        h  <- if (is.numeric(height)) height else info$height()
        shiny::req(w > 0, h > 0)
        pr <- shiny::getDefaultReactiveDomain()$clientData$pixelratio
        if (is.null(pr)) pr <- 1
        f   <- tempfile(fileext = ".png")
        dev <- shiny:::startPNG(f, w * pr, h * pr, res = res * pr)
        on.exit(grDevices::dev.off(dev), add = TRUE)
        grDevices::dev.control(displaylist = "enable")
        v <- withVisible(func())
        if (v$visible) print(v$value)
        list(src = f, contentType = "image/png", width = w, height = h,
             coordmap = shiny:::getCoordmap(v$value, w * pr, h * pr, res * pr))
    }, deleteFile = TRUE)
}

log_sum_exp <- function(lx) { m <- max(lx); m + log(sum(exp(lx - m))) }

log_lik   <- function(x, mu, w) sum(dnorm(x, mu, exp(w / 2), log = TRUE))
log_prior <- function(mu, w, mu_0, sigma_mu, w_0, sigma_w) {
    dnorm(mu, mu_0, sigma_mu, log = TRUE) + dnorm(w, w_0, sigma_w, log = TRUE)
}
neg_log_post <- function(theta, x, mu_0, sigma_mu, w_0, sigma_w) {
    -log_lik(x, theta[1], theta[2]) -
        log_prior(theta[1], theta[2], mu_0, sigma_mu, w_0, sigma_w)
}
log_dmvnorm_batch <- function(Theta, mu, A) {
    Tc <- Theta - mu
    quad <- colSums((A %*% Tc) * Tc)
    0.5 * (-nrow(Theta) * log(2 * pi) + sum(log(svd(A)$d)) - quad)
}

## same grid-quadrature "truth" as log_marlik_grid() above
marlik_truth <- function(x, mu_0, sigma_mu, w_0, sigma_w, n_grid = 400, width = 8) {
    n   <- length(x)
    fit <- nlm(neg_log_post, c(mean(x), log(stats::var(x))), hessian = TRUE,
               x = x, mu_0 = mu_0, sigma_mu = sigma_mu, w_0 = w_0, sigma_w = sigma_w)
    se  <- sqrt(diag(solve(fit$hessian)))
    mu_grid <- fit$estimate[1] + seq(-width, width, length.out = n_grid) * se[1]
    w_grid  <- fit$estimate[2] + seq(-width, width, length.out = n_grid) * se[2]
    SS <- sum(x^2) - 2 * mu_grid * sum(x) + n * mu_grid^2
    log_lik_grid   <- outer(SS, w_grid,
                             function(ss, w) -0.5 * n * log(2 * pi) - n * w / 2 - 0.5 * exp(-w) * ss)
    log_prior_grid <- outer(dnorm(mu_grid, mu_0, sigma_mu, log = TRUE),
                             dnorm(w_grid, w_0, sigma_w, log = TRUE), "+")
    h_mu <- diff(mu_grid[1:2]); h_w <- diff(w_grid[1:2])
    log_sum_exp(as.vector(log_lik_grid + log_prior_grid)) + log(h_mu) + log(h_w)
}

## Laplace-shaped proposal: draw, weight, and return the log estimate, its
## standard error (delta method), and the sorted normalized weights
sim_laplace <- function(x, mu_0, sigma_mu, w_0, sigma_w, S) {
    fit <- nlm(neg_log_post, c(mean(x), log(stats::var(x))), hessian = TRUE,
               x = x, mu_0 = mu_0, sigma_mu = sigma_mu, w_0 = w_0, sigma_w = sigma_w)
    mu_hat <- fit$estimate; H <- fit$hessian
    L <- t(chol(solve(H)))
    Theta <- L %*% matrix(rnorm(2 * S), 2, S) + mu_hat
    log_g <- log_dmvnorm_batch(Theta, mu_hat, H)
    log_f <- -apply(Theta, 2, neg_log_post, x = x, mu_0 = mu_0, sigma_mu = sigma_mu,
                     w_0 = w_0, sigma_w = sigma_w)
    lw <- log_f - log_g
    m  <- max(lw); v <- exp(lw - m); wn <- v / sum(v)
    list(est = log_sum_exp(lw) - log(S), se = sd(v) / (sqrt(S) * mean(v)),
         ess = 1 / sum(wn^2), wn = sort(wn, decreasing = TRUE))
}

## prior proposal (g = pi): same bookkeeping, unfavourable g
sim_prior <- function(x, mu_0, sigma_mu, w_0, sigma_w, S) {
    mus <- rnorm(S, mu_0, sigma_mu); ws <- rnorm(S, w_0, sigma_w)
    lw  <- vapply(seq_len(S), function(i) log_lik(x, mus[i], ws[i]), numeric(1))
    m   <- max(lw); v <- exp(lw - m); wn <- v / sum(v)
    list(est = log_sum_exp(lw) - log(S), se = sd(v) / (sqrt(S) * mean(v)),
         ess = 1 / sum(wn^2), wn = sort(wn, decreasing = TRUE))
}

ui <- fluidPage(
    sidebarLayout(
        sidebarPanel(
            width = 3,
            sliderInput("n", "data size  n", min = 5, max = 200, value = 20, step = 5),
            sliderInput("sig_mu", HTML("prior sd on μ"), min = 1, max = 10, value = 5, step = 0.5),
            sliderInput("sig_w", HTML("prior sd on w"), min = 1, max = 10, value = 5, step = 0.5),
            selectInput("S", "importance sample size  S",
                        choices = c(500, 2000, 5000, 20000), selected = 2000),
            actionButton("new", "New sample"),
            checkboxInput("logw", "log scale for weights", TRUE)
        ),
        mainPanel(width = 9, plotOutput("panel", height = "720px"))
    )
)

server <- function(input, output) {

    sim <- reactive({
        n <- input$n; S <- as.integer(input$S)
        sig_mu <- input$sig_mu; sig_w <- input$sig_w
        set.seed(input$new + 1)
        x <- rnorm(n)

        list(S = S,
             truth = marlik_truth(x, 0, sig_mu, 0, sig_w),
             lap   = sim_laplace(x, 0, sig_mu, 0, sig_w, S),
             pri   = sim_prior(x, 0, sig_mu, 0, sig_w, S))
    })

    output$panel <- renderPlot({
        s <- sim(); S <- s$S
        rank_frac <- seq_len(S) / S
        uselog <- input$logw

        lwr_lap <- s$lap$est - 1.96 * s$lap$se; upr_lap <- s$lap$est + 1.96 * s$lap$se
        lwr_pri <- s$pri$est - 1.96 * s$pri$se; upr_pri <- s$pri$est + 1.96 * s$pri$se
        cov_lap <- if (lwr_lap <= s$truth && s$truth <= upr_lap) "darkgreen" else "firebrick"
        cov_pri <- if (lwr_pri <= s$truth && s$truth <= upr_pri) "darkgreen" else "firebrick"

        draw_panel <- function(wn, col, title, xlab, est, lwr, upr, ess_pct, cov_col) {
            if (uselog) {
                floor <- max(min(wn[wn > 0]), 1e-300)
                wn    <- pmax(wn, floor)
                ylim  <- range(wn)
                ylab  <- "normalized weight (log scale)"
            } else {
                ylim <- c(0, max(wn))
                ylab <- "normalized weight"
            }
            plot(rank_frac, wn, type = "n", log = if (uselog) "y" else "",
                 ylim = ylim, xlab = xlab, ylab = ylab, main = title)
            lines(rank_frac, wn, lwd = 3, col = col)
            abline(h = 1 / S, lty = 2, col = "darkgreen", lwd = 2)
            legend("topright", inset = c(0.02, 0.05), bty = "n", cex = 1.05,
                   text.col = c("black", cov_col),
                   legend = c(
                       sprintf("truth: log P(y) = %.3f", s$truth),
                       sprintf("est=%.3f  CI=(%.3f,%.3f)  ESS=%.2f%%", est, lwr, upr, ess_pct)))
        }

        layout(matrix(1:2, 2))

        par(mar = c(2.5, 5, 3, 1))
        draw_panel(s$lap$wn, "steelblue", "Laplace-shaped proposal", "",
                   s$lap$est, lwr_lap, upr_lap, 100 * s$lap$ess / S, cov_lap)

        par(mar = c(4.5, 5, 2.5, 1))
        draw_panel(s$pri$wn, "firebrick", "prior proposal",
                   "rank / S  (draws sorted by weight, largest first)",
                   s$pri$est, lwr_pri, upr_pri, 100 * s$pri$ess / S, cov_pri)
    })
}

shinyApp(ui, server)

title: Sorted Importance Weights
text:
About the app
Shows how the distribution of the importance weights reveals the quality of a proposal for estimating a marginal likelihood, comparing a Laplace-shaped proposal with the prior. Sliders control the simulated data size \(n\) and the prior spreads on \(\mu\) and \(w\); the top panel plots the sorted, normalized importance weights from the Laplace-shaped proposal and the bottom panel the same for the prior — each on its own axis, since one proposal’s weights routinely span far more orders of magnitude than the other’s — with a checkbox toggling both between log and linear scale, and the dashed line at \(1/S\) marking perfectly balanced weights in both.
A single number like \(S_{\text{eff}}\) summarizes the weight distribution; looking at the weights themselves is more direct. The app above draws \(S\) importance samples from each proposal and plots their normalized weights, sorted from largest to smallest against rank\(/S\), in two separate panels, because the two proposals’ weights live on such different scales that a shared axis would flatten the well-behaved one to a barely visible line. The weight axis defaults to a log scale — a proposal shaped like the target gives a nearly flat curve close to \(1/S\) (every draw contributes about equally), while a poorly matched proposal gives a curve that falls off a cliff, with a handful of draws near rank \(0\) carrying nearly all the weight; a checkbox switches both panels to a linear scale instead, where that same cliff collapses to a single spike against an otherwise invisible floor — a useful reminder that the log scale is doing real work, not just spreading the picture out. Each panel’s legend reports the grid-quadrature truth and that proposal’s estimate and 95% CI, colored green when the interval covers the truth and red when it does not.
Raise \(n\) with the sliders at their defaults and watch the prior’s curve rotate from a gentle slope into a cliff at the very first few ranks, while the Laplace curve barely moves — the same collapse as in Table 11.2, now visible in the shape of the curve rather than only in a single summary number.

## same grid-quadrature "truth" as log_marlik_grid() above
marlik_truth <- function(x, mu_0, sigma_mu, w_0, sigma_w, n_grid = 400, width = 8) {
    n   <- length(x)

    se  <- sqrt(diag(solve(fit$hessian)))
    mu_grid <- fit$estimate[1] + seq(-width, width, length.out = n_grid) * se[1]
    w_grid  <- fit$estimate[2] + seq(-width, width, length.out = n_grid) * se[2]
    SS <- sum(x^2) - 2 * mu_grid * sum(x) + n * mu_grid^2
    log_lik_grid   <- outer(SS, w_grid,
                             function(ss, w) -0.5 * n * log(2 * pi) - n * w / 2 - 0.5 * exp(-w) * ss)
    log_prior_grid <- outer(dnorm(mu_grid, mu_0, sigma_mu, log = TRUE),
                             dnorm(w_grid, w_0, sigma_w, log = TRUE), "+")
    h_mu <- diff(mu_grid[1:2]); h_w <- diff(w_grid[1:2])
    log_sum_exp(as.vector(log_lik_grid + log_prior_grid)) + log(h_mu) + log(h_w)
}

## Laplace-shaped proposal: draw, weight, and return the log estimate, its
## standard error (delta method), and the sorted normalized weights
sim_laplace <- function(x, mu_0, sigma_mu, w_0, sigma_w, S) {
    fit <- nlm(neg_log_post, c(mean(x), log(stats::var(x))), hessian = TRUE,
               x = x, mu_0 = mu_0, sigma_mu = sigma_mu, w_0 = w_0, sigma_w = sigma_w)
    mu_hat <- fit$estimate; H <- fit$hessian
    L <- t(chol(solve(H)))
    Theta <- L %*% matrix(rnorm(2 * S), 2, S) + mu_hat
    log_g <- log_dmvnorm_batch(Theta, mu_hat, H)
    log_f <- -apply(Theta, 2, neg_log_post, x = x, mu_0 = mu_0, sigma_mu = sigma_mu,
                     w_0 = w_0, sigma_w = sigma_w)
    lw <- log_f - log_g
    m  <- max(lw); v <- exp(lw - m); wn <- v / sum(v)
    list(est = log_sum_exp(lw) - log(S), se = sd(v) / (sqrt(S) * mean(v)),
         ess = 1 / sum(wn^2), wn = sort(wn, decreasing = TRUE))
}

## prior proposal (g = pi): same bookkeeping, unfavourable g
sim_prior <- function(x, mu_0, sigma_mu, w_0, sigma_w, S) {
    mus <- rnorm(S, mu_0, sigma_mu); ws <- rnorm(S, w_0, sigma_w)
    lw  <- vapply(seq_len(S), function(i) log_lik(x, mus[i], ws[i]), numeric(1))
    m   <- max(lw); v <- exp(lw - m); wn <- v / sum(v)
    list(est = log_sum_exp(lw) - log(S), se = sd(v) / (sqrt(S) * mean(v)),
         ess = 1 / sum(wn^2), wn = sort(wn, decreasing = TRUE))
}

server <- function(input, output) {

    sim <- reactive({
        n <- input$n; S <- as.integer(input$S)
        sig_mu <- input$sig_mu; sig_w <- input$sig_w
        set.seed(input$new + 1)
        x <- rnorm(n)

        list(S = S,
             truth = marlik_truth(x, 0, sig_mu, 0, sig_w),
             lap   = sim_laplace(x, 0, sig_mu, 0, sig_w, S),
             pri   = sim_prior(x, 0, sig_mu, 0, sig_w, S))
    })

    output$panel <- renderPlot({
        s <- sim(); S <- s$S
        rank_frac <- seq_len(S) / S
        uselog <- input$logw

        lwr_lap <- s$lap$est - 1.96 * s$lap$se; upr_lap <- s$lap$est + 1.96 * s$lap$se
        lwr_pri <- s$pri$est - 1.96 * s$pri$se; upr_pri <- s$pri$est + 1.96 * s$pri$se
        cov_lap <- if (lwr_lap <= s$truth && s$truth <= upr_lap) "darkgreen" else "firebrick"
        cov_pri <- if (lwr_pri <= s$truth && s$truth <= upr_pri) "darkgreen" else "firebrick"

        draw_panel <- function(wn, col, title, xlab, est, lwr, upr, ess_pct, cov_col) {
            if (uselog) {
                floor <- max(min(wn[wn > 0]), 1e-300)
                wn    <- pmax(wn, floor)
                ylim  <- range(wn)
                ylab  <- "normalized weight (log scale)"
            } else {
                ylim <- c(0, max(wn))
                ylab <- "normalized weight"
            }
            plot(rank_frac, wn, type = "n", log = if (uselog) "y" else "",
                 ylim = ylim, xlab = xlab, ylab = ylab, main = title)
            lines(rank_frac, wn, lwd = 3, col = col)
            abline(h = 1 / S, lty = 2, col = "darkgreen", lwd = 2)
            legend("topright", inset = c(0.02, 0.05), bty = "n", cex = 1.05,
                   text.col = c("black", cov_col),
                   legend = c(
                       sprintf("truth: log P(y) = %.3f", s$truth),
                       sprintf("est=%.3f  CI=(%.3f,%.3f)  ESS=%.2f%%", est, lwr, upr, ess_pct)))
        }

        layout(matrix(1:2, 2))

        par(mar = c(2.5, 5, 3, 1))
        draw_panel(s$lap$wn, "steelblue", "Laplace-shaped proposal", "",
                   s$lap$est, lwr_lap, upr_lap, 100 * s$lap$ess / S, cov_lap)

        par(mar = c(4.5, 5, 2.5, 1))
        draw_panel(s$pri$wn, "firebrick", "prior proposal",
                   "rank / S  (draws sorted by weight, largest first)",
                   s$pri$est, lwr_pri, upr_pri, 100 * s$pri$ess / S, cov_pri)
    })
}

Sigma <- matrix(c(1, 0.98, 0.98, 1), 2)
Sinv  <- solve(Sigma)
log_pi_corr  <- function(z) -0.5 * sum(z * (Sinv %*% z))
grad_pi_corr <- function(z) -as.vector(Sinv %*% z)

hmc <- function(log_pi, grad_log_pi, theta, eps, L, iters) {
    d <- length(theta)
    out <- matrix(NA_real_, iters, d); n_acc <- 0
    for (t in seq_len(iters)) {
        p0 <- rnorm(d)
        th <- theta; p <- p0 + eps / 2 * grad_log_pi(th)
        for (l in seq_len(L)) {
            th <- th + eps * p
            if (l < L) p <- p + eps * grad_log_pi(th)
        }
        p <- p + eps / 2 * grad_log_pi(th)
        H0 <- -log_pi(theta) + 0.5 * sum(p0^2)
        H1 <- -log_pi(th)    + 0.5 * sum(p^2)
        if (log(runif(1)) < H0 - H1) { theta <- th; n_acc <- n_acc + 1 }
        out[t, ] <- theta
    }
    attr(out, "accept_rate") <- n_acc / iters
    out
}

    })

    output$traj <- renderPlot({
        d <- fit()
        g <- seq(-3.5, 3.5, length.out = 60)
        Z <- outer(g, g, Vectorize(function(a, b) exp(-0.5 * c(a, b) %*% Sinv %*% c(a, b))))
        par(mar = c(4, 4, 2, 1))
        contour(g, g, Z, nlevels = 6, drawlabels = FALSE, col = "gray60",
                xlab = expression(theta[1]), ylab = expression(theta[2]),
                main = sprintf("accept rate: %.2f", attr(d, "accept_rate")))
        k <- min(100, nrow(d))
        lines(d[1:k, ], col = "steelblue", lwd = 1.2)
        points(d[1:k, ], pch = 19, cex = 0.5, col = "steelblue")
    })

    output$acfplot <- renderPlot({
        d <- fit()
        par(mar = c(4, 4, 1, 1))

    })

    output$tab <- renderTable({
        d <- fit()
        data.frame(quantity = c("acceptance rate", "mean theta_1", "sd theta_1"),
                   value = c(attr(d, "accept_rate"), mean(d[, 1]), sd(d[, 1])))
    }, digits = 3, rownames = FALSE)
}

title: Hamiltonian Monte Carlo Tuning
text:
About the app
Lets you tune the step size and number of leapfrog steps of Hamiltonian Monte Carlo to see how they affect its exploration of a correlated target. The app above runs the hmc() function above on the same correlated target and lets you vary \(\epsilon\) and \(L\) directly.
Leapfrog step size \(\epsilon\) and step count \(L\) both need tuning: too large an \(\epsilon\) makes the discretized trajectory unstable (rejections rise sharply); too small an \(L\) reduces HMC to a random walk; too large an \(L\) lets the trajectory turn back on itself and waste computation.






NoteReproducing this figure



The chunk above uses the shinylive extension, which compiles the app to WebAssembly so it runs in the reader’s browser with no Shiny server. Install it once per project with
quarto add quarto-ext/shinylive
and add filters: [shinylive] to the document or project YAML. Only packages available in webR may be used inside the app, so the code above is restricted to base R and shiny.

mu_0 <- 0; tau <- 10                                    # prior: mu ~ N(0, 10^2)
a_0 <- 1; b_0 <- 1                                      # prior: sigma^2 ~ Inverse-Gamma(1, 1)

server <- function(input, output, session) {

    ### data: y_i ~ Cauchy(mu_true, sig_true)
    dat <- reactive({
        set.seed(100 + input$new)
        y <- input$mu_true + input$sig_true * rcauchy(input$n_obs)
        n <- length(y)
        ### exact joint posterior of (mu, sigma) on a grid, for the contours and the exact summaries:
        ### a wide first pass locates the mass, a second pass on the region that holds 99.9% of it refines
        post_grid <- function(mu_g, sg_g) {
            ll <- matrix(0, 200, 200)
            for (yi in y) ll <- ll + outer(mu_g, sg_g, function(m, s) dcauchy(yi, m, s, log = TRUE))
            lp_sigma <- log(2 * sg_g) + a_0 * log(b_0) - lgamma(a_0) - (a_0 + 1) * log(sg_g^2) - b_0 / sg_g^2
            lpost <- ll + dnorm(mu_g, mu_0, tau, log = TRUE) + matrix(lp_sigma, 200, 200, byrow = TRUE)
            p <- exp(lpost - max(lpost)); p / sum(p)
        }
        span <- function(g, marg) {
            cdf <- cumsum(marg); r <- g[c(max(1, which(cdf > 0.0005)[1] - 1), min(length(g), which(cdf > 0.9995)[1] + 1))]
            pad <- 0.2 * diff(r); c(r[1] - pad, r[2] + pad)
        }
        m0 <- median(y); s0 <- max(IQR(y) / 2, 0.5)
        mu_g <- seq(m0 - 8 * s0, m0 + 8 * s0, length.out = 200)
        sg_g <- seq(0.05, 6 * s0 + 2, length.out = 200)
        p <- post_grid(mu_g, sg_g)
        mr <- span(mu_g, rowSums(p)); sr <- span(sg_g, colSums(p))
        mu_g <- seq(mr[1], mr[2], length.out = 200)
        sg_g <- seq(max(sr[1], 0.02), sr[2], length.out = 200)
        p <- post_grid(mu_g, sg_g)
        pm <- rowSums(p); ps <- colSums(p)
        e_mu <- sum(pm * mu_g); e_sg <- sum(ps * sg_g)
        q_of <- function(g, marg) approx(cumsum(marg), g, xout = c(0.025, 0.975), rule = 2)$y
        ### maximum likelihood for Cauchy(mu, sigma) with a Wald interval from the observed information
        ### (the interval for sigma is formed on the log scale and transformed back)
        nll <- function(th) -sum(dcauchy(y, th[1], exp(th[2]), log = TRUE))
        fit <- optim(c(median(y), log(s0)), nll, method = "BFGS", hessian = TRUE)
        se  <- tryCatch(sqrt(diag(solve(fit$hessian))), error = function(e) c(NA, NA))
        mle <- list(mu = fit$par[1], sg = exp(fit$par[2]), se_mu = se[1], se_sg = exp(fit$par[2]) * se[2],
                    ci_mu = fit$par[1] + c(-1, 1) * 1.96 * se[1],
                    ci_sg = exp(fit$par[2] + c(-1, 1) * 1.96 * se[2]))
        list(y = y, n = n, mu_g = mu_g, sg_g = sg_g, post = p, mle = mle,
             q_mu = q_of(mu_g, pm), q_sg = q_of(sg_g, ps),
             exact = c(mean_mu = e_mu, mean_sg = e_sg,
                       sd_mu = sqrt(sum(pm * (mu_g - e_mu)^2)), sd_sg = sqrt(sum(ps * (sg_g - e_sg)^2))))
    })

    rv <- reactiveValues(N = 500, t = 0, phase = 0, mu = NULL, sg = NULL, v = NULL,
                         cur_mu = 0, cur_sg = 1, path = NULL, np = 0, last = "", playing = FALSE)

    reset_run <- function() {
        N <- input$N
        rv$N <- N; rv$t <- 0; rv$phase <- 0
        rv$mu <- c(input$mu_init, rep(NA_real_, N)); rv$sg <- c(input$sig_init, rep(NA_real_, N))
        rv$cur_mu <- input$mu_init; rv$cur_sg <- input$sig_init
        rv$v <- NULL
        rv$path <- matrix(NA_real_, 3 * N + 2, 3)            # columns: mu, sigma, sub-step (0 start, 1 v, 2 mu, 3 sigma)
        rv$path[1, ] <- c(input$mu_init, input$sig_init, 0); rv$np <- 1
        rv$last <- "start"
        rv$playing <- FALSE
        updateActionButton(session, "play", label = "▶ Play")
        set.seed(1000 + input$new)
    }

    add_path <- function(code) {
        rv$np <- rv$np + 1
        rv$path[rv$np, ] <- c(rv$cur_mu, rv$cur_sg, code)
    }

    ### one Gibbs sub-step: (1) the latent variances v_i, (2) mu, (3) sigma
    step_one <- function() {
        d <- dat(); y <- d$y; n <- d$n
        if (rv$t >= rv$N && rv$phase == 0) return(invisible(NULL))
        if (rv$phase == 0) {
            r2 <- (y - rv$cur_mu)^2 / rv$cur_sg^2
            rv$v <- 1 / rgamma(n, shape = 1, rate = (1 + r2) / 2)                 # v_i | mu, sigma, y_i ~ IG(1, (1 + r_i^2)/2)
            rv$phase <- 1; rv$last <- "v_i | mu, sigma"; add_path(1)
        } else if (rv$phase == 1) {
            prec <- 1 / tau^2 + sum(1 / (rv$cur_sg^2 * rv$v))
            mean <- (mu_0 / tau^2 + sum(y / (rv$cur_sg^2 * rv$v))) / prec
            rv$cur_mu <- rnorm(1, mean, 1 / sqrt(prec))                            # mu | v, sigma, y ~ normal
            rv$phase <- 2; rv$last <- "mu | v, sigma"; add_path(2)
        } else {
            rate <- b_0 + sum((y - rv$cur_mu)^2 / (2 * rv$v))
            rv$cur_sg <- sqrt(1 / rgamma(1, shape = a_0 + n / 2, rate = rate))     # sigma^2 | mu, v, y ~ inverse gamma
            rv$phase <- 0; rv$t <- rv$t + 1; rv$last <- "sigma | mu, v"; add_path(3)
            rv$mu[rv$t + 1] <- rv$cur_mu; rv$sg[rv$t + 1] <- rv$cur_sg
        }
    }
    step_iter <- function() {                       # finish the current iteration, or run a whole one
        repeat {
            step_one()
            if (rv$phase == 0 || rv$t >= rv$N) break
        }
    }
    finished <- function() rv$t >= rv$N && rv$phase == 0

    observeEvent(list(input$n_obs, input$mu_true, input$sig_true, input$N, input$mu_init, input$sig_init,
                      input$new, input$restart),
                 { req(input$N, input$mu_init, input$sig_init); reset_run() })

    observeEvent(input$play, {
        if (finished()) return()
        rv$playing <- !rv$playing
        updateActionButton(session, "play", label = if (rv$playing) "⏸ Pause" else "▶ Play")
    })
    observeEvent(input$next_step, {
        rv$playing <- FALSE; updateActionButton(session, "play", label = "▶ Play")
        if (isTRUE(input$sub)) step_one() else step_iter()
    })
    observeEvent(input$end, {
        rv$playing <- FALSE; updateActionButton(session, "play", label = "▶ Play")
        while (!finished()) step_iter()
    })
    observe({
        if (isTRUE(rv$playing)) {
            invalidateLater(150, session)
            isolate({
                if (isTRUE(input$sub)) step_one() else for (k in seq_len(input$speed)) step_iter()
                if (finished()) { rv$playing <- FALSE; updateActionButton(session, "play", label = "▶ Play") }
            })
        }
    })

    output$status <- renderText({
        req(rv$mu)
        sprintf("iteration %d / %d; current (mu, sigma) = (%.3f, %.3f)", rv$t, rv$N, rv$cur_mu, rv$cur_sg)
    })

    ### the (mu, sigma) plane: exact posterior contours, the Gibbs draws, and optionally the path of each step
    output$plane <- renderPlot({
        req(rv$mu); d <- dat(); t <- rv$t
        ex <- d$exact                                          # the window is the exact posterior mean +- 3 sd, not the starting value
        xlim <- ex["mean_mu"] + c(-3, 3) * ex["sd_mu"]; ylim <- ex["mean_sg"] + c(-3, 3) * ex["sd_sg"]
        par(mar = c(4, 4, 3, 1))
        cols <- hcl.colors(30, "YlOrRd", rev = TRUE)
        plot(NA, xlim = xlim, ylim = ylim, xlab = expression(mu), ylab = expression(sigma),
             main = "Gibbs draws on the exact posterior")
        rect(par("usr")[1], par("usr")[3], par("usr")[2], par("usr")[4], col = cols[1], border = NA)
        image(d$mu_g, d$sg_g, d$post, col = cols, add = TRUE)
        contour(d$mu_g, d$sg_g, d$post, nlevels = 6, drawlabels = FALSE, add = TRUE, col = "gray40")
        if (t >= 1) points(rv$mu[2:(t + 1)], rv$sg[2:(t + 1)], pch = 19, cex = 0.4, col = adjustcolor("black", 0.45))
        points(input$mu_init, input$sig_init, pch = 17, col = "steelblue", cex = 1.4)
        if (isTRUE(input$sub) && rv$np >= 2) {
            k <- max(2, rv$np - 1):rv$np                                    # the last two sub-steps
            P <- rv$path
            for (j in k) {
                if (P[j, 3] == 2) arrows(P[j - 1, 1], P[j - 1, 2], P[j, 1], P[j, 2], length = 0.08, lwd = 2, col = "darkorange")
                if (P[j, 3] == 3) arrows(P[j - 1, 1], P[j - 1, 2], P[j, 1], P[j, 2], length = 0.08, lwd = 2, col = "steelblue")
                if (P[j, 3] == 1) points(P[j, 1], P[j, 2], pch = 1, cex = 2.2, lwd = 2, col = "forestgreen")
            }
        }
        points(rv$cur_mu, rv$cur_sg, pch = 19, cex = 1.3, col = "red")
        legend("topright", bty = "n", cex = 0.8, pch = c(19, 17, 19), col = c("black", "steelblue", "red"),
               legend = c("draws", "start", "current"))
    })

    ### the augmented variances v_i: outlying observations get large v_i, so they are downweighted
    output$vplot <- renderPlot({
        req(rv$mu); d <- dat(); par(mar = c(4, 4, 3, 1))
        if (is.null(rv$v)) {
            plot(d$y, rep(1, d$n), type = "n", log = "y", xlab = "y", ylab = expression(v[i]),
                 main = expression("latent variances"~v[i]~"(not drawn yet)"))
            rug(d$y)
        } else {
            plot(d$y, rv$v, log = "y", pch = 19, col = adjustcolor("forestgreen", 0.7), xlab = "y",
                 ylab = expression(v[i]), main = expression("latent variances"~v[i]~"(current)"))
            abline(v = rv$cur_mu, col = "red", lty = 2)
            legend("topright", bty = "n", cex = 0.8, lty = 2, col = "red", legend = expression(current~mu))
        }
    })

    trace_plot <- function(x, exact, sd, ylab) {
        par(mar = c(4, 4, 2, 1))
        plot(0:rv$N, x, type = "n", xlab = "iteration", ylab = ylab,
             ylim = exact + c(-3, 3) * sd)                                  # window around the posterior, not the start
        lines(0:rv$t, x[1:(rv$t + 1)], col = "gray30")
        abline(h = exact, col = "red", lty = 2)
    }
    output$tr_mu <- renderPlot({ req(rv$mu); d <- dat(); trace_plot(rv$mu, d$exact["mean_mu"], d$exact["sd_mu"], expression(mu)) })
    output$tr_sg <- renderPlot({ req(rv$mu); d <- dat(); trace_plot(rv$sg, d$exact["mean_sg"], d$exact["sd_sg"], expression(sigma)) })

    output$tab <- renderTable({
        req(rv$mu); d <- dat(); t <- rv$t; m <- d$mle
        burn <- floor(0.2 * t)
        idx <- if (t - burn >= 2) (burn + 2):(t + 1) else integer(0)
        f4  <- function(x) sprintf("%.4f", x)
        ci4 <- function(x) sprintf("(%.4f, %.4f)", x[1], x[2])
        gm <- function(x) if (length(idx)) f4(mean(x[idx])) else "-"
        gs <- function(x) if (length(idx)) f4(sd(x[idx])) else "-"
        gq <- function(x) if (length(idx)) ci4(quantile(x[idx], c(0.025, 0.975))) else "-"
        data.frame(
            ` ` = c("mu: mean / estimate", "mu: sd / SE", "mu: 95% interval",
                    "sigma: mean / estimate", "sigma: sd / SE", "sigma: 95% interval"),
            `Exact posterior` = c(f4(d$exact["mean_mu"]), f4(d$exact["sd_mu"]), ci4(d$q_mu),
                                  f4(d$exact["mean_sg"]), f4(d$exact["sd_sg"]), ci4(d$q_sg)),
            Gibbs = c(gm(rv$mu), gs(rv$mu), gq(rv$mu), gm(rv$sg), gs(rv$sg), gq(rv$sg)),
            MLE = c(f4(m$mu), f4(m$se_mu), ci4(m$ci_mu), f4(m$sg), f4(m$se_sg), ci4(m$ci_sg)),
            check.names = FALSE)
    }, striped = TRUE, align = "lrrr", width = "100%")
}

shinyApp(ui, server)

title: Gibbs Sampling for the Cauchy Model with Unknown Location and Scale
text:
About the app
Shows a Gibbs sampler for the Cauchy model with unknown location and scale, built on data augmentation with a latent variance for each observation, and lets you step through the sampler one conditional update at a time.
The model and the augmentation. The data are \(y_1,\ldots,y_n\overset{iid}{\sim}\text{Cauchy}(\mu,\sigma)\), with the priors \(\mu\sim N(0,10^2)\) and \(\sigma^2\sim\text{Inverse-Gamma}(1,1)\). The Cauchy density has no conjugate form, but it is a scale mixture of normals: if \[y_i\mid\mu,\sigma,v_i\sim N(\mu,\,\sigma^2v_i),\qquad v_i\sim\text{Inverse-Gamma}\big(\tfrac12,\tfrac12\big)\ \text{independently},\] then integrating out \(v_i\) gives \(y_i\sim\text{Cauchy}(\mu,\sigma)\). Treating \(v_1,\ldots,v_n\) as extra unknowns, all the full conditionals are standard distributions.
The full conditionals. Write \(r_i=(y_i-\mu)/\sigma\). Multiplying the augmented likelihood by the priors gives \[v_i\mid\mu,\sigma,y\sim\text{Inverse-Gamma}\Big(1,\ \tfrac{1+r_i^2}{2}\Big),\] \[\mu\mid v,\sigma,y\sim N\Big(\frac{\mu_0/\tau^2+\sum_iy_i/(\sigma^2v_i)}{1/\tau^2+\sum_i1/(\sigma^2v_i)},\ \Big[\frac1{\tau^2}+\sum_i\frac1{\sigma^2v_i}\Big]^{-1}\Big),\] \[\sigma^2\mid\mu,v,y\sim\text{Inverse-Gamma}\Big(a_0+\tfrac n2,\ b_0+\sum_i\frac{(y_i-\mu)^2}{2v_i}\Big),\] with \(\mu_0=0\), \(\tau=10\), \(a_0=b_0=1\). One Gibbs iteration draws \(v\) given \((\mu,\sigma)\), then \(\mu\) given \((v,\sigma)\), then \(\sigma\) given \((\mu,v)\). A large \(r_i\) (an outlier) gives a large \(v_i\), which makes the observation contribute little to the draws of \(\mu\) and \(\sigma\); this is how the sampler reproduces the robustness of the Cauchy model.
The panels.

Top left: the exact joint posterior of \((\mu,\sigma)\) computed on a grid (contours and heat) with the Gibbs draws on top. The triangle is the starting value and the red dot the current state. With “show each Gibbs step” ticked, the plot shows the last two sub-steps: a green circle for the \(v\) update (it does not move \((\mu,\sigma)\)), an orange horizontal arrow for the \(\mu\) update and a blue vertical arrow for the \(\sigma\) update, which are the two legs of the staircase of a Gibbs sampler.
Top right: the current latent variances \(v_i\) (log scale) against \(y_i\); the outliers far from \(\mu\) have the largest \(v_i\).
Bottom: trace plots of \(\mu\) and \(\sigma\), with the exact posterior means (red dashed lines).
Table: for \(\mu\) and for \(\sigma\), the posterior mean, standard deviation and 95% credible interval, computed exactly on the grid and from the Gibbs draws so far (after discarding the first 20% as burn-in), next to the maximum likelihood estimate of the Cauchy model, its standard error and its 95% Wald interval. The MLE and its standard error come from the observed information at the maximum, and the interval for \(\sigma\) is formed on the log scale and transformed back so that it stays positive. The prior is weak, so the posterior is centred near the MLE, but the posterior (and the Gibbs draws) account for the uncertainty without the normal approximation: the credible interval for \(\sigma\) is asymmetric, and for small samples the Wald intervals are noticeably different.

Controls. Play and Pause advance the sampler automatically, Next advances by one step, End runs to the last iteration and Restart starts the chain again. With “show each Gibbs step” ticked, Play and Next move one sub-step at a time (update \(v\), then \(\mu\), then \(\sigma\)); with it unticked they move by whole iterations, and “iterations per tick” sets how many iterations Play takes at each tick. Changing the data, the number of iterations or the starting values restarts the chain.
What to try. The axes of the plane plot and of the traces are fixed to the exact posterior mean \(\pm3\) posterior standard deviations, so a starting value far from it (the default is \(\mu=-10,\sigma=6\)) is outside the view and the first few staircases enter from the edge. Then set the number of iterations to a few thousand and press End to see the chain mix and the table agree. Add outliers by increasing the sample size (a Cauchy sample always has some) and compare their \(v_i\) with those of the observations near \(\mu\).

library(shiny)

### renderPlot replacement: Safari 27 (WebKit) cannot hold the call stack of
### shiny::renderPlot in webR ("Maximum call stack size exceeded"), so draw with
### renderImage instead, which nests about 45 fewer R calls
renderPlot <- function(expr, width = "auto", height = "auto", res = 72, ...,
                       env = parent.frame(), quoted = FALSE) {
    func <- shiny::exprToFunction(expr, env, quoted)
    shiny::renderImage({
        info <- shiny::getCurrentOutputInfo()
        w  <- if (is.numeric(width))  width  else info$width()
        h  <- if (is.numeric(height)) height else info$height()
        shiny::req(w > 0, h > 0)
        pr <- shiny::getDefaultReactiveDomain()$clientData$pixelratio
        if (is.null(pr)) pr <- 1
        f   <- tempfile(fileext = ".png")
        dev <- shiny:::startPNG(f, w * pr, h * pr, res = res * pr)
        on.exit(grDevices::dev.off(dev), add = TRUE)
        grDevices::dev.control(displaylist = "enable")
        v <- withVisible(func())
        if (v$visible) print(v$value)
        list(src = f, contentType = "image/png", width = w, height = h,
             coordmap = shiny:::getCoordmap(v$value, w * pr, h * pr, res * pr))
    }, deleteFile = TRUE)
}

mu_0 <- 0; tau <- 10                                    # prior: mu ~ N(0, 10^2)
a_0 <- 1; b_0 <- 1                                      # prior: sigma^2 ~ Inverse-Gamma(1, 1)

ui <- fluidPage(
    wellPanel(
        fluidRow(
            column(3,
                sliderInput("n_obs", "number of observations", min = 5, max = 200, value = 30, step = 5),
                sliderInput("N", "number of Gibbs iterations", min = 50, max = 5000, value = 500, step = 50)),
            column(3,
                sliderInput("mu_true", "true location mu", min = -10, max = 10, value = 2, step = 0.5),
                sliderInput("sig_true", "true scale sigma", min = 0.2, max = 5, value = 1, step = 0.1)),
            column(3,
                sliderInput("mu_init", "starting value of mu", min = -20, max = 20, value = -10, step = 1),
                sliderInput("sig_init", "starting value of sigma", min = 0.2, max = 10, value = 6, step = 0.2)),
            column(3,
                sliderInput("speed", "iterations per tick", min = 1, max = 50, value = 1, step = 1),
                checkboxInput("sub", "show each Gibbs step", TRUE),
                actionButton("new", "New data", width = "100%"))),
        fluidRow(
            column(3, actionButton("play", "▶ Play", width = "100%")),
            column(3, actionButton("next_step", "Next ↷", width = "100%")),
            column(3, actionButton("end", "End ⏭", width = "100%")),
            column(3, actionButton("restart", "↺ Restart", width = "100%")))
    ),
    fluidRow(
        column(7,
            fluidRow(
                column(6, plotOutput("plane", height = "320px")),
                column(6, plotOutput("vplot", height = "320px"))),
            fluidRow(
                column(6, plotOutput("tr_mu", height = "240px")),
                column(6, plotOutput("tr_sg", height = "240px")))),
        column(5,
            tags$style("#tab td, #tab th { white-space: nowrap; font-size: 85%; }"),
            h5("Where the sampler is"),
            textOutput("status"),
            h5("Posterior summaries"),
            tableOutput("tab"))
    )
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {

    ### data: y_i ~ Cauchy(mu_true, sig_true)
    dat <- reactive({
        set.seed(100 + input$new)
        y <- input$mu_true + input$sig_true * rcauchy(input$n_obs)
        n <- length(y)
        ### exact joint posterior of (mu, sigma) on a grid, for the contours and the exact summaries:
        ### a wide first pass locates the mass, a second pass on the region that holds 99.9% of it refines
        post_grid <- function(mu_g, sg_g) {
            ll <- matrix(0, 200, 200)
            for (yi in y) ll <- ll + outer(mu_g, sg_g, function(m, s) dcauchy(yi, m, s, log = TRUE))
            lp_sigma <- log(2 * sg_g) + a_0 * log(b_0) - lgamma(a_0) - (a_0 + 1) * log(sg_g^2) - b_0 / sg_g^2
            lpost <- ll + dnorm(mu_g, mu_0, tau, log = TRUE) + matrix(lp_sigma, 200, 200, byrow = TRUE)
            p <- exp(lpost - max(lpost)); p / sum(p)
        }
        span <- function(g, marg) {
            cdf <- cumsum(marg); r <- g[c(max(1, which(cdf > 0.0005)[1] - 1), min(length(g), which(cdf > 0.9995)[1] + 1))]
            pad <- 0.2 * diff(r); c(r[1] - pad, r[2] + pad)
        }
        m0 <- median(y); s0 <- max(IQR(y) / 2, 0.5)
        mu_g <- seq(m0 - 8 * s0, m0 + 8 * s0, length.out = 200)
        sg_g <- seq(0.05, 6 * s0 + 2, length.out = 200)
        p <- post_grid(mu_g, sg_g)
        mr <- span(mu_g, rowSums(p)); sr <- span(sg_g, colSums(p))
        mu_g <- seq(mr[1], mr[2], length.out = 200)
        sg_g <- seq(max(sr[1], 0.02), sr[2], length.out = 200)
        p <- post_grid(mu_g, sg_g)
        pm <- rowSums(p); ps <- colSums(p)
        e_mu <- sum(pm * mu_g); e_sg <- sum(ps * sg_g)
        q_of <- function(g, marg) approx(cumsum(marg), g, xout = c(0.025, 0.975), rule = 2)$y
        ### maximum likelihood for Cauchy(mu, sigma) with a Wald interval from the observed information
        ### (the interval for sigma is formed on the log scale and transformed back)
        nll <- function(th) -sum(dcauchy(y, th[1], exp(th[2]), log = TRUE))
        fit <- optim(c(median(y), log(s0)), nll, method = "BFGS", hessian = TRUE)
        se  <- tryCatch(sqrt(diag(solve(fit$hessian))), error = function(e) c(NA, NA))
        mle <- list(mu = fit$par[1], sg = exp(fit$par[2]), se_mu = se[1], se_sg = exp(fit$par[2]) * se[2],
                    ci_mu = fit$par[1] + c(-1, 1) * 1.96 * se[1],
                    ci_sg = exp(fit$par[2] + c(-1, 1) * 1.96 * se[2]))
        list(y = y, n = n, mu_g = mu_g, sg_g = sg_g, post = p, mle = mle,
             q_mu = q_of(mu_g, pm), q_sg = q_of(sg_g, ps),
             exact = c(mean_mu = e_mu, mean_sg = e_sg,
                       sd_mu = sqrt(sum(pm * (mu_g - e_mu)^2)), sd_sg = sqrt(sum(ps * (sg_g - e_sg)^2))))
    })

    rv <- reactiveValues(N = 500, t = 0, phase = 0, mu = NULL, sg = NULL, v = NULL,
                         cur_mu = 0, cur_sg = 1, path = NULL, np = 0, last = "", playing = FALSE)

    reset_run <- function() {
        N <- input$N
        rv$N <- N; rv$t <- 0; rv$phase <- 0
        rv$mu <- c(input$mu_init, rep(NA_real_, N)); rv$sg <- c(input$sig_init, rep(NA_real_, N))
        rv$cur_mu <- input$mu_init; rv$cur_sg <- input$sig_init
        rv$v <- NULL
        rv$path <- matrix(NA_real_, 3 * N + 2, 3)            # columns: mu, sigma, sub-step (0 start, 1 v, 2 mu, 3 sigma)
        rv$path[1, ] <- c(input$mu_init, input$sig_init, 0); rv$np <- 1
        rv$last <- "start"
        rv$playing <- FALSE
        updateActionButton(session, "play", label = "▶ Play")
        set.seed(1000 + input$new)
    }

    add_path <- function(code) {
        rv$np <- rv$np + 1
        rv$path[rv$np, ] <- c(rv$cur_mu, rv$cur_sg, code)
    }

    ### one Gibbs sub-step: (1) the latent variances v_i, (2) mu, (3) sigma
    step_one <- function() {
        d <- dat(); y <- d$y; n <- d$n
        if (rv$t >= rv$N && rv$phase == 0) return(invisible(NULL))
        if (rv$phase == 0) {
            r2 <- (y - rv$cur_mu)^2 / rv$cur_sg^2
            rv$v <- 1 / rgamma(n, shape = 1, rate = (1 + r2) / 2)                 # v_i | mu, sigma, y_i ~ IG(1, (1 + r_i^2)/2)
            rv$phase <- 1; rv$last <- "v_i | mu, sigma"; add_path(1)
        } else if (rv$phase == 1) {
            prec <- 1 / tau^2 + sum(1 / (rv$cur_sg^2 * rv$v))
            mean <- (mu_0 / tau^2 + sum(y / (rv$cur_sg^2 * rv$v))) / prec
            rv$cur_mu <- rnorm(1, mean, 1 / sqrt(prec))                            # mu | v, sigma, y ~ normal
            rv$phase <- 2; rv$last <- "mu | v, sigma"; add_path(2)
        } else {
            rate <- b_0 + sum((y - rv$cur_mu)^2 / (2 * rv$v))
            rv$cur_sg <- sqrt(1 / rgamma(1, shape = a_0 + n / 2, rate = rate))     # sigma^2 | mu, v, y ~ inverse gamma
            rv$phase <- 0; rv$t <- rv$t + 1; rv$last <- "sigma | mu, v"; add_path(3)
            rv$mu[rv$t + 1] <- rv$cur_mu; rv$sg[rv$t + 1] <- rv$cur_sg
        }
    }
    step_iter <- function() {                       # finish the current iteration, or run a whole one
        repeat {
            step_one()
            if (rv$phase == 0 || rv$t >= rv$N) break
        }
    }
    finished <- function() rv$t >= rv$N && rv$phase == 0

    observeEvent(list(input$n_obs, input$mu_true, input$sig_true, input$N, input$mu_init, input$sig_init,
                      input$new, input$restart),
                 { req(input$N, input$mu_init, input$sig_init); reset_run() })

    observeEvent(input$play, {
        if (finished()) return()
        rv$playing <- !rv$playing
        updateActionButton(session, "play", label = if (rv$playing) "⏸ Pause" else "▶ Play")
    })
    observeEvent(input$next_step, {
        rv$playing <- FALSE; updateActionButton(session, "play", label = "▶ Play")
        if (isTRUE(input$sub)) step_one() else step_iter()
    })
    observeEvent(input$end, {
        rv$playing <- FALSE; updateActionButton(session, "play", label = "▶ Play")
        while (!finished()) step_iter()
    })
    observe({
        if (isTRUE(rv$playing)) {
            invalidateLater(150, session)
            isolate({
                if (isTRUE(input$sub)) step_one() else for (k in seq_len(input$speed)) step_iter()
                if (finished()) { rv$playing <- FALSE; updateActionButton(session, "play", label = "▶ Play") }
            })
        }
    })

    output$status <- renderText({
        req(rv$mu)
        sprintf("iteration %d / %d; current (mu, sigma) = (%.3f, %.3f)", rv$t, rv$N, rv$cur_mu, rv$cur_sg)
    })

    ### the (mu, sigma) plane: exact posterior contours, the Gibbs draws, and optionally the path of each step
    output$plane <- renderPlot({
        req(rv$mu); d <- dat(); t <- rv$t
        ex <- d$exact                                          # the window is the exact posterior mean +- 3 sd, not the starting value
        xlim <- ex["mean_mu"] + c(-3, 3) * ex["sd_mu"]; ylim <- ex["mean_sg"] + c(-3, 3) * ex["sd_sg"]
        par(mar = c(4, 4, 3, 1))
        cols <- hcl.colors(30, "YlOrRd", rev = TRUE)
        plot(NA, xlim = xlim, ylim = ylim, xlab = expression(mu), ylab = expression(sigma),
             main = "Gibbs draws on the exact posterior")
        rect(par("usr")[1], par("usr")[3], par("usr")[2], par("usr")[4], col = cols[1], border = NA)
        image(d$mu_g, d$sg_g, d$post, col = cols, add = TRUE)
        contour(d$mu_g, d$sg_g, d$post, nlevels = 6, drawlabels = FALSE, add = TRUE, col = "gray40")
        if (t >= 1) points(rv$mu[2:(t + 1)], rv$sg[2:(t + 1)], pch = 19, cex = 0.4, col = adjustcolor("black", 0.45))
        points(input$mu_init, input$sig_init, pch = 17, col = "steelblue", cex = 1.4)
        if (isTRUE(input$sub) && rv$np >= 2) {
            k <- max(2, rv$np - 1):rv$np                                    # the last two sub-steps
            P <- rv$path
            for (j in k) {
                if (P[j, 3] == 2) arrows(P[j - 1, 1], P[j - 1, 2], P[j, 1], P[j, 2], length = 0.08, lwd = 2, col = "darkorange")
                if (P[j, 3] == 3) arrows(P[j - 1, 1], P[j - 1, 2], P[j, 1], P[j, 2], length = 0.08, lwd = 2, col = "steelblue")
                if (P[j, 3] == 1) points(P[j, 1], P[j, 2], pch = 1, cex = 2.2, lwd = 2, col = "forestgreen")
            }
        }
        points(rv$cur_mu, rv$cur_sg, pch = 19, cex = 1.3, col = "red")
        legend("topright", bty = "n", cex = 0.8, pch = c(19, 17, 19), col = c("black", "steelblue", "red"),
               legend = c("draws", "start", "current"))
    })

    ### the augmented variances v_i: outlying observations get large v_i, so they are downweighted
    output$vplot <- renderPlot({
        req(rv$mu); d <- dat(); par(mar = c(4, 4, 3, 1))
        if (is.null(rv$v)) {
            plot(d$y, rep(1, d$n), type = "n", log = "y", xlab = "y", ylab = expression(v[i]),
                 main = expression("latent variances"~v[i]~"(not drawn yet)"))
            rug(d$y)
        } else {
            plot(d$y, rv$v, log = "y", pch = 19, col = adjustcolor("forestgreen", 0.7), xlab = "y",
                 ylab = expression(v[i]), main = expression("latent variances"~v[i]~"(current)"))
            abline(v = rv$cur_mu, col = "red", lty = 2)
            legend("topright", bty = "n", cex = 0.8, lty = 2, col = "red", legend = expression(current~mu))
        }
    })

    trace_plot <- function(x, exact, sd, ylab) {
        par(mar = c(4, 4, 2, 1))
        plot(0:rv$N, x, type = "n", xlab = "iteration", ylab = ylab,
             ylim = exact + c(-3, 3) * sd)                                  # window around the posterior, not the start
        lines(0:rv$t, x[1:(rv$t + 1)], col = "gray30")
        abline(h = exact, col = "red", lty = 2)
    }
    output$tr_mu <- renderPlot({ req(rv$mu); d <- dat(); trace_plot(rv$mu, d$exact["mean_mu"], d$exact["sd_mu"], expression(mu)) })
    output$tr_sg <- renderPlot({ req(rv$mu); d <- dat(); trace_plot(rv$sg, d$exact["mean_sg"], d$exact["sd_sg"], expression(sigma)) })

    output$tab <- renderTable({
        req(rv$mu); d <- dat(); t <- rv$t; m <- d$mle
        burn <- floor(0.2 * t)
        idx <- if (t - burn >= 2) (burn + 2):(t + 1) else integer(0)
        f4  <- function(x) sprintf("%.4f", x)
        ci4 <- function(x) sprintf("(%.4f, %.4f)", x[1], x[2])
        gm <- function(x) if (length(idx)) f4(mean(x[idx])) else "-"
        gs <- function(x) if (length(idx)) f4(sd(x[idx])) else "-"
        gq <- function(x) if (length(idx)) ci4(quantile(x[idx], c(0.025, 0.975))) else "-"
        data.frame(
            ` ` = c("mu: mean / estimate", "mu: sd / SE", "mu: 95% interval",
                    "sigma: mean / estimate", "sigma: sd / SE", "sigma: 95% interval"),
            `Exact posterior` = c(f4(d$exact["mean_mu"]), f4(d$exact["sd_mu"]), ci4(d$q_mu),
                                  f4(d$exact["mean_sg"]), f4(d$exact["sd_sg"]), ci4(d$q_sg)),
            Gibbs = c(gm(rv$mu), gs(rv$mu), gq(rv$mu), gm(rv$sg), gs(rv$sg), gq(rv$sg)),
            MLE = c(f4(m$mu), f4(m$se_mu), ci4(m$ci_mu), f4(m$sg), f4(m$se_sg), ci4(m$ci_sg)),
            check.names = FALSE)
    }, striped = TRUE, align = "lrrr", width = "100%")
}

### ---------- Cauchy location model ------------------------------------------
## Negative log-likelihood of a location theta for data x (the constant
## n*log(pi) is dropped), its gradient g = L' and its curvature J = L''.
nll  <- function(th, x)
    vapply(th, function(t) sum(log1p((x - t)^2)), numeric(1))
gfun <- function(th, x)
    vapply(th, function(t) -sum(2 * (x - t) / (1 + (x - t)^2)), numeric(1))
jfun <- function(th, x)
    vapply(th, function(t) sum(2 * (1 - (x - t)^2) / (1 + (x - t)^2)^2),
           numeric(1))

### ---------- robustification of the curvature -------------------------------
## The Newton step is -g / J.  Where J <= 0 (the tails) it points uphill, and
## where J is close to 0 it is enormous.  Two repairs replace J by J~ > 0:
##   ridge   : J~ = J + tau, with tau >= 0 the smallest value giving
##             J~ >= rho * n/2   (Levenberg-Marquardt; in one dimension this
##             is the same as flooring the curvature at rho * n/2)
##   scoring : J~ = n/2, the expected information of n Cauchy observations
adjust_curv <- function(J, method, n, rho) {
    switch(method,
           none    = J,
           ridge   = J + max(0, rho * n / 2 - J),
           scoring = n / 2)
}

### ---------- Newton-Raphson path --------------------------------------------
## Returns the iterates with L, g, J, the curvature actually used (J~), the
## proposed step and the fraction s of it that was accepted.  Stops on
## convergence, or when the iteration breaks down.
newton_path <- function(th0, x, maxit = 25, halve = FALSE, robust = "none",
                        rho = 0.2, tol = 1e-9) {
    n <- length(x)
    cn <- c("theta", "nll", "g", "J", "Jt", "step", "s")
    P <- matrix(NA_real_, maxit + 1, length(cn), dimnames = list(NULL, cn))
    fill <- function(i, th) {
        J <- jfun(th, x)
        P[i, 1:5] <<- c(th, nll(th, x), gfun(th, x), J,
                        adjust_curv(J, robust, n, rho))
    }
    th <- th0; fill(1, th)
    n_ok <- 1; note <- "maximum number of iterations reached"
    for (i in seq_len(maxit)) {
        g <- P[i, 3]; Jt <- P[i, 5]
        if (abs(g) < 1e-12) { note <- "converged: the gradient is zero"; break }
        if (!is.finite(Jt) || Jt == 0) {
            note <- "the curvature is zero: the Newton step is undefined"
            break
        }
        step <- -g / Jt
        P[i, 6] <- step
        s <- 1
        ## step halving: shrink s until the Armijo condition
        ## L(theta + s*step) <= L(theta) + c1 * s * g * step holds
        if (halve) {
            if (g * step >= 0) {
                note <- paste("the step points uphill (the curvature is not",
                              "positive), so halving cannot help: stopped")
                break
            }
            f0 <- P[i, 2]
            while (s > 1e-12) {
                fn <- nll(th + s * step, x)
                if (is.finite(fn) && fn <= f0 + 1e-4 * s * g * step) break
                s <- s / 2
            }
            if (s <= 1e-12) { note <- "halving found no decrease: stopped"; break }
        }
        th <- th + s * step
        if (!is.finite(th)) { note <- "the iterate is no longer finite: diverged"; break }
        P[i, 7] <- s
        fill(i + 1, th)
        n_ok <- i + 1
        if (abs(th) > 1e6) { note <- "diverged: the iterate has run off to infinity"; break }
        if (abs(s * step) < tol) { note <- "converged"; break }
    }
    list(P = P[seq_len(n_ok), , drop = FALSE], n = n_ok, note = note)
}

## an icon-only playback button; the title shows as a tooltip
