### ---------- server ----------------------------------------------------------
server <- function(input, output, session) {

    playing <- reactiveVal(FALSE)
    play_ms <- 900

    ## clicking either plot moves the starting value
    set_start <- function(cl) {
        if (!is.null(cl) && is.finite(cl$x))
            updateNumericInput(session, "th0", value = round(cl$x, 2))
    }
    observeEvent(input$clickL, set_start(input$clickL))
    observeEvent(input$clickg, set_start(input$clickg))

    x <- reactive({
        if (input$data == "single") return(0)
        req(input$n, input$seed)
        set.seed(input$seed)
        rcauchy(max(1, round(input$n)), location = 0)
    })

    ## the plotted window is centred on the median of the data
    win <- reactive(median(x()) + c(-1, 1) * input$W)

    start <- reactive({ req(is.finite(input$th0)); input$th0 })

    modified <- reactive(input$halve != "none" || input$robust != "none")

    path <- reactive(newton_path(start(), x(), halve = input$halve == "halve",
                                 robust = input$robust,
                                 rho = if (is.null(input$rho)) 0.2 else input$rho))

    ## the plain (unsafeguarded) path, shown for comparison
    ref <- reactive({
        if (!isTRUE(input$compare) || !modified()) return(NULL)
        newton_path(start(), x())
    })

    ## curves on a fixed grid over the window
    grid <- reactive({
        th <- seq(win()[1], win()[2], length.out = 600)
        list(th = th, L = nll(th, x()), g = gfun(th, x()))
    })

    ## current iteration, clamped to the length of the path
    k <- reactive(min(as.integer(input$iter), path()$n - 1))

    ## a new path restarts the display at iteration 0
    observeEvent(path(), {
        updateSliderInput(session, "iter", max = max(1, path()$n - 1), value = 0)
        playing(isTRUE(input$autoplay) && path()$n > 1)
    })

    go_to <- function(i) {
        updateSliderInput(session, "iter",
                          value = max(0, min(i, path()$n - 1)))
    }

    observeEvent(input$play, {
        if (k() >= path()$n - 1) go_to(0)
        if (path()$n > 1) playing(TRUE)
    })
    observeEvent(input$pause, playing(FALSE))
    observeEvent(input$step,  { playing(FALSE); go_to(k() + 1) })
    observeEvent(input$back,  { playing(FALSE); go_to(k() - 1) })
    observeEvent(input$first, { playing(FALSE); go_to(0) })
    observeEvent(input$toend, { playing(FALSE); go_to(path()$n - 1) })

    observe({
        if (!isTRUE(playing())) return()
        kk <- isolate(k())
        if (kk >= isolate(path()$n) - 1) { playing(FALSE); return() }
        invalidateLater(play_ms, session)
        isolate(go_to(kk + 1))
    })

    in_win <- function(v) v >= win()[1] & v <= win()[2]

    ## the marks shared by both plots: data, the grid minimum, the plain path
    base_marks <- function() {
        rug(x(), col = "darkgreen", lwd = 2, ticksize = 0.05)
    }

    output$pL <- renderPlot({
        G <- grid(); P <- path()$P; kk <- k() + 1L; RP <- ref()
        par(mar = c(4, 4.5, 2, 1))
        plot(G$th, G$L, type = "l", lwd = 2, col = "grey30",
             xlab = expression(theta), ylab = expression(L(theta)),
             main = "negative log-likelihood and the Newton iterates")
        base_marks()
        i0 <- which.min(G$L)
        points(G$th[i0], G$L[i0], pch = 4, col = "darkgreen", lwd = 2, cex = 1.3)

        if (!is.null(RP)) {
            Q <- RP$P[seq_len(min(kk, RP$n)), , drop = FALSE]
            Q <- Q[in_win(Q[, 1]), , drop = FALSE]
            if (nrow(Q) > 1) lines(Q[, 1], Q[, 2], col = "grey45", lty = 2, lwd = 2)
            points(Q[, 1], Q[, 2], pch = 21, bg = "grey85", col = "grey45", cex = 0.9)
        }
        Q <- P[1:kk, , drop = FALSE]; Q <- Q[in_win(Q[, 1]), , drop = FALSE]
        if (nrow(Q) > 1) lines(Q[, 1], Q[, 2], col = "steelblue", lwd = 2)
        points(Q[, 1], Q[, 2], pch = 21, bg = "steelblue", cex = 1.1)

        cur <- P[kk, ]
        if (in_win(cur[1])) {
            points(cur[1], cur[2], pch = 21, bg = "firebrick", cex = 1.8)
        } else {
            mtext(sprintf("current iterate (theta = %.3g) is outside the plotted window",
                          cur[1]), side = 3, line = -1.5, col = "firebrick",
                  cex = 0.9)
        }
        leg <- c("current iterate", "minimum in the window", "data")
        legend("top", bg = "#ffffffcc", box.col = NA, cex = 0.85, ncol = 3,
               pch = c(21, 4, NA), pt.bg = c("firebrick", NA, NA),
               lwd = c(NA, 2, 2), lty = c(NA, NA, 1),
               col = c("black", "darkgreen", "darkgreen"), legend = leg)
    })

    output$pg <- renderPlot({
        G <- grid(); P <- path()$P; kk <- k() + 1L; RP <- ref()
        par(mar = c(4, 4.5, 2, 1))
        plot(G$th, G$g, type = "l", lwd = 2, col = "grey30",
             xlab = expression(theta), ylab = expression(g(theta)),
             main = "gradient and the tangent (Newton) steps")
        abline(h = 0, lty = 3)
        base_marks()

        ## each step follows the line through (theta_k, g_k) whose slope is
        ## the curvature that was used, J~, down to the horizontal axis
        draw_steps <- function(Q, col, lwd, lty) {
            m <- nrow(Q)
            if (m < 2) return()
            for (i in seq_len(m - 1)) {
                segments(Q[i, 1], Q[i, 3], Q[i, 1] + Q[i, 6], 0,
                         col = col, lwd = lwd, lty = lty)
                if (isTRUE(Q[i, 7] < 1))      # halved: mark where the full step lands
                    points(Q[i, 1] + Q[i, 6], 0, pch = 4, col = col, cex = 0.9)
                else
                    segments(Q[i + 1, 1], 0, Q[i + 1, 1], Q[i + 1, 3],
                             col = "grey40", lty = 3)
            }
        }
        if (!is.null(RP)) {
            Q <- RP$P[seq_len(min(kk, RP$n)), , drop = FALSE]
            draw_steps(Q, "grey65", 1.5, 2)
            Q <- Q[in_win(Q[, 1]), , drop = FALSE]
            points(Q[, 1], Q[, 3], pch = 21, bg = "grey85", col = "grey45", cex = 0.9)
        }
        draw_steps(P[1:kk, , drop = FALSE], "steelblue", 2, 1)
        Q <- P[1:kk, , drop = FALSE]; Q <- Q[in_win(Q[, 1]), , drop = FALSE]
        points(Q[, 1], Q[, 3], pch = 21, bg = "steelblue", cex = 1.1)
        cur <- P[kk, ]
        if (in_win(cur[1])) {
            points(cur[1], cur[3], pch = 21, bg = "firebrick", cex = 1.8)
        } else {
            mtext(sprintf("current iterate (theta = %.3g) is outside the plotted window",
                          cur[1]), side = 3, line = -1.5, col = "firebrick",
                  cex = 0.9)
        }
    })

    ## significant digits throughout; a diverging run reaches values that would
    ## otherwise be far too wide
    fs <- function(v) ifelse(!is.finite(v), "", formatC(v, digits = 4, format = "g"))

    ## why the run ended, shown as one line under the table
    output$note <- renderUI({
        R <- path(); RP <- ref()
        if (k() + 1 < R$n) return(NULL)
        HTML(paste0("<i>", R$note,
                    if (!is.null(RP)) paste0("; plain Newton-Raphson: ", RP$note),
                    "</i>"))
    })

    output$tab <- renderTable({
        P <- path()$P[seq_len(k() + 1), , drop = FALSE]
        d <- data.frame(iteration = as.character(seq_len(nrow(P)) - 1),
                        theta = fs(P[, 1]), `L(theta)` = fs(P[, 2]),
                        g = fs(P[, 3]), J = fs(P[, 4]), `J~ used` = fs(P[, 5]),
                        `step kept` = ifelse(is.na(P[, 7]), "", fs(P[, 7])),
                        check.names = FALSE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
        tail(d, 6)
    }, rownames = FALSE, align = "r", width = "100%")
}

title: Newton-Raphson on the Cauchy Likelihood
text:
About the app
Shows how the Newton-Raphson step diverges on the univariate Cauchy location likelihood, and how step halving and a robustified Hessian each repair it. The upper plot is the negative log-likelihood \(L(\theta) = \sum_i \log\{1 + (x_i - \theta)^2\}\) with the iterates marked on it; the lower plot is its gradient \(g = L'\), where each Newton step is drawn as the line through \((\theta_k, g_k)\) whose slope is the curvature used, followed down to the horizontal axis.
Click in either plot (or type a value) to choose the starting value \(\theta_0\), then use the playback buttons to step through the iterations or play the path as an animation. With one observation at \(0\) the gradient \(g(\theta) = 2\theta/(1+\theta^2)\) flattens in the tails and the curvature \(J = L''\) turns negative for \(|\theta| > 1\), so the tangent points away from the minimum and the iterates run off to infinity; plain Newton-Raphson converges only from starts with \(|\theta_0| < 1/\sqrt{3}\). Choose a random sample instead to see the same behaviour on a likelihood with several local minima.
The two safeguards act on different parts of the step \(-g/\tilde J\). Step halving shortens a step until the Armijo condition holds, so it tames the length but cannot fix a step that points uphill. Robustifying the Hessian replaces \(J\) by a positive \(\tilde J\), which fixes the direction: ridge adds the smallest \(\tau \ge 0\) that makes \(J + \tau \ge \varepsilon\), and Fisher scoring uses the expected information \(n/2\). In one dimension ridging and flooring the curvature coincide. Switching on either keeps the plain iteration visible as a dashed grey path for comparison; the details of each iteration, and the reason the run ended, are reported under the plots.

gfun <- function(th, x)
    vapply(th, function(t) -sum(2 * (x - t) / (1 + (x - t)^2)), numeric(1))
jfun <- function(th, x)
    vapply(th, function(t) sum(2 * (1 - (x - t)^2) / (1 + (x - t)^2)^2),
           numeric(1))

### ---------- robustification of the curvature -------------------------------
## The Newton step is -g / J.  Where J <= 0 (the tails) it points uphill, and
## where J is close to 0 it is enormous.  Two repairs replace J by J~ > 0:
##   ridge   : J~ = J + tau, with tau >= 0 the smallest value giving
##             J~ >= rho * n/2   (Levenberg-Marquardt; in one dimension this
##             is the same as flooring the curvature at rho * n/2)
##   scoring : J~ = n/2, the expected information of n Cauchy observations
adjust_curv <- function(J, method, n, rho) {
    switch(method,
           none    = J,
           ridge   = J + max(0, rho * n / 2 - J),
           scoring = n / 2)
}

### ---------- Newton-Raphson path --------------------------------------------
## Returns the iterates with L, g, J, the curvature actually used (J~), the
## proposed step and the fraction s of it that was accepted.  Stops on
## convergence, or when the iteration breaks down.
newton_path <- function(th0, x, maxit = 25, halve = FALSE, robust = "none",
                        rho = 0.2, tol = 1e-9) {
    n <- length(x)
    cn <- c("theta", "nll", "g", "J", "Jt", "step", "s")
    P <- matrix(NA_real_, maxit + 1, length(cn), dimnames = list(NULL, cn))
    fill <- function(i, th) {
        J <- jfun(th, x)
        P[i, 1:5] <<- c(th, nll(th, x), gfun(th, x), J,
                        adjust_curv(J, robust, n, rho))
    }
    th <- th0; fill(1, th)
    n_ok <- 1; note <- "maximum number of iterations reached"
    for (i in seq_len(maxit)) {
        g <- P[i, 3]; Jt <- P[i, 5]
        if (abs(g) < 1e-12) { note <- "converged: the gradient is zero"; break }
        if (!is.finite(Jt) || Jt == 0) {
            note <- "the curvature is zero: the Newton step is undefined"
            break
        }
        step <- -g / Jt
        P[i, 6] <- step
        s <- 1
        ## step halving: shrink s until the Armijo condition
        ## L(theta + s*step) <= L(theta) + c1 * s * g * step holds
        if (halve) {
            if (g * step >= 0) {
                note <- paste("the step points uphill (the curvature is not",
                              "positive), so halving cannot help: stopped")
                break
            }
            f0 <- P[i, 2]
            while (s > 1e-12) {
                fn <- nll(th + s * step, x)
                if (is.finite(fn) && fn <= f0 + 1e-4 * s * g * step) break
                s <- s / 2
            }
            if (s <= 1e-12) { note <- "halving found no decrease: stopped"; break }
        }
        th <- th + s * step
        if (!is.finite(th)) { note <- "the iterate is no longer finite: diverged"; break }
        P[i, 7] <- s
        fill(i + 1, th)
        n_ok <- i + 1
        if (abs(th) > 1e6) { note <- "diverged: the iterate has run off to infinity"; break }
        if (abs(s * step) < tol) { note <- "converged"; break }
    }
    list(P = P[seq_len(n_ok), , drop = FALSE], n = n_ok, note = note)
}

### ---------- server ----------------------------------------------------------
server <- function(input, output, session) {

    playing <- reactiveVal(FALSE)
    play_ms <- 900

    ## clicking either plot moves the starting value
    set_start <- function(cl) {
        if (!is.null(cl) && is.finite(cl$x))
            updateNumericInput(session, "th0", value = round(cl$x, 2))
    }
    observeEvent(input$clickL, set_start(input$clickL))
    observeEvent(input$clickg, set_start(input$clickg))

    x <- reactive({
        if (input$data == "single") return(0)
        req(input$n, input$seed)
        set.seed(input$seed)
        rcauchy(max(1, round(input$n)), location = 0)
    })

    ## the plotted window is centred on the median of the data
    win <- reactive(median(x()) + c(-1, 1) * input$W)

    start <- reactive({ req(is.finite(input$th0)); input$th0 })

    modified <- reactive(input$halve != "none" || input$robust != "none")

    path <- reactive(newton_path(start(), x(), halve = input$halve == "halve",
                                 robust = input$robust,
                                 rho = if (is.null(input$rho)) 0.2 else input$rho))

    ## the plain (unsafeguarded) path, shown for comparison
    ref <- reactive({
        if (!isTRUE(input$compare) || !modified()) return(NULL)
        newton_path(start(), x())
    })

    ## curves on a fixed grid over the window
    grid <- reactive({
        th <- seq(win()[1], win()[2], length.out = 600)
        list(th = th, L = nll(th, x()), g = gfun(th, x()))
    })

    ## current iteration, clamped to the length of the path
    k <- reactive(min(as.integer(input$iter), path()$n - 1))

    ## a new path restarts the display at iteration 0
    observeEvent(path(), {
        updateSliderInput(session, "iter", max = max(1, path()$n - 1), value = 0)
        playing(isTRUE(input$autoplay) && path()$n > 1)
    })

    go_to <- function(i) {
        updateSliderInput(session, "iter",
                          value = max(0, min(i, path()$n - 1)))
    }

    observeEvent(input$play, {
        if (k() >= path()$n - 1) go_to(0)
        if (path()$n > 1) playing(TRUE)
    })
    observeEvent(input$pause, playing(FALSE))
    observeEvent(input$step,  { playing(FALSE); go_to(k() + 1) })
    observeEvent(input$back,  { playing(FALSE); go_to(k() - 1) })
    observeEvent(input$first, { playing(FALSE); go_to(0) })
    observeEvent(input$toend, { playing(FALSE); go_to(path()$n - 1) })

    observe({
        if (!isTRUE(playing())) return()
        kk <- isolate(k())
        if (kk >= isolate(path()$n) - 1) { playing(FALSE); return() }
        invalidateLater(play_ms, session)
        isolate(go_to(kk + 1))
    })

    in_win <- function(v) v >= win()[1] & v <= win()[2]

    ## the marks shared by both plots: data, the grid minimum, the plain path
    base_marks <- function() {
        rug(x(), col = "darkgreen", lwd = 2, ticksize = 0.05)
    }

    output$pL <- renderPlot({
        G <- grid(); P <- path()$P; kk <- k() + 1L; RP <- ref()
        par(mar = c(4, 4.5, 2, 1))
        plot(G$th, G$L, type = "l", lwd = 2, col = "grey30",
             xlab = expression(theta), ylab = expression(L(theta)),
             main = "negative log-likelihood and the Newton iterates")
        base_marks()
        i0 <- which.min(G$L)
        points(G$th[i0], G$L[i0], pch = 4, col = "darkgreen", lwd = 2, cex = 1.3)

        if (!is.null(RP)) {
            Q <- RP$P[seq_len(min(kk, RP$n)), , drop = FALSE]
            Q <- Q[in_win(Q[, 1]), , drop = FALSE]
            if (nrow(Q) > 1) lines(Q[, 1], Q[, 2], col = "grey45", lty = 2, lwd = 2)
            points(Q[, 1], Q[, 2], pch = 21, bg = "grey85", col = "grey45", cex = 0.9)
        }
        Q <- P[1:kk, , drop = FALSE]; Q <- Q[in_win(Q[, 1]), , drop = FALSE]
        if (nrow(Q) > 1) lines(Q[, 1], Q[, 2], col = "steelblue", lwd = 2)
        points(Q[, 1], Q[, 2], pch = 21, bg = "steelblue", cex = 1.1)

        cur <- P[kk, ]
        if (in_win(cur[1])) {
            points(cur[1], cur[2], pch = 21, bg = "firebrick", cex = 1.8)
        } else {
            mtext(sprintf("current iterate (theta = %.3g) is outside the plotted window",
                          cur[1]), side = 3, line = -1.5, col = "firebrick",
                  cex = 0.9)
        }
        leg <- c("current iterate", "minimum in the window", "data")
        legend("top", bg = "#ffffffcc", box.col = NA, cex = 0.85, ncol = 3,
               pch = c(21, 4, NA), pt.bg = c("firebrick", NA, NA),
               lwd = c(NA, 2, 2), lty = c(NA, NA, 1),
               col = c("black", "darkgreen", "darkgreen"), legend = leg)
    })

    output$pg <- renderPlot({
        G <- grid(); P <- path()$P; kk <- k() + 1L; RP <- ref()
        par(mar = c(4, 4.5, 2, 1))
        plot(G$th, G$g, type = "l", lwd = 2, col = "grey30",
             xlab = expression(theta), ylab = expression(g(theta)),
             main = "gradient and the tangent (Newton) steps")
        abline(h = 0, lty = 3)
        base_marks()

        ## each step follows the line through (theta_k, g_k) whose slope is
        ## the curvature that was used, J~, down to the horizontal axis
        draw_steps <- function(Q, col, lwd, lty) {
            m <- nrow(Q)
            if (m < 2) return()
            for (i in seq_len(m - 1)) {
                segments(Q[i, 1], Q[i, 3], Q[i, 1] + Q[i, 6], 0,
                         col = col, lwd = lwd, lty = lty)
                if (isTRUE(Q[i, 7] < 1))      # halved: mark where the full step lands
                    points(Q[i, 1] + Q[i, 6], 0, pch = 4, col = col, cex = 0.9)
                else
                    segments(Q[i + 1, 1], 0, Q[i + 1, 1], Q[i + 1, 3],
                             col = "grey40", lty = 3)
            }
        }
        if (!is.null(RP)) {
            Q <- RP$P[seq_len(min(kk, RP$n)), , drop = FALSE]
            draw_steps(Q, "grey65", 1.5, 2)
            Q <- Q[in_win(Q[, 1]), , drop = FALSE]
            points(Q[, 1], Q[, 3], pch = 21, bg = "grey85", col = "grey45", cex = 0.9)
        }
        draw_steps(P[1:kk, , drop = FALSE], "steelblue", 2, 1)
        Q <- P[1:kk, , drop = FALSE]; Q <- Q[in_win(Q[, 1]), , drop = FALSE]
        points(Q[, 1], Q[, 3], pch = 21, bg = "steelblue", cex = 1.1)
        cur <- P[kk, ]
        if (in_win(cur[1])) {
            points(cur[1], cur[3], pch = 21, bg = "firebrick", cex = 1.8)
        } else {
            mtext(sprintf("current iterate (theta = %.3g) is outside the plotted window",
                          cur[1]), side = 3, line = -1.5, col = "firebrick",
                  cex = 0.9)
        }
    })

    ## significant digits throughout; a diverging run reaches values that would
    ## otherwise be far too wide
    fs <- function(v) ifelse(!is.finite(v), "", formatC(v, digits = 4, format = "g"))

    ## why the run ended, shown as one line under the table
    output$note <- renderUI({
        R <- path(); RP <- ref()
        if (k() + 1 < R$n) return(NULL)
        HTML(paste0("<i>", R$note,
                    if (!is.null(RP)) paste0("; plain Newton-Raphson: ", RP$note),
                    "</i>"))
    })

    output$tab <- renderTable({
        P <- path()$P[seq_len(k() + 1), , drop = FALSE]
        d <- data.frame(iteration = as.character(seq_len(nrow(P)) - 1),
                        theta = fs(P[, 1]), `L(theta)` = fs(P[, 2]),
                        g = fs(P[, 3]), J = fs(P[, 4]), `J~ used` = fs(P[, 5]),
                        `step kept` = ifelse(is.na(P[, 7]), "", fs(P[, 7])),
                        check.names = FALSE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
        tail(d, 6)
    }, rownames = FALSE, align = "r", width = "100%")
}

### renderPlot replacement: Safari 27 (WebKit) cannot hold the call stack of
### shiny::renderPlot in webR ("Maximum call stack size exceeded"), so draw with
### renderImage instead, which nests about 45 fewer R calls
renderPlot <- function(expr, width = "auto", height = "auto", res = 72, ...,
                       env = parent.frame(), quoted = FALSE) {
    func <- shiny::exprToFunction(expr, env, quoted)
    shiny::renderImage({
        info <- shiny::getCurrentOutputInfo()
        w  <- if (is.numeric(width))  width  else info$width()
        h  <- if (is.numeric(height)) height else info$height()
        shiny::req(w > 0, h > 0)
        pr <- shiny::getDefaultReactiveDomain()$clientData$pixelratio
        if (is.null(pr)) pr <- 1
        f   <- tempfile(fileext = ".png")
        dev <- shiny:::startPNG(f, w * pr, h * pr, res = res * pr)
        on.exit(grDevices::dev.off(dev), add = TRUE)
        grDevices::dev.control(displaylist = "enable")
        v <- withVisible(func())
        if (v$visible) print(v$value)
        list(src = f, contentType = "image/png", width = w, height = h,
             coordmap = shiny:::getCoordmap(v$value, w * pr, h * pr, res * pr))
    }, deleteFile = TRUE)
}

h <- function(x) -x^2 / 2          # log unnormalized N(0,1) density
hprime <- function(x) -x

build_hull <- function(xs, lb, ub) {
    xs <- sort(xs)
    hx <- h(xs); hpx <- hprime(xs)
    k <- length(xs)
    z <- numeric(k + 1); z[1] <- lb; z[k + 1] <- ub
    if (k > 1) for (i in 1:(k - 1)) {
        z[i + 1] <- (hx[i + 1] - hx[i] - xs[i + 1] * hpx[i + 1] + xs[i] * hpx[i]) /
            (hpx[i] - hpx[i + 1])
    }
    list(x = xs, hx = hx, hp = hpx, z = z)
}

### log-area under the exponential of a single tangent-line piece, between its
### breakpoints -- computed entirely in log space so it stays finite even far
### out in the tail, where exp(hull value) itself would underflow to exactly 0
log_piece_area <- function(hull, j) {
    a <- hull$hx[j]; b <- hull$hp[j]; xj <- hull$x[j]
    lo <- hull$z[j]; hi <- hull$z[j + 1]
    val_lo <- a + b * (lo - xj); val_hi <- a + b * (hi - xj)
    if (abs(b) < 1e-10) return(val_lo + log(hi - lo))
    m <- max(val_lo, val_hi); d <- min(val_lo, val_hi)
    m + log1p(-exp(d - m)) - log(abs(b))
}

### draw one point from the piecewise-exponential envelope: pick a piece
### proportional to its area, then invert its (exponential) CDF within it --
### both steps done on the log scale for the same underflow-safety reason
sample_hull <- function(hull) {
    k <- length(hull$x)
    log_areas <- vapply(seq_len(k), function(j) log_piece_area(hull, j), numeric(1))
    log_areas[!is.finite(log_areas)] <- -Inf
    areas <- exp(log_areas - max(log_areas))    # relative areas, safely in (0, 1]
    logA  <- max(log_areas) + log(sum(areas))   # log of the total area under the envelope
    j <- sample.int(k, 1, prob = areas)
    a <- hull$hx[j]; b <- hull$hp[j]; xj <- hull$x[j]
    lo <- hull$z[j]; hi <- hull$z[j + 1]
    U <- runif(1)
    if (abs(b) < 1e-10) {
        x <- lo + U * (hi - lo)
        logg <- a
    } else {
        val_lo <- a + b * (lo - xj); val_hi <- a + b * (hi - xj)
        m <- max(val_lo, val_hi)
        val_x <- m + log((1 - U) * exp(val_lo - m) + U * exp(val_hi - m))
        x <- xj + (val_x - a) / b
        logg <- val_x
    }
    list(x = x, logg = logg, logA = logA)
}

### piecewise-linear hull value (log scale) at a vector of x's
hull_val <- function(hull, xgrid) {
    j <- findInterval(xgrid, hull$z, rightmost.closed = TRUE)
    j <- pmax(1, pmin(j, length(hull$x)))
    hull$hx[j] + hull$hp[j] * (xgrid - hull$x[j])
}

init_hull <- function(lb, ub) {
    x_init <- sort(unique(pmin(pmax(c(lb + 0.25 * (ub - lb), (lb + ub) / 2,
                                       ub - 0.25 * (ub - lb)), lb + 1e-6), ub - 1e-6)))
    build_hull(x_init, lb, ub)
}

### smart plotting window: view = [mode - 2, mode + 2], clipped to [lb, ub],
### where "mode" is the peak of the density *within* the truncation window --
### 0 if the window straddles it, otherwise whichever edge is nearest 0 (the
### window is then entirely on one side of the peak, so the density is
### monotonic and highest right at that edge). A wide window far out in the
### tail (e.g. [100, 200]) would otherwise dilute the whole plot into a
### mostly-flat, uninformative sliver near that one edge.
smart_xlim <- function(lb, ub) {
    m <- if (lb >= 0) lb else if (ub <= 0) ub else 0
    c(max(lb, m - 2), min(ub, m + 2))
}

### log(pnorm(ub) - pnorm(lb)), numerically stable even when the naive
### difference underflows to 0 for windows far out in either tail
log_pnorm_diff <- function(lb, ub) {
    if (ub <= 0) {
        log_pu <- pnorm(ub, log.p = TRUE); log_pl <- pnorm(lb, log.p = TRUE)
        log_pu + log1p(-exp(log_pl - log_pu))
    } else if (lb >= 0) {
        log_su <- pnorm(ub, lower.tail = FALSE, log.p = TRUE)
        log_sl <- pnorm(lb, lower.tail = FALSE, log.p = TRUE)
        log_sl + log1p(-exp(log_su - log_sl))
    } else {
        log(pnorm(ub) - pnorm(lb))
    }
}
tnorm_density <- function(x, lb, ub) exp(dnorm(x, log = TRUE) - log_pnorm_diff(lb, ub))

ui <- fluidPage(

        fluidRow(
            column(2, numericInput("n", "sample size (target)", value = 200, min = 1, step = 10)),
            column(4, sliderInput("lim", "truncation interval (l, u)", min = -10, max = 10,

        helpText("Each step draws one candidate from the current hull. ",

server <- function(input, output, session) {

    rv <- reactiveValues(hull = NULL, samples = numeric(0), tries = 0, target_n = 200,
                          lb = -2, ub = 2, done = FALSE, playing = FALSE,
                          last_x = NULL, last_accept = NA, logsumw = -Inf, logsumw2 = -Inf)

    reset_run <- function() {
        lb <- if (!is.null(input$lim)) input$lim[1] else -2
        ub <- if (!is.null(input$lim)) input$lim[2] else 2
        if (ub - lb < 0.05) ub <- lb + 0.05      # guard against a degenerate window
        rv$hull <- init_hull(lb, ub)
        rv$samples <- numeric(0)
        rv$tries <- 0
        rv$lb <- lb; rv$ub <- ub
        rv$target_n <- if (!is.null(input$n) && !is.na(input$n) && input$n >= 1) input$n else 200
        rv$done <- FALSE
        rv$playing <- FALSE
        rv$last_x <- NULL; rv$last_accept <- NA
        rv$logsumw <- -Inf; rv$logsumw2 <- -Inf
        updateActionButton(session, "play_pause", label = "▶ Play")
    }
    isolate(reset_run())

    do_step <- function() {
        if (rv$done) return(invisible(NULL))
        draw <- sample_hull(rv$hull)
        x <- draw$x; logg <- draw$logg; logf <- h(x)
        rv$tries <- rv$tries + 1
        ### importance weight of this proposal under the envelope that generated it:
        ### w = f(x) / g_t(x) with g_t = envelope / (its area), so log w = log f - log envelope + log area
        lw <- logf - logg + draw$logA
        mw <- max(rv$logsumw, lw)
        rv$logsumw <- mw + log(exp(rv$logsumw - mw) + exp(lw - mw))
        mw2 <- max(rv$logsumw2, 2 * lw)                  # running sum of w^2, for the standard error
        rv$logsumw2 <- mw2 + log(exp(rv$logsumw2 - mw2) + exp(2 * lw - mw2))
        accept <- log(runif(1)) < logf - logg
        rv$last_x <- x; rv$last_accept <- accept
        if (accept) {
            rv$samples <- c(rv$samples, x)
        } else {
            rv$hull <- build_hull(sort(c(rv$hull$x, x)), rv$lb, rv$ub)
        }
        if (length(rv$samples) >= rv$target_n) {
            rv$done <- TRUE
            rv$playing <- FALSE
            updateActionButton(session, "play_pause", label = "▶ Play")
        }
    }

    observeEvent(input$lim, { reset_run() }, ignoreInit = TRUE)
    observeEvent(input$restart, { reset_run() })

    observeEvent(input$n, {
        req(input$n)
        rv$target_n <- input$n
        if (length(rv$samples) < rv$target_n) rv$done <- FALSE
    }, ignoreInit = TRUE)

    observeEvent(input$play_pause, {
        if (rv$done) return()
        rv$playing <- !rv$playing
        updateActionButton(session, "play_pause",
                            label = if (rv$playing) "⏸ Pause" else "▶ Play")
    })

    observeEvent(input$next_step, {
        rv$playing <- FALSE
        updateActionButton(session, "play_pause", label = "▶ Play")
        do_step()
    })

    ### auto-advance one step every 120ms while playing
    observe({
        if (isTRUE(rv$playing) && !rv$done) {
            invalidateLater(120, session)
            isolate(do_step())
        }
    })

    ### P(l < X < u) for X ~ N(0,1): Z = integral of exp(-x^2/2) over (l, u) = sqrt(2 pi) P(l < X < u), and
    ### the mean of the importance weights of ALL proposals (each under its own envelope) estimates Z.
    ### The standard error uses the sample variance of the weights (an approximation, since the
    ### weights come from a varying sequence of proposals), so the interval is estimate * (1 +- 1.96 se_rel)
    output$tab <- renderTable({
        fmt  <- function(lp) if (lp > -700) sprintf("%.4g", exp(lp)) else sprintf("exp(%.4f)", lp)   # probability
        flog <- function(lp) sprintf("%.4f", lp)                                                     # log probability
        log_true <- log_pnorm_diff(rv$lb, rv$ub)
        T <- rv$tries
        est <- c("-", "-"); ci <- c("-", "-")
        if (T >= 2) {
            log_m  <- rv$logsumw - log(T)                          # log of the mean weight
            rel_se <- sqrt(max(expm1(rv$logsumw2 - log(T) - 2 * log_m), 0) / T)
            log_est <- log_m - 0.5 * log(2 * pi)
            lo <- log_est + log(max(1 - 1.96 * rel_se, 1e-12)); hi <- log_est + log1p(1.96 * rel_se)
            est <- c(fmt(log_est), flog(log_est))
            ci  <- c(sprintf("(%s, %s)", fmt(lo), fmt(hi)), sprintf("(%s, %s)", flog(lo), flog(hi)))
        }
        data.frame(
            ` ` = c("true", "IS estimate", "95% CI"),
            `P(l < X < u)` = c(fmt(log_true), est[1], ci[1]),
            `log P` = c(flog(log_true), est[2], ci[2]),
            check.names = FALSE)
    }, striped = TRUE, align = "lll", width = "100%")

    output$status <- renderText({
        sprintf("%d / %d samples accepted  |  %d proposals  |  %d tangent points",
                length(rv$samples), rv$target_n, rv$tries, length(rv$hull$x))
    })

    output$panels <- renderPlot({
        hull <- rv$hull; lb <- rv$lb; ub <- rv$ub
        dl <- smart_xlim(lb, ub)
        xg <- seq(dl[1], dl[2], length.out = 400)
        hull_log <- hull_val(hull, xg); target_log <- h(xg)

        par(mfrow = c(2, 1), mar = c(4, 4, 3, 1))

        plot(xg, hull_log, type = "l", lwd = 2, col = "steelblue",
             ylim = range(c(hull_log, target_log)), xlab = "x",
             ylab = "log density (unnormalized)",
             main = sprintf("log target vs. hull (%d tangent points)", length(hull$x)))
        lines(xg, target_log, lwd = 2, col = "firebrick")
        points(hull$x, hull$hx, pch = 19, col = "gray20", cex = 0.9)
        abline(v = hull$z[-c(1, length(hull$z))], col = adjustcolor("gray40", 0.4), lty = 3)
        abline(v = c(lb, ub), col = "darkorange", lty = 2)
        if (!is.null(rv$last_x)) {
            points(rv$last_x, h(rv$last_x), pch = if (rv$last_accept) 19 else 4,
                   col = if (rv$last_accept) "forestgreen" else "black", cex = 1.6, lwd = 2)
        }
        legend("bottomleft", bty = "n", cex = 0.85,
               lwd = c(2, 2, 1, NA, NA), lty = c(1, 1, 2, NA, NA), pch = c(NA, NA, NA, 19, 4),
               col = c("steelblue", "firebrick", "darkorange", "forestgreen", "black"),
               legend = c("log hull", "log target", "truncation limits", "last: accepted", "last: rejected"))

        if (length(rv$samples) == 0) {
            plot(0, 0, type = "n", xlim = dl, ylim = c(0, 1), xlab = "x", ylab = "",
                 main = "no samples accepted yet")
        } else {
            ### scale the bin count so ~30 bins fall within the *visible* view,
            ### not the full [lb, ub] window -- otherwise a wide window (e.g.
            ### [100, 200] zoomed to [100, 102]) puts everything in one giant bin
            n_bins <- min(5000, max(30, ceiling(30 * (ub - lb) / (dl[2] - dl[1]))))
            breaks <- seq(lb, ub, length.out = n_bins + 1)
            hist(rv$samples, breaks = breaks, freq = FALSE, col = "steelblue", border = "white",
                 xlim = dl, xlab = "x",
                 main = sprintf("%d / %d samples%s", length(rv$samples), rv$target_n,
                                 if (rv$done) "  (done)" else ""))
            curve(tnorm_density(x, lb, ub), add = TRUE, lwd = 3, col = "firebrick", n = 300)
            legend("topright", bty = "n", lwd = 3, col = "firebrick", legend = "true truncated-normal density")
        }
    })
}

title: Computing Normal Probability with Adaptive Rejection Sampling
text:
About the app
Shows how adaptive rejection sampling improves its envelope automatically, so that it becomes more efficient as sampling proceeds. The app above reimplements the same idea directly — start with a few tangent lines to \(\log f\), sample from the piecewise-exponential envelope they define, and whenever a candidate is rejected, add it as a new tangent point and rebuild the hull — one candidate at a time, so every step of the mechanism is visible. Next advances a single candidate; Play advances automatically.
The ars package above is a black box: it returns samples but not the sequence of hulls it built along the way. The top panel shows \(\log f\) against the current hull (in log scale the hull is exactly piecewise-linear, since it is built from tangent lines), marking the most recent candidate as accepted (green dot) or rejected (black x, becoming a new tangent point). The bottom panel is a histogram of the accepted draws so far against the true truncated normal density. Controls: the target sample size, and the truncation interval \([l, u]\), set with a two-handled slider from \(-10\) to \(10\) (changing the interval restarts the run).
Estimating a probability with the varying envelope. Besides producing exact draws from the truncated normal, the run gives an estimate of the normal probability \(P(l<X<u)\) for \(X\sim N(0,1)\), shown in the run summary beside the plots next to the true value, with a 95% confidence interval. Write \(f(x)=e^{-x^2/2}\) on \((l,u)\), so that \(Z=\int_l^u f(x)\,dx=\sqrt{2\pi}\,P(l<X<u)\). At proposal \(t\) the envelope is \(e_t(x)\ge f(x)\), with area \(A_t=\int e_t\), and the candidate is drawn from the normalized envelope \(g_t=e_t/A_t\). The envelope \(g_t\) changes whenever a rejection adds a tangent point, so the proposal varies from draw to draw. Importance sampling still works if each candidate is weighted by the proposal that actually generated it: \[w_t=\frac{f(X_t)}{g_t(X_t)}=A_t\,\frac{f(X_t)}{e_t(X_t)},\qquad \hat Z=\frac1T\sum_{t=1}^T w_t,\qquad \widehat{P}(l<X<u)=\frac{\hat Z}{\sqrt{2\pi}} .\] Conditional on the past, \(g_t\) is fixed, so \(E[w_t\mid \text{past}]=\int_l^u f=Z\) for every \(t\): each weight is unbiased for \(Z\) whatever the envelope is, and \(\hat Z\) is an average of martingale differences around \(Z\). It would be wrong to weight all the draws by the final envelope, because that would use information from later draws. All \(T\) proposals are used, rejected ones included (a rejected candidate is still a draw from \(g_t\) with a weight; it just also tightens the hull for the next step). The weights are bounded, \(0\le w_t\le A_t\) since \(f\le e_t\), so the variance is finite. As the hull tightens, \(e_t\to f\) and \(A_t\to Z\), so every weight approaches \(Z\) and the estimate becomes exact, which is why it improves with the number of tangent points. The interval is \(\hat P\,(1\pm1.96\,\widehat{\mathrm{se}}_{\rm rel})\), where \(\widehat{\mathrm{se}}_{\rm rel}=\sqrt{s_w^2/T}\big/\bar w\) is computed from the sample variance \(s_w^2\) of the weights. This is the usual importance-sampling standard error; because the proposals vary it is an approximation (the weights are martingale differences, not independent), but it is accurate once the hull has stopped changing much, and it shrinks quickly as the envelope tightens. The weights are accumulated on the log scale, so the estimate stays finite even for windows far out in the tail, where it is shown as \(\exp(\log P)\).

library(shiny)

### renderPlot replacement: Safari 27 (WebKit) cannot hold the call stack of
### shiny::renderPlot in webR ("Maximum call stack size exceeded"), so draw with
### renderImage instead, which nests about 45 fewer R calls
renderPlot <- function(expr, width = "auto", height = "auto", res = 72, ...,
                       env = parent.frame(), quoted = FALSE) {
    func <- shiny::exprToFunction(expr, env, quoted)
    shiny::renderImage({
        info <- shiny::getCurrentOutputInfo()
        w  <- if (is.numeric(width))  width  else info$width()
        h  <- if (is.numeric(height)) height else info$height()
        shiny::req(w > 0, h > 0)
        pr <- shiny::getDefaultReactiveDomain()$clientData$pixelratio
        if (is.null(pr)) pr <- 1
        f   <- tempfile(fileext = ".png")
        dev <- shiny:::startPNG(f, w * pr, h * pr, res = res * pr)
        on.exit(grDevices::dev.off(dev), add = TRUE)
        grDevices::dev.control(displaylist = "enable")
        v <- withVisible(func())
        if (v$visible) print(v$value)
        list(src = f, contentType = "image/png", width = w, height = h,
             coordmap = shiny:::getCoordmap(v$value, w * pr, h * pr, res * pr))
    }, deleteFile = TRUE)
}

h <- function(x) -x^2 / 2          # log unnormalized N(0,1) density
hprime <- function(x) -x

build_hull <- function(xs, lb, ub) {
    xs <- sort(xs)
    hx <- h(xs); hpx <- hprime(xs)
    k <- length(xs)
    z <- numeric(k + 1); z[1] <- lb; z[k + 1] <- ub
    if (k > 1) for (i in 1:(k - 1)) {
        z[i + 1] <- (hx[i + 1] - hx[i] - xs[i + 1] * hpx[i + 1] + xs[i] * hpx[i]) /
            (hpx[i] - hpx[i + 1])
    }
    list(x = xs, hx = hx, hp = hpx, z = z)
}

### log-area under the exponential of a single tangent-line piece, between its
### breakpoints -- computed entirely in log space so it stays finite even far
### out in the tail, where exp(hull value) itself would underflow to exactly 0
log_piece_area <- function(hull, j) {
    a <- hull$hx[j]; b <- hull$hp[j]; xj <- hull$x[j]
    lo <- hull$z[j]; hi <- hull$z[j + 1]
    val_lo <- a + b * (lo - xj); val_hi <- a + b * (hi - xj)
    if (abs(b) < 1e-10) return(val_lo + log(hi - lo))
    m <- max(val_lo, val_hi); d <- min(val_lo, val_hi)
    m + log1p(-exp(d - m)) - log(abs(b))
}

### draw one point from the piecewise-exponential envelope: pick a piece
### proportional to its area, then invert its (exponential) CDF within it --
### both steps done on the log scale for the same underflow-safety reason
sample_hull <- function(hull) {
    k <- length(hull$x)
    log_areas <- vapply(seq_len(k), function(j) log_piece_area(hull, j), numeric(1))
    log_areas[!is.finite(log_areas)] <- -Inf
    areas <- exp(log_areas - max(log_areas))    # relative areas, safely in (0, 1]
    logA  <- max(log_areas) + log(sum(areas))   # log of the total area under the envelope
    j <- sample.int(k, 1, prob = areas)
    a <- hull$hx[j]; b <- hull$hp[j]; xj <- hull$x[j]
    lo <- hull$z[j]; hi <- hull$z[j + 1]
    U <- runif(1)
    if (abs(b) < 1e-10) {
        x <- lo + U * (hi - lo)
        logg <- a
    } else {
        val_lo <- a + b * (lo - xj); val_hi <- a + b * (hi - xj)
        m <- max(val_lo, val_hi)
        val_x <- m + log((1 - U) * exp(val_lo - m) + U * exp(val_hi - m))
        x <- xj + (val_x - a) / b
        logg <- val_x
    }
    list(x = x, logg = logg, logA = logA)
}

### piecewise-linear hull value (log scale) at a vector of x's
hull_val <- function(hull, xgrid) {
    j <- findInterval(xgrid, hull$z, rightmost.closed = TRUE)
    j <- pmax(1, pmin(j, length(hull$x)))
    hull$hx[j] + hull$hp[j] * (xgrid - hull$x[j])
}

init_hull <- function(lb, ub) {
    x_init <- sort(unique(pmin(pmax(c(lb + 0.25 * (ub - lb), (lb + ub) / 2,
                                       ub - 0.25 * (ub - lb)), lb + 1e-6), ub - 1e-6)))
    build_hull(x_init, lb, ub)
}

### smart plotting window: view = [mode - 2, mode + 2], clipped to [lb, ub],
### where "mode" is the peak of the density *within* the truncation window --
### 0 if the window straddles it, otherwise whichever edge is nearest 0 (the
### window is then entirely on one side of the peak, so the density is
### monotonic and highest right at that edge). A wide window far out in the
### tail (e.g. [100, 200]) would otherwise dilute the whole plot into a
### mostly-flat, uninformative sliver near that one edge.
smart_xlim <- function(lb, ub) {
    m <- if (lb >= 0) lb else if (ub <= 0) ub else 0
    c(max(lb, m - 2), min(ub, m + 2))
}

### log(pnorm(ub) - pnorm(lb)), numerically stable even when the naive
### difference underflows to 0 for windows far out in either tail
log_pnorm_diff <- function(lb, ub) {
    if (ub <= 0) {
        log_pu <- pnorm(ub, log.p = TRUE); log_pl <- pnorm(lb, log.p = TRUE)
        log_pu + log1p(-exp(log_pl - log_pu))
    } else if (lb >= 0) {
        log_su <- pnorm(ub, lower.tail = FALSE, log.p = TRUE)
        log_sl <- pnorm(lb, lower.tail = FALSE, log.p = TRUE)
        log_sl + log1p(-exp(log_su - log_sl))
    } else {
        log(pnorm(ub) - pnorm(lb))
    }
}
tnorm_density <- function(x, lb, ub) exp(dnorm(x, log = TRUE) - log_pnorm_diff(lb, ub))

ui <- fluidPage(
    wellPanel(
        fluidRow(
            column(2, numericInput("n", "sample size (target)", value = 200, min = 1, step = 10)),
            column(4, sliderInput("lim", "truncation interval (l, u)", min = -10, max = 10,
                                  value = c(-2, 2), step = 0.1)),
            column(2, br(), actionButton("play_pause", "▶ Play", width = "100%")),
            column(2, br(), actionButton("next_step", "Next ↷", width = "100%")),
            column(2, br(), actionButton("restart", "↺ Restart", width = "100%"))),
        helpText("Each step draws one candidate from the current hull. ",
                 "Accepted points (green) join the histogram; rejected ",
                 "points (black x) become new tangent lines, tightening ",
                 "the hull. Changing the limits restarts the run. Every proposal, ",
                 "accepted or not, also gets an importance weight under the hull ",
                 "that produced it; their mean estimates P(l < X < u).")
    ),
    fluidRow(
        column(8, plotOutput("panels", height = "560px")),
        column(4,
            tags$style("#tab td, #tab th { white-space: nowrap; }"),
            h5("Run summary"),
            tableOutput("tab"),
            textOutput("status"))
    )
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {

    rv <- reactiveValues(hull = NULL, samples = numeric(0), tries = 0, target_n = 200,
                          lb = -2, ub = 2, done = FALSE, playing = FALSE,
                          last_x = NULL, last_accept = NA, logsumw = -Inf, logsumw2 = -Inf)

    reset_run <- function() {
        lb <- if (!is.null(input$lim)) input$lim[1] else -2
        ub <- if (!is.null(input$lim)) input$lim[2] else 2
        if (ub - lb < 0.05) ub <- lb + 0.05      # guard against a degenerate window
        rv$hull <- init_hull(lb, ub)
        rv$samples <- numeric(0)
        rv$tries <- 0
        rv$lb <- lb; rv$ub <- ub
        rv$target_n <- if (!is.null(input$n) && !is.na(input$n) && input$n >= 1) input$n else 200
        rv$done <- FALSE
        rv$playing <- FALSE
        rv$last_x <- NULL; rv$last_accept <- NA
        rv$logsumw <- -Inf; rv$logsumw2 <- -Inf
        updateActionButton(session, "play_pause", label = "▶ Play")
    }
    isolate(reset_run())

    do_step <- function() {
        if (rv$done) return(invisible(NULL))
        draw <- sample_hull(rv$hull)
        x <- draw$x; logg <- draw$logg; logf <- h(x)
        rv$tries <- rv$tries + 1
        ### importance weight of this proposal under the envelope that generated it:
        ### w = f(x) / g_t(x) with g_t = envelope / (its area), so log w = log f - log envelope + log area
        lw <- logf - logg + draw$logA
        mw <- max(rv$logsumw, lw)
        rv$logsumw <- mw + log(exp(rv$logsumw - mw) + exp(lw - mw))
        mw2 <- max(rv$logsumw2, 2 * lw)                  # running sum of w^2, for the standard error
        rv$logsumw2 <- mw2 + log(exp(rv$logsumw2 - mw2) + exp(2 * lw - mw2))
        accept <- log(runif(1)) < logf - logg
        rv$last_x <- x; rv$last_accept <- accept
        if (accept) {
            rv$samples <- c(rv$samples, x)
        } else {
            rv$hull <- build_hull(sort(c(rv$hull$x, x)), rv$lb, rv$ub)
        }
        if (length(rv$samples) >= rv$target_n) {
            rv$done <- TRUE
            rv$playing <- FALSE
            updateActionButton(session, "play_pause", label = "▶ Play")
        }
    }

    observeEvent(input$lim, { reset_run() }, ignoreInit = TRUE)
    observeEvent(input$restart, { reset_run() })

    observeEvent(input$n, {
        req(input$n)
        rv$target_n <- input$n
        if (length(rv$samples) < rv$target_n) rv$done <- FALSE
    }, ignoreInit = TRUE)

    observeEvent(input$play_pause, {
        if (rv$done) return()
        rv$playing <- !rv$playing
        updateActionButton(session, "play_pause",
                            label = if (rv$playing) "⏸ Pause" else "▶ Play")
    })

    observeEvent(input$next_step, {
        rv$playing <- FALSE
        updateActionButton(session, "play_pause", label = "▶ Play")
        do_step()
    })

    ### auto-advance one step every 120ms while playing
    observe({
        if (isTRUE(rv$playing) && !rv$done) {
            invalidateLater(120, session)
            isolate(do_step())
        }
    })

    ### P(l < X < u) for X ~ N(0,1): Z = integral of exp(-x^2/2) over (l, u) = sqrt(2 pi) P(l < X < u), and
    ### the mean of the importance weights of ALL proposals (each under its own envelope) estimates Z.
    ### The standard error uses the sample variance of the weights (an approximation, since the
    ### weights come from a varying sequence of proposals), so the interval is estimate * (1 +- 1.96 se_rel)
    output$tab <- renderTable({
        fmt  <- function(lp) if (lp > -700) sprintf("%.4g", exp(lp)) else sprintf("exp(%.4f)", lp)   # probability
        flog <- function(lp) sprintf("%.4f", lp)                                                     # log probability
        log_true <- log_pnorm_diff(rv$lb, rv$ub)
        T <- rv$tries
        est <- c("-", "-"); ci <- c("-", "-")
        if (T >= 2) {
            log_m  <- rv$logsumw - log(T)                          # log of the mean weight
            rel_se <- sqrt(max(expm1(rv$logsumw2 - log(T) - 2 * log_m), 0) / T)
            log_est <- log_m - 0.5 * log(2 * pi)
            lo <- log_est + log(max(1 - 1.96 * rel_se, 1e-12)); hi <- log_est + log1p(1.96 * rel_se)
            est <- c(fmt(log_est), flog(log_est))
            ci  <- c(sprintf("(%s, %s)", fmt(lo), fmt(hi)), sprintf("(%s, %s)", flog(lo), flog(hi)))
        }
        data.frame(
            ` ` = c("true", "IS estimate", "95% CI"),
            `P(l < X < u)` = c(fmt(log_true), est[1], ci[1]),
            `log P` = c(flog(log_true), est[2], ci[2]),
            check.names = FALSE)
    }, striped = TRUE, align = "lll", width = "100%")

    output$status <- renderText({
        sprintf("%d / %d samples accepted  |  %d proposals  |  %d tangent points",
                length(rv$samples), rv$target_n, rv$tries, length(rv$hull$x))
    })

    output$panels <- renderPlot({
        hull <- rv$hull; lb <- rv$lb; ub <- rv$ub
        dl <- smart_xlim(lb, ub)
        xg <- seq(dl[1], dl[2], length.out = 400)
        hull_log <- hull_val(hull, xg); target_log <- h(xg)

        par(mfrow = c(2, 1), mar = c(4, 4, 3, 1))

        plot(xg, hull_log, type = "l", lwd = 2, col = "steelblue",
             ylim = range(c(hull_log, target_log)), xlab = "x",
             ylab = "log density (unnormalized)",
             main = sprintf("log target vs. hull (%d tangent points)", length(hull$x)))
        lines(xg, target_log, lwd = 2, col = "firebrick")
        points(hull$x, hull$hx, pch = 19, col = "gray20", cex = 0.9)
        abline(v = hull$z[-c(1, length(hull$z))], col = adjustcolor("gray40", 0.4), lty = 3)
        abline(v = c(lb, ub), col = "darkorange", lty = 2)
        if (!is.null(rv$last_x)) {
            points(rv$last_x, h(rv$last_x), pch = if (rv$last_accept) 19 else 4,
                   col = if (rv$last_accept) "forestgreen" else "black", cex = 1.6, lwd = 2)
        }
        legend("bottomleft", bty = "n", cex = 0.85,
               lwd = c(2, 2, 1, NA, NA), lty = c(1, 1, 2, NA, NA), pch = c(NA, NA, NA, 19, 4),
               col = c("steelblue", "firebrick", "darkorange", "forestgreen", "black"),
               legend = c("log hull", "log target", "truncation limits", "last: accepted", "last: rejected"))

        if (length(rv$samples) == 0) {
            plot(0, 0, type = "n", xlim = dl, ylim = c(0, 1), xlab = "x", ylab = "",
                 main = "no samples accepted yet")
        } else {
            ### scale the bin count so ~30 bins fall within the *visible* view,
            ### not the full [lb, ub] window -- otherwise a wide window (e.g.
            ### [100, 200] zoomed to [100, 102]) puts everything in one giant bin
            n_bins <- min(5000, max(30, ceiling(30 * (ub - lb) / (dl[2] - dl[1]))))
            breaks <- seq(lb, ub, length.out = n_bins + 1)
            hist(rv$samples, breaks = breaks, freq = FALSE, col = "steelblue", border = "white",
                 xlim = dl, xlab = "x",
                 main = sprintf("%d / %d samples%s", length(rv$samples), rv$target_n,
                                 if (rv$done) "  (done)" else ""))
            curve(tnorm_density(x, lb, ub), add = TRUE, lwd = 3, col = "firebrick", n = 300)
            legend("topright", bty = "n", lwd = 3, col = "firebrick", legend = "true truncated-normal density")
        }
    })
}

server <- function(input, output, session) {

    n_eff <- 3; sigma_prior <- 5                    # likelihood as if 3 obs, sigma = 1; prior N(0, 5^2)

    ### everything that depends on mu_hat: the kernel z, the true log P(y), and the two grid transforms
    setup <- function(mu_hat) {
        log_z <- function(mu) dnorm(mu_hat, mu, 1 / sqrt(n_eff), log = TRUE) +
            dnorm(mu, 0, sigma_prior, log = TRUE)
        z <- function(mu) exp(log_z(mu))
        ### normal-normal conjugate kernel: the exact log marginal likelihood, mu_hat ~ N(0, 1/n_eff + sigma_prior^2)
        ### (integrate() is no longer reliable once the narrow peak lies far out)
        log_marlik <- dnorm(mu_hat, 0, sqrt(1 / n_eff + sigma_prior^2), log = TRUE)
        ### Laplace approximation for THIS mu_hat: its mode and se define the second transform
        op <- nlm(function(mu) -log_z(mu), p = mu_hat, hessian = TRUE)
        m  <- op$estimate
        se <- 1 / sqrt(op$hessian[1, 1])
        log_lap <- -op$minimum + 0.5 * log(2 * pi) + log(se)   # Laplace approximation: log z(mode) + log of sqrt(2 pi) se
        list(z = z, log_z = log_z, log_marlik = log_marlik, log_lap = log_lap,
             logit = list(q = qlogis, p = plogis, d = dlogis,
                          lab = expression(u == 1 / (1 + e^-mu)),
                          main = "Logistic grid: mu = logit(u)"),
             laplace = list(q = function(u) qnorm(u, m, se), p = function(mu) pnorm(mu, m, se),
                            d = function(mu) dnorm(mu, m, se),
                            lab = expression(u == Phi((mu - hat(mu)[L]) / s[L])),
                            main = "Laplace-normalized grid: mu = mode + se * qnorm(u)"))
    }

    log_sum_exp <- function(lx) { m <- max(lx); m + log(sum(exp(lx - m))) }

    ### the midpoint rule in u with n points, mapped back to mu by the transform q; d = du/dmu
    log_midpoint <- function(S, tr, n) {
        u_pts <- (seq_len(n) - 0.5) / n
        mu_pts <- tr$q(u_pts)
        log_sum_exp(S$log_z(mu_pts) - log(tr$d(mu_pts))) + log(1 / n)
    }

    ### the grid is the midpoint rule in u, mapped back to mu by the transform q; d = du/dmu
    mu_plot <- function(type) {
        S <- setup(input$mu_hat); tr <- S[[type]]
        mu_grid <- seq(-20, 20, length.out = 500)          # fixed x-axis
        u_pts   <- (seq_len(input$n_pts) - 0.5) / input$n_pts
        mu_pts  <- tr$q(u_pts)
        log_quad <- log_midpoint(S, tr, input$n_pts)

        par(mar = c(4, 4, 2, 4))
        plot(mu_grid, S$z(mu_grid), type = "l", lwd = 3, col = "firebrick", main = tr$main,
             xlab = expression(mu), ylab = expression(z(mu) == pi(mu) * L(mu)))
        polygon(c(mu_grid, rev(mu_grid)), c(S$z(mu_grid), rep(0, length(mu_grid))),
                col = adjustcolor("firebrick", 0.15), border = NA)
        segments(mu_pts, 0, mu_pts, S$z(mu_pts), col = "gray30", lwd = 1.5)
        points(mu_pts, S$z(mu_pts), pch = 19, col = "gray30")

        par(new = TRUE)
        plot(mu_grid, tr$p(mu_grid), type = "l", lwd = 3, col = "steelblue",
             axes = FALSE, xlab = "", ylab = "", ylim = c(0, 1))
        axis(4, col.axis = "steelblue", col.ticks = "steelblue")
        mtext(tr$lab, side = 4, line = 2.5, col = "steelblue")

        guide_col <- adjustcolor("gray50", 0.6)
        segments(mu_pts, 0, mu_pts, u_pts, col = guide_col, lty = 3)
        segments(mu_pts, u_pts, max(mu_grid), u_pts, col = guide_col, lty = 3)
        points(mu_pts, u_pts, pch = 19, col = "gray30")

        legend("topleft", bty = "n", lwd = c(3, 3, NA, NA), col = c("firebrick", "steelblue", NA, NA),
               cex = 0.85,
               legend = c(expression(z(mu) == pi(mu) * L(mu)), tr$lab,
                          as.expression(bquote("true"~log~P(y) == .(round(S$log_marlik, 3)))),
                          as.expression(bquote("quadrature"~log~P(y) == .(round(log_quad, 3))))))
    }

    ### the function the midpoint rule integrates over u: g(u) = z(q(u)) / d(q(u)), with rectangles
    u_plot <- function(type) {
        S <- setup(input$mu_hat); tr <- S[[type]]
        g <- function(u) { mu <- tr$q(u); exp(S$log_z(mu) - log(tr$d(mu))) }
        n      <- input$n_pts
        h      <- 1 / n
        u_pts  <- (seq_len(n) - 0.5) / n
        g_pts  <- g(u_pts)
        u_fine <- seq(0.0005, 0.9995, length.out = 2000)
        g_fine <- g(u_fine)
        true_val <- exp(S$log_marlik)                      # the area is the same for every transform
        quad_val <- sum(g_pts) * h

        par(mar = c(4, 4, 2, 1))
        plot(u_fine, g_fine, type = "l", lwd = 3, col = "firebrick", main = "Integrand in u",
             ylim = c(0, max(g_fine, g_pts) * 1.45), xlab = expression(u),   # head room for the legend
             ylab = expression(g(u) == z(mu(u)) / (du / dmu)))
        rect(u_pts - h / 2, 0, u_pts + h / 2, g_pts,
             col = adjustcolor("gray50", 0.3), border = "gray30")
        points(u_pts, g_pts, pch = 19, col = "gray30")
        legend("topright", bty = "n", lwd = c(3, NA, NA), col = c("firebrick", NA, NA), cex = 0.85,
               legend = c(expression(g(u)),
                          as.expression(bquote("true area" == .(signif(true_val, 4)))),
                          as.expression(bquote("midpoint rule" == .(signif(quad_val, 4))))))
    }

    output$tab <- renderTable({
        S <- setup(input$mu_hat); n <- input$n_pts
        est <- c(S$log_marlik, S$log_lap, log_midpoint(S, S$logit, n), log_midpoint(S, S$laplace, n))
        data.frame(
            Method = c("True", "Laplace", sprintf("Logistic grid, n = %d", n),
                       sprintf("Laplace grid, n = %d", n)),
            Evals = c("-", "1", n, n),
            `log P(y)` = sprintf("%.3f", est),
            Error = c("", sprintf("%.3f", est[-1] - est[1])),
            check.names = FALSE)
    }, striped = TRUE, align = "lrrr")

    output$mu_logit   <- renderPlot(mu_plot("logit"))
    output$u_logit    <- renderPlot(u_plot("logit"))
    output$mu_laplace <- renderPlot(mu_plot("laplace"))
    output$u_laplace  <- renderPlot(u_plot("laplace"))
}

title: Computing ML of Normal Data with Unknown Mean: Quadrature vs Laplace
text:
About the app
Shows how a fixed quadrature grid can miss the posterior mode entirely, so that the computed marginal likelihood is badly wrong. The app models a single unknown mean \(\mu\).
The problem. The data enter through a normal likelihood \(L(\mu)=N(\hat\mu\mid\mu,1/3)\), the likelihood of three observations with unit variance whose sample mean is the slider value \(\hat\mu\) (“data location”). The prior is \(\pi(\mu)=N(0,5^2)\). The marginal likelihood is \[P(y)=\int_{-\infty}^{\infty} z(\mu)\,d\mu,\qquad z(\mu)=\pi(\mu)L(\mu).\] To integrate over the whole real line with a fixed grid, the app maps \(\mu\) to the unit interval by \(u=1/(1+e^{-\mu})\), so \(\mu=\text{logit}(u)\), and applies the midpoint rule with \(n\) equally spaced points \(u_i=(i-0.5)/n\) on \((0,1)\): \[P(y)=\int_0^1 \frac{z(\text{logit}\,u)}{u(1-u)}\,du\;\approx\;\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n \frac{z(\text{logit}\,u_i)}{u_i(1-u_i)}.\] The grid is fixed in advance, without looking at where the posterior mass is.
The Laplace-normalized grid. The second rule uses the same midpoint points \(u_i=(i-0.5)/n\) but a different map between \(u\) and \(\mu\), centred and scaled by the Laplace approximation of the posterior, \(\hat\mu_L\) (the mode of \(z\)) and \(s_L=\big(-\partial^2\log z(\hat\mu_L)\big)^{-1/2}\), recomputed for the current \(\hat\mu\): \(u=\Phi\big((\mu-\hat\mu_L)/s_L\big)\), so \(\mu_i=\hat\mu_L+s_L\,\Phi^{-1}(u_i)\) and \(du/d\mu=\varphi\big((\mu-\hat\mu_L)/s_L\big)/s_L\), where \(\varphi\) is the standard normal density. Changing variables gives \[P(y)=\int_0^1 \frac{z(\mu(u))}{\varphi\big((\mu(u)-\hat\mu_L)/s_L\big)/s_L}\,du\;\approx\;\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n \frac{s_L\,z(\mu_i)}{\varphi\big(\Phi^{-1}(u_i)\big)}.\] Each term is the posterior kernel at the grid point divided by the Laplace (normal) density at that point, i.e. an importance-sampling-style ratio. Because \(z\) is close to \(\varphi\)-shaped around \(\hat\mu_L\), this ratio is nearly constant in \(u\) and the rule is accurate with few points. With the logistic map the same formula holds with \(du/d\mu=u(1-u)\) in place of the normal density.
What the plots show. Two grids are compared on the same data, one per row; the sliders are shared. In each row the left plot shows \(z(\mu)\) and the grid in \(\mu\), and the right plot shows the function the rule actually integrates over \(u\), with the midpoint rectangles.

Top row, logistic grid. \(\mu=\text{logit}(u)\), fixed in advance whatever the data. Left: \(z(\mu)\) (red), the map \(u=1/(1+e^{-\mu})\) (blue), and the grid points \(u_i\) with the \(\mu_i=\text{logit}(u_i)\) they correspond to. Equally spaced \(u_i\) are densely packed near \(\mu=0\) and spread very thinly far from it. Right: \(g(u)=z(\text{logit}\,u)/\{u(1-u)\}\); the gray rectangles are the midpoint rule, and their total area is the estimate.
Bottom row, Laplace-normalized grid. The transform is centred and scaled by the Laplace approximation recomputed for the current \(\hat\mu\): \(u=\Phi\big((\mu-\hat\mu_L)/s_L\big)\), where \(\hat\mu_L\) is the posterior mode and \(s_L\) the inverse square root of the curvature there. The midpoint grid in \(u\) is therefore uniform in Laplace-normalized space, so it concentrates where the posterior mass lives. Right: \(g(u)=z(\mu(u))\big/\,\phi\big((\mu(u)-\hat\mu_L)/s_L\big)\big/s_L\), which is nearly flat, so a few rectangles already give the right area.

What to try. At \(\hat\mu=0\) both grids work: the posterior mass sits under the logistic grid, and the two estimates agree with the true value. As \(\hat\mu\) moves to 8 or 20, the logistic grid fails: the mass is squeezed into a tiny interval of \(u\) near 1 that falls between grid points, so the rule sees essentially nothing and the estimate is wrong by many orders of magnitude, however many points you add. The Laplace-normalized grid follows the posterior wherever it sits, and its estimate stays close to the true value. The lesson is that a fixed grid that ignores the location of the mode can miss it, and that centring and scaling the grid with the Laplace approximation fixes this.

sigma_true <- 2                                       # true sd of the simulated data

### Gauss-Hermite nodes z_j and weights w_j for the weight function exp(-z^2/2) (Golub-Welsch)
gauss_hermite <- function(k) {
    J <- matrix(0, k, k)
    for (i in seq_len(k - 1)) J[i, i + 1] <- J[i + 1, i] <- sqrt(i)
    e <- eigen(J, symmetric = TRUE)
    list(z = e$values, w = sqrt(2 * pi) * e$vectors[1, ]^2)
}

server <- function(input, output, session) {

    ### simulated normal data: y_i ~ N(mu_true, sigma_true^2); only the sufficient statistics are needed
    dat <- reactive({
        set.seed(input$new + 1)
        x <- input$mu_true + sigma_true * rnorm(input$n_obs)
        list(n = length(x), S1 = sum(x), S2 = sum(x^2), xbar = mean(x), sd = sd(x))
    })

    ### log L(mu, w) + log pi(mu, w) at the points (mu[i], w[i]), and on the outer product of mu and w
    log_post_pt <- function(mu, w, d, sig_mu, sig_w) {
        SS <- d$S2 - 2 * mu * d$S1 + d$n * mu^2
        -0.5 * d$n * log(2 * pi) - d$n * w - 0.5 * exp(-2 * w) * SS +
            dnorm(mu, mu_0, sig_mu, log = TRUE) + dnorm(w, w_0, sig_w, log = TRUE)
    }
    log_post <- function(mu, w, d, sig_mu, sig_w) {
        SS <- d$S2 - 2 * mu * d$S1 + d$n * mu^2
        outer(SS, w, function(ss, w) -0.5 * d$n * log(2 * pi) - d$n * w - 0.5 * exp(-2 * w) * ss) +
            outer(dnorm(mu, mu_0, sig_mu, log = TRUE), dnorm(w, w_0, sig_w, log = TRUE), "+")
    }

    st <- reactive({
        d <- dat(); sig_mu <- input$sig_mu; sig_w <- input$sig_w

        ### Laplace approximation: posterior mode and curvature
        fit  <- nlm(function(th) -log_post_pt(th[1], th[2], d, sig_mu, sig_w),
                    c(d$xbar, log(d$sd)), hessian = TRUE)
        mode <- fit$estimate
        H    <- fit$hessian
        Lc   <- t(chol(solve(H)))                              # covariance = Lc Lc'
        se   <- sqrt(diag(solve(H)))
        log_lap <- -fit$minimum + log(2 * pi) - 0.5 * as.numeric(determinant(H)$modulus)

        ### reference value: a fine grid centred on the posterior mode
        mu_f <- mode[1] + seq(-8, 8, length.out = 400) * se[1]
        w_f  <- mode[2] + seq(-8, 8, length.out = 400) * se[2]
        log_true <- log_sum_exp(as.vector(log_post(mu_f, w_f, d, sig_mu, sig_w))) +
            log(diff(mu_f[1:2])) + log(diff(w_f[1:2]))

        ### product midpoint rule on the unit square, u = logistic(mu), v = logistic(w)
        n <- input$n_grid; h <- 1 / n; grid <- (seq_len(n) - 0.5) * h
        log_jac <- function(u) -log(u) - log(1 - u)            # log |d mu / d u|
        G <- log_post(qlogis(grid), qlogis(grid), d, sig_mu, sig_w) + outer(log_jac(grid), log_jac(grid), "+")
        log_mid <- log_sum_exp(as.vector(G)) + 2 * log(h)
        wn <- exp(G - max(G)); wn <- wn / sum(wn)

        ### Gauss-Hermite rule centred and scaled by the Laplace approximation: theta = mode + Lc z
        gh <- gauss_hermite(input$n_gh)
        Z  <- as.matrix(expand.grid(z1 = gh$z, z2 = gh$z))
        Wt <- as.vector(outer(gh$w, gh$w))
        Th <- t(mode + Lc %*% t(Z))                            # nodes in the (mu, w) scale
        lf <- log_post_pt(Th[, 1], Th[, 2], d, sig_mu, sig_w) + 0.5 * rowSums(Z^2) + log(Wt) +
            sum(log(diag(Lc)))
        log_gh <- log_sum_exp(lf)

        list(d = d, sig_mu = sig_mu, sig_w = sig_w, mode = mode, se = se, Lc = Lc,
             log_true = log_true, log_lap = log_lap,
             n = n, h = h, grid = grid, log_jac = log_jac, log_mid = log_mid, ess = 1 / sum(wn^2),
             k = input$n_gh, Z = Z, Th = Th, log_gh = log_gh)
    })

    heat_cols <- hcl.colors(40, "YlOrRd", rev = TRUE)

    ### a heatmap of L(mu, w) pi(mu, w) on its natural scale, with a set of points drawn on top
    draw_nat <- function(s, pts, ptlab) {
        if (input$zoom) {
            xr <- s$mode[1] + c(-6, 6) * s$se[1]; yr <- s$mode[2] + c(-6, 6) * s$se[2]
        } else {
            xr <- c(-10, 10); yr <- c(-5, 5)
        }
        mu_g <- seq(xr[1], xr[2], length.out = 300); w_g <- seq(yr[1], yr[2], length.out = 300)
        lp <- log_post(mu_g, w_g, s$d, s$sig_mu, s$sig_w)
        f  <- exp(lp - max(lp))
        par(mar = c(4, 4, 3, 1))
        image(mu_g, w_g, f, col = heat_cols, xlab = expression(mu), ylab = expression(w == log~sigma),
              main = expression(L(mu, w)~pi(mu, w)~"(natural scale)"))
        if (max(f) > 0) contour(mu_g, w_g, f, nlevels = 6, drawlabels = FALSE, add = TRUE, col = "gray30")
        points(pts, pch = 19, cex = 0.4, col = adjustcolor("black", 0.55))
        points(s$mode[1], s$mode[2], pch = 3, lwd = 2, col = "steelblue", cex = 1.3)
        legend("topright", bty = "n", pch = c(19, 3), col = c("gray30", "steelblue"),
               legend = c(ptlab, "posterior mode"), cex = 0.85)
    }

    ### row 1, left: the midpoint grid mapped back to (mu, w)
    output$nat <- renderPlot({
        s <- st()
        draw_nat(s, expand.grid(mu = qlogis(s$grid), w = qlogis(s$grid)), "midpoint grid, mapped back")
    })

    ### row 1, right: the transformed integrand g(u, v) on the unit square, with the midpoint grid
    output$unit <- renderPlot({
        s <- st()
        m <- 200; ug <- (seq_len(m) - 0.5) / m
        G <- log_post(qlogis(ug), qlogis(ug), s$d, s$sig_mu, s$sig_w) +
            outer(s$log_jac(ug), s$log_jac(ug), "+")
        par(mar = c(4, 4, 3, 1))
        image(ug, ug, exp(G - max(G)), col = heat_cols, xlab = "u", ylab = "v",
              main = expression(g(u, v) == L~pi~"/"~"{"*u(1-u)*v(1-v)*"}"~"(unit square)"))
        contour(ug, ug, exp(G - max(G)), nlevels = 6, drawlabels = FALSE, add = TRUE, col = "gray30")
        if (s$n <= 40) abline(v = seq(0, 1, by = s$h), h = seq(0, 1, by = s$h), col = adjustcolor("gray30", 0.35))
        points(expand.grid(s$grid, s$grid), pch = 19, cex = 0.35, col = adjustcolor("black", 0.5))
    })

    ### row 2, left: the Gauss-Hermite nodes mapped to (mu, w)
    output$nat_gh <- renderPlot({
        s <- st()
        draw_nat(s, data.frame(mu = s$Th[, 1], w = s$Th[, 2]), "Gauss-Hermite nodes")
    })

    ### row 2, right: the posterior in the Laplace-standardized coordinates z, where theta = mode + Lc z;
    ### dashed circles are the contours of the standard normal that the Gauss-Hermite weight assumes
    output$z_gh <- renderPlot({
        s <- st()
        zg <- seq(-4.5, 4.5, length.out = 200)
        Zg <- as.matrix(expand.grid(zg, zg))
        Tg <- t(s$mode + s$Lc %*% t(Zg))
        lp <- matrix(log_post_pt(Tg[, 1], Tg[, 2], s$d, s$sig_mu, s$sig_w), 200, 200)
        par(mar = c(4, 4, 3, 1))
        image(zg, zg, exp(lp - max(lp)), col = heat_cols, xlab = expression(z[1]), ylab = expression(z[2]),
              main = expression(L~pi~"in Laplace-standardized coordinates z"))
        contour(zg, zg, outer(zg, zg, function(a, b) exp(-0.5 * (a^2 + b^2))), levels = exp(-0.5 * c(1, 4, 9)),
                drawlabels = FALSE, add = TRUE, col = "steelblue", lty = 2, lwd = 1.5)
        points(s$Z, pch = 19, cex = 0.5, col = adjustcolor("black", 0.6))
    })

    output$tab <- renderTable({
        s <- st()
        est <- c(s$log_true, s$log_lap, s$log_mid, s$log_gh)
        data.frame(
            Method = c("Reference", "Laplace", sprintf("Midpoint %dx%d", s$n, s$n),
                       sprintf("Gauss-Hermite %dx%d", s$k, s$k)),
            Evals = c(400^2, 1, s$n^2, s$k^2),
            `log P(y)` = sprintf("%.3f", est),
            Error = c("", sprintf("%.3f", est[-1] - est[1])),
            `Eff. pts` = c("", "", sprintf("%.1f", s$ess), ""),
            check.names = FALSE)
    }, striped = TRUE, align = "lrrrr")
}

shinyApp(ui, server)

title: Marginal Likelihood of Normal Data: Midpoint, Laplace and Gauss–Hermite
text:
About the app
Shows how the product midpoint rule of the Numerical Quadrature unit computes the marginal likelihood of normal data when both the mean \(\mu\) and the standard deviation are unknown, how it fails when the posterior is far from where the grid looks, and how a Gauss–Hermite rule centred and scaled by the Laplace approximation avoids the failure.
The problem. Data \(y_1,\ldots,y_n\mid\mu,\sigma\overset{iid}{\sim}N(\mu,\sigma^2)\) are simulated with the “data location” as the true mean and \(\sigma=2\). With \(w=\log\sigma\), the priors are independent, \(\mu\sim N(0,\sigma_\mu^2)\) and \(w\sim N(0,\sigma_w^2)\), and the marginal likelihood is the two-dimensional integral \[P(y)=\iint L(\mu,w)\,\pi(\mu,w)\,d\mu\,dw .\]
Rule 1: product midpoint rule on a logistic grid. Mapping each parameter to \((0,1)\) by \(u=1/(1+e^{-\mu})\), \(v=1/(1+e^{-w})\) gives \(P(y)=\int_0^1\!\int_0^1 g(u,v)\,du\,dv\) with \(g(u,v)=L\pi\big/\{u(1-u)v(1-v)\}\), and the midpoint rule is \(P(y)\approx h^2\sum_{j,k}g(u_j,v_k)\) with \(u_j=(j-\tfrac12)h\), \(v_k=(k-\tfrac12)h\), \(h=1/n\). The grid is fixed in advance and does not look at where the posterior is.
Rule 2: Laplace approximation. Let \(\hat\theta=(\hat\mu,\hat w)\) be the posterior mode and \(H\) the Hessian of \(-\log(L\pi)\) there. Approximating the log of the integrand by a quadratic gives \[\log P(y)\approx\log\{L\pi\}(\hat\theta)+\log 2\pi-\tfrac12\log\det H,\] one function evaluation after the optimization.
Rule 3: Gauss–Hermite rule centred and scaled by the Laplace approximation. Write the covariance of the Laplace approximation as \(\Sigma=H^{-1}=CC^\top\) and change variables to \(\theta=\hat\theta+Cz\), so that \(z\sim N(0,I)\) under the approximation. With \(\phi_2\) the standard bivariate normal density, \[P(y)=|\det C|\iint \frac{(L\pi)(\hat\theta+Cz)}{\phi_2(z)}\,\phi_2(z)\,dz\;\approx\;|\det C|\sum_{j=1}^k\sum_{l=1}^k \omega_j\,\omega_l\,e^{(z_j^2+z_l^2)/2}\,(L\pi)(\hat\theta+C z_{jl}),\] where \(z_j\) and \(\omega_j\) are the nodes and weights of the \(k\)-point Gauss–Hermite rule for the weight \(e^{-z^2/2}\) and \(z_{jl}=(z_j,z_l)\). Each term is the posterior kernel divided by its Laplace normal density, a ratio that is nearly constant when the posterior is close to normal, so a handful of nodes per axis is enough. The Cholesky factor \(C\) also takes care of the correlation between \(\mu\) and \(w\).
The four plots. Each is a contour heatmap of the same posterior kernel in a different coordinate system, with the points of a rule drawn on top.

Row 1, left: \(L\pi\) on its natural scale with the logistic midpoint grid mapped back to \((\mu,w)\). The grid points crowd around \((0,0)\) and thin out quickly away from it. The cross is the posterior mode. Tick “zoom to the posterior” (it applies to both left plots) to see the shape of the posterior itself.
Row 1, right: the transformed integrand \(g(u,v)\) on the unit square with the \(n\times n\) midpoint grid (the lines are drawn for up to 40 points per axis).
Row 2, left: the same natural-scale surface with the Gauss–Hermite nodes \(\hat\theta+Cz_{jl}\), which sit on and around the posterior wherever it is.
Row 2, right: the posterior in the standardized coordinates \(z\), with the Gauss–Hermite nodes and dashed circles at 1, 2 and 3 standard deviations of the standard normal that the rule assumes. The closer the posterior is to the circles, the better the rule works.

The table (to the right of the plots) lists the value of \(\log P(y)\) from each method (Reference: a fine product grid centred on the posterior mode; Laplace; Midpoint \(n\times n\); Gauss–Hermite \(k\times k\)), the number of function evaluations (Evals), the error against the reference, and, for the midpoint rule, the effective number of grid points (Eff. pts) \(1/\sum_i\tilde g_i^2\) (\(\tilde g_i\) the normalized values of \(g\) at the grid points), a measure of how many points carry the mass.
What to try. With the data location near 0 and a vague prior, all the rules are close to the reference. Move the data location to \(-5\) and then \(-10\): the posterior moves out into the tail of the logistic grid, \(g\) becomes a thin spike near the boundary of the square, the effective number of grid points collapses, and the midpoint error becomes large however many points per axis you add (a larger sample makes the posterior narrower and the failure worse). The Laplace-centred Gauss–Hermite rule is unaffected by the location of the data and is accurate with 5 to 10 nodes per axis. The Laplace approximation alone is already close for normal data with a moderate \(n\), and the Gauss–Hermite rule improves on it as the number of nodes grows. Reduce the number of observations to see the posterior depart from normality and the Laplace error grow.

library(shiny)

### renderPlot replacement: Safari 27 (WebKit) cannot hold the call stack of
### shiny::renderPlot in webR ("Maximum call stack size exceeded"), so draw with
### renderImage instead, which nests about 45 fewer R calls
renderPlot <- function(expr, width = "auto", height = "auto", res = 72, ...,
                       env = parent.frame(), quoted = FALSE) {
    func <- shiny::exprToFunction(expr, env, quoted)
    shiny::renderImage({
        info <- shiny::getCurrentOutputInfo()
        w  <- if (is.numeric(width))  width  else info$width()
        h  <- if (is.numeric(height)) height else info$height()
        shiny::req(w > 0, h > 0)
        pr <- shiny::getDefaultReactiveDomain()$clientData$pixelratio
        if (is.null(pr)) pr <- 1
        f   <- tempfile(fileext = ".png")
        dev <- shiny:::startPNG(f, w * pr, h * pr, res = res * pr)
        on.exit(grDevices::dev.off(dev), add = TRUE)
        grDevices::dev.control(displaylist = "enable")
        v <- withVisible(func())
        if (v$visible) print(v$value)
        list(src = f, contentType = "image/png", width = w, height = h,
             coordmap = shiny:::getCoordmap(v$value, w * pr, h * pr, res * pr))
    }, deleteFile = TRUE)
}

log_sum_exp <- function(lx) { m <- max(lx); m + log(sum(exp(lx - m))) }

mu_0 <- 0; w_0 <- 0                                   # prior means for mu and w = log(sigma)
sigma_true <- 2                                       # true sd of the simulated data

### Gauss-Hermite nodes z_j and weights w_j for the weight function exp(-z^2/2) (Golub-Welsch)
gauss_hermite <- function(k) {
    J <- matrix(0, k, k)
    for (i in seq_len(k - 1)) J[i, i + 1] <- J[i + 1, i] <- sqrt(i)
    e <- eigen(J, symmetric = TRUE)
    list(z = e$values, w = sqrt(2 * pi) * e$vectors[1, ]^2)
}
