server <- function(input, output, session) {

    ### simulated normal data: y_i ~ N(mu_true, sigma_true^2); only the sufficient statistics are needed
    dat <- reactive({
        set.seed(input$new + 1)
        x <- input$mu_true + sigma_true * rnorm(input$n_obs)
        list(n = length(x), S1 = sum(x), S2 = sum(x^2), xbar = mean(x), sd = sd(x))
    })

    ### log L(mu, w) + log pi(mu, w) at the points (mu[i], w[i]), and on the outer product of mu and w
    log_post_pt <- function(mu, w, d, sig_mu, sig_w) {
        SS <- d$S2 - 2 * mu * d$S1 + d$n * mu^2
        -0.5 * d$n * log(2 * pi) - d$n * w - 0.5 * exp(-2 * w) * SS +
            dnorm(mu, mu_0, sig_mu, log = TRUE) + dnorm(w, w_0, sig_w, log = TRUE)
    }
    log_post <- function(mu, w, d, sig_mu, sig_w) {
        SS <- d$S2 - 2 * mu * d$S1 + d$n * mu^2
        outer(SS, w, function(ss, w) -0.5 * d$n * log(2 * pi) - d$n * w - 0.5 * exp(-2 * w) * ss) +
            outer(dnorm(mu, mu_0, sig_mu, log = TRUE), dnorm(w, w_0, sig_w, log = TRUE), "+")
    }

    st <- reactive({
        d <- dat(); sig_mu <- input$sig_mu; sig_w <- input$sig_w

        ### Laplace approximation: posterior mode and curvature
        fit  <- nlm(function(th) -log_post_pt(th[1], th[2], d, sig_mu, sig_w),
                    c(d$xbar, log(d$sd)), hessian = TRUE)
        mode <- fit$estimate
        H    <- fit$hessian
        Lc   <- t(chol(solve(H)))                              # covariance = Lc Lc'
        se   <- sqrt(diag(solve(H)))
        log_lap <- -fit$minimum + log(2 * pi) - 0.5 * as.numeric(determinant(H)$modulus)

        ### reference value: a fine grid centred on the posterior mode
        mu_f <- mode[1] + seq(-8, 8, length.out = 400) * se[1]
        w_f  <- mode[2] + seq(-8, 8, length.out = 400) * se[2]
        log_true <- log_sum_exp(as.vector(log_post(mu_f, w_f, d, sig_mu, sig_w))) +
            log(diff(mu_f[1:2])) + log(diff(w_f[1:2]))

        ### product midpoint rule on the unit square, u = logistic(mu), v = logistic(w)
        n <- input$n_grid; h <- 1 / n; grid <- (seq_len(n) - 0.5) * h
        log_jac <- function(u) -log(u) - log(1 - u)            # log |d mu / d u|
        G <- log_post(qlogis(grid), qlogis(grid), d, sig_mu, sig_w) + outer(log_jac(grid), log_jac(grid), "+")
        log_mid <- log_sum_exp(as.vector(G)) + 2 * log(h)
        wn <- exp(G - max(G)); wn <- wn / sum(wn)

        ### Gauss-Hermite rule centred and scaled by the Laplace approximation: theta = mode + Lc z
        gh <- gauss_hermite(input$n_gh)
        Z  <- as.matrix(expand.grid(z1 = gh$z, z2 = gh$z))
        Wt <- as.vector(outer(gh$w, gh$w))
        Th <- t(mode + Lc %*% t(Z))                            # nodes in the (mu, w) scale
        lf <- log_post_pt(Th[, 1], Th[, 2], d, sig_mu, sig_w) + 0.5 * rowSums(Z^2) + log(Wt) +
            sum(log(diag(Lc)))
        log_gh <- log_sum_exp(lf)

        list(d = d, sig_mu = sig_mu, sig_w = sig_w, mode = mode, se = se, Lc = Lc,
             log_true = log_true, log_lap = log_lap,
             n = n, h = h, grid = grid, log_jac = log_jac, log_mid = log_mid, ess = 1 / sum(wn^2),
             k = input$n_gh, Z = Z, Th = Th, log_gh = log_gh)
    })

    heat_cols <- hcl.colors(40, "YlOrRd", rev = TRUE)

    ### a heatmap of L(mu, w) pi(mu, w) on its natural scale, with a set of points drawn on top
    draw_nat <- function(s, pts, ptlab) {
        if (input$zoom) {
            xr <- s$mode[1] + c(-6, 6) * s$se[1]; yr <- s$mode[2] + c(-6, 6) * s$se[2]
        } else {
            xr <- c(-10, 10); yr <- c(-5, 5)
        }
        mu_g <- seq(xr[1], xr[2], length.out = 300); w_g <- seq(yr[1], yr[2], length.out = 300)
        lp <- log_post(mu_g, w_g, s$d, s$sig_mu, s$sig_w)
        f  <- exp(lp - max(lp))
        par(mar = c(4, 4, 3, 1))
        image(mu_g, w_g, f, col = heat_cols, xlab = expression(mu), ylab = expression(w == log~sigma),
              main = expression(L(mu, w)~pi(mu, w)~"(natural scale)"))
        if (max(f) > 0) contour(mu_g, w_g, f, nlevels = 6, drawlabels = FALSE, add = TRUE, col = "gray30")
        points(pts, pch = 19, cex = 0.4, col = adjustcolor("black", 0.55))
        points(s$mode[1], s$mode[2], pch = 3, lwd = 2, col = "steelblue", cex = 1.3)
        legend("topright", bty = "n", pch = c(19, 3), col = c("gray30", "steelblue"),
               legend = c(ptlab, "posterior mode"), cex = 0.85)
    }

    ### row 1, left: the midpoint grid mapped back to (mu, w)
    output$nat <- renderPlot({
        s <- st()
        draw_nat(s, expand.grid(mu = qlogis(s$grid), w = qlogis(s$grid)), "midpoint grid, mapped back")
    })

    ### row 1, right: the transformed integrand g(u, v) on the unit square, with the midpoint grid
    output$unit <- renderPlot({
        s <- st()
        m <- 200; ug <- (seq_len(m) - 0.5) / m
        G <- log_post(qlogis(ug), qlogis(ug), s$d, s$sig_mu, s$sig_w) +
            outer(s$log_jac(ug), s$log_jac(ug), "+")
        par(mar = c(4, 4, 3, 1))
        image(ug, ug, exp(G - max(G)), col = heat_cols, xlab = "u", ylab = "v",
              main = expression(g(u, v) == L~pi~"/"~"{"*u(1-u)*v(1-v)*"}"~"(unit square)"))
        contour(ug, ug, exp(G - max(G)), nlevels = 6, drawlabels = FALSE, add = TRUE, col = "gray30")
        if (s$n <= 40) abline(v = seq(0, 1, by = s$h), h = seq(0, 1, by = s$h), col = adjustcolor("gray30", 0.35))
        points(expand.grid(s$grid, s$grid), pch = 19, cex = 0.35, col = adjustcolor("black", 0.5))
    })

    ### row 2, left: the Gauss-Hermite nodes mapped to (mu, w)
    output$nat_gh <- renderPlot({
        s <- st()
        draw_nat(s, data.frame(mu = s$Th[, 1], w = s$Th[, 2]), "Gauss-Hermite nodes")
    })

    ### row 2, right: the posterior in the Laplace-standardized coordinates z, where theta = mode + Lc z;
    ### dashed circles are the contours of the standard normal that the Gauss-Hermite weight assumes
    output$z_gh <- renderPlot({
        s <- st()
        zg <- seq(-4.5, 4.5, length.out = 200)
        Zg <- as.matrix(expand.grid(zg, zg))
        Tg <- t(s$mode + s$Lc %*% t(Zg))
        lp <- matrix(log_post_pt(Tg[, 1], Tg[, 2], s$d, s$sig_mu, s$sig_w), 200, 200)
        par(mar = c(4, 4, 3, 1))
        image(zg, zg, exp(lp - max(lp)), col = heat_cols, xlab = expression(z[1]), ylab = expression(z[2]),
              main = expression(L~pi~"in Laplace-standardized coordinates z"))
        contour(zg, zg, outer(zg, zg, function(a, b) exp(-0.5 * (a^2 + b^2))), levels = exp(-0.5 * c(1, 4, 9)),
                drawlabels = FALSE, add = TRUE, col = "steelblue", lty = 2, lwd = 1.5)
        points(s$Z, pch = 19, cex = 0.5, col = adjustcolor("black", 0.6))
    })

    output$tab <- renderTable({
        s <- st()
        est <- c(s$log_true, s$log_lap, s$log_mid, s$log_gh)
        data.frame(
            Method = c("Reference", "Laplace", sprintf("Midpoint %dx%d", s$n, s$n),
                       sprintf("Gauss-Hermite %dx%d", s$k, s$k)),
            Evals = c(400^2, 1, s$n^2, s$k^2),
            `log P(y)` = sprintf("%.3f", est),
            Error = c("", sprintf("%.3f", est[-1] - est[1])),
            `Eff. pts` = c("", "", sprintf("%.1f", s$ess), ""),
            check.names = FALSE)
    }, striped = TRUE, align = "lrrrr")
}

server <- function(input, output, session) {

  ## the raw data implied by the MLE slider and n
  output$data_bb <- renderText({
    y <- round(input$mle_bb * input$n_bb)
    sprintf("Data: y = %d successes in n = %d trials (y/n = %.3f)", y, input$n_bb, y / input$n_bb)
  })
  output$prior_pg <- renderText({
    alpha <- 1 / input$disp_pg
    sprintf("Prior: Gamma(alpha = %.2f, beta = %.2f)", alpha, alpha / input$mean_pg)
  })
  output$data_pg <- renderText({
    S <- round(input$mle_pg * input$n_pg)
    sprintf("Data: sum of counts S = %d over n = %d observations (S/n = %.3f)", S, input$n_pg, S / input$n_pg)
  })
  output$data_nn <- renderText(
    sprintf("Data: sum of y_i = %.1f over n = %d observations (y-bar = %.3f)",
            input$n_nn * input$ybar_nn, input$n_nn, input$ybar_nn)
  )

  output$densplot <- renderPlot({
    par(mar = c(4, 4, 2, 4.5))
    ## likelihood (relative to its maximum) on a second y-axis, drawn on the density scale
    addlik <- function(loglik, from, to, ylim, col) {
      xs <- seq(from, to, length.out = 500)
      ll <- loglik(xs)
      L <- exp(ll - max(ll))
      k <- 0.85 * ylim[2] / 1.1          # right axis: likelihood 1 sits a little below the density peak
      lines(xs, L * k, lwd = 2, col = col, lty = 4)
      axis(4, at = c(0, 0.5, 1) * k, labels = c(0, 0.5, 1), col = col,
           col.axis = col, las = 1)
      mtext("likelihood (relative to its maximum)", side = 4, line = 3, col = col)
    }
    if (input$model == "bb") {
      a1 <- input$a1; a0 <- input$a0; n <- input$n_bb; y <- round(input$mle_bb * input$n_bb)
      post_a1 <- a1 + y; post_a0 <- a0 + (n - y)
      xs <- seq(0, 1, length.out = 500)
      dpost <- dbeta(xs, post_a1, post_a0)       # y-limit from the posterior only: the prior may be unbounded (alpha < 1)
      ylim <- c(0, max(dpost[is.finite(dpost)]) * 1.1)
      curve(dbeta(x, a1, a0), 0, 1, lwd = 2, lty = 2, col = "gray40",
            xlab = expression(theta), ylab = "density", ylim = ylim)
      curve(dbeta(x, post_a1, post_a0), add = TRUE, lwd = 3, col = "steelblue")
      addlik(function(x) dbinom(y, n, x, log = TRUE), 0, 1, ylim, "forestgreen")
      abline(v = y / n, lty = 3)
      abline(v = post_a1 / (post_a1 + post_a0), lty = 1, lwd = 1.5, col = "steelblue")
      legend("topright", bty = "n", lwd = c(2, 3, 2, 1.5), lty = c(2, 1, 4, 1),
             col = c("gray40", "steelblue", "forestgreen", "steelblue"),
             legend = c("prior", "posterior", "likelihood (right axis)", "posterior mean"))
    } else if (input$model == "pg") {
      alpha <- 1 / input$disp_pg; beta <- alpha / input$mean_pg; n <- input$n_pg; S <- round(input$mle_pg * input$n_pg)
      post_alpha <- alpha + S; post_beta <- beta + n
      hi <- 18                                  # fixed x-axis: a little beyond the largest MLE the slider allows (15)
      xs <- seq(0, hi, length.out = 500)
      dpost <- dgamma(xs, post_alpha, post_beta)  # y-limit from the posterior only: the prior may be unbounded (alpha < 1)
      ylim <- c(0, max(dpost[is.finite(dpost)]) * 1.1)
      curve(dgamma(x, alpha, beta), 0, hi, lwd = 2, lty = 2, col = "gray40",
            xlab = expression(lambda), ylab = "density", ylim = ylim)
      curve(dgamma(x, post_alpha, post_beta), add = TRUE, lwd = 3, col = "firebrick")
      addlik(function(x) dpois(S, n * x, log = TRUE), 0, hi, ylim, "forestgreen")
      abline(v = S / n, lty = 3)
      abline(v = post_alpha / post_beta, lty = 1, lwd = 1.5, col = "firebrick")
      legend("topright", bty = "n", lwd = c(2, 3, 2, 1.5), lty = c(2, 1, 4, 1),
             col = c("gray40", "firebrick", "forestgreen", "firebrick"),
             legend = c("prior", "posterior", "likelihood (right axis)", "posterior mean"))
    } else {
      mu0 <- input$mu0; kappa0 <- input$kappa0; sigma <- input$sigma_nn
      n <- input$n_nn; ybar <- input$ybar_nn
      post_kappa <- kappa0 + n
      post_mu <- (kappa0 * mu0 + n * ybar) / post_kappa
      post_sd <- sigma / sqrt(post_kappa)
      prior_sd <- sigma / sqrt(kappa0)
      lo <- -6; hi <- 6                          # fixed x-axis: a little beyond the y-bar slider range (-5 to 5)
      xs <- seq(lo, hi, length.out = 500)
      ylim <- c(0, max(dnorm(xs, mu0, prior_sd), dnorm(xs, post_mu, post_sd)) * 1.1)
      curve(dnorm(x, mu0, prior_sd), lo, hi, lwd = 2, lty = 2, col = "gray40",
            xlab = expression(mu), ylab = "density", ylim = ylim)
      curve(dnorm(x, post_mu, post_sd), add = TRUE, lwd = 3, col = "darkorchid")
      addlik(function(x) dnorm(ybar, x, sigma / sqrt(n), log = TRUE), lo, hi, ylim, "forestgreen")
      abline(v = ybar, lty = 3)
      abline(v = post_mu, lty = 1, lwd = 1.5, col = "darkorchid")
      legend("topright", bty = "n", lwd = c(2, 3, 2, 1.5), lty = c(2, 1, 4, 1),
             col = c("gray40", "darkorchid", "forestgreen", "darkorchid"),
             legend = c("prior", "posterior", "likelihood (right axis)", "posterior mean"))
    }
  })

  ## MLE vs Bayesian: estimate, standard error, 95% interval
  output$cmptab <- renderTable({
    if (input$model == "bb") {
      a1 <- input$a1; a0 <- input$a0; n <- input$n_bb; y <- round(input$mle_bb * input$n_bb)
      post_a1 <- a1 + y; post_a0 <- a0 + (n - y)
      p <- y / n; se <- sqrt(p * (1 - p) / n)
      ci <- pmin(pmax(p + c(-1, 1) * qnorm(0.975) * se, 0), 1)
      pm <- post_a1 / (post_a1 + post_a0)
      psd <- sqrt(post_a1 * post_a0 / ((post_a1 + post_a0)^2 * (post_a1 + post_a0 + 1)))
      pci <- qbeta(c(0.025, 0.975), post_a1, post_a0)
    } else if (input$model == "pg") {
      alpha <- 1 / input$disp_pg; beta <- alpha / input$mean_pg; n <- input$n_pg; S <- round(input$mle_pg * input$n_pg)
      post_alpha <- alpha + S; post_beta <- beta + n
      p <- S / n; se <- sqrt(p / n)
      ci <- pmax(p + c(-1, 1) * qnorm(0.975) * se, 0)
      pm <- post_alpha / post_beta
      psd <- sqrt(post_alpha) / post_beta
      pci <- qgamma(c(0.025, 0.975), post_alpha, post_beta)
    } else {
      mu0 <- input$mu0; kappa0 <- input$kappa0; sigma <- input$sigma_nn
      n <- input$n_nn; ybar <- input$ybar_nn
      post_kappa <- kappa0 + n
      p <- ybar; se <- sigma / sqrt(n)
      ci <- p + c(-1, 1) * qnorm(0.975) * se
      pm <- (kappa0 * mu0 + n * ybar) / post_kappa
      psd <- sigma / sqrt(post_kappa)
      pci <- qnorm(c(0.025, 0.975), pm, psd)
    }
    data.frame(
      Method = c("MLE (Wald interval)", "Bayesian (posterior)"),
      Estimate = sprintf("%.3f", c(p, pm)),
      SE = sprintf("%.3f", c(se, psd)),
      `95% interval` = c(sprintf("(%.3f, %.3f)", ci[1], ci[2]),
                         sprintf("(%.3f, %.3f)", pci[1], pci[2])),
      check.names = FALSE)
  }, striped = TRUE)

  output$summtab <- renderTable({
    if (input$model == "bb") {
      a1 <- input$a1; a0 <- input$a0; n <- input$n_bb; y <- round(input$mle_bb * input$n_bb)
      post_a1 <- a1 + y; post_a0 <- a0 + (n - y)
      logmarg    <- lbeta(post_a1, post_a0) - lbeta(a1, a0)         # exact
      pred_mean  <- post_a1 / (post_a1 + post_a0)
      pred_sd    <- sqrt(pred_mean * (1 - pred_mean))
      data.frame(
        quantity = c("prior mean", "log marginal likelihood*", "posterior distribution",
                     "predictive distribution", "predictive mean", "predictive sd"),
        value = c(sprintf("%.3f", a1 / (a1 + a0)),
                  sprintf("%.3f", logmarg),
                  sprintf("Beta(%.2f, %.2f)", post_a1, post_a0),
                  sprintf("Bernoulli(%.3f)", pred_mean),
                  sprintf("%.3f", pred_mean), sprintf("%.3f", pred_sd)))
    } else if (input$model == "pg") {
      alpha <- 1 / input$disp_pg; beta <- alpha / input$mean_pg; n <- input$n_pg; S <- round(input$mle_pg * input$n_pg)
      post_alpha <- alpha + S; post_beta <- beta + n
      logmarg   <- alpha * log(beta) - lgamma(alpha) + lgamma(post_alpha) -
        post_alpha * log(post_beta)                                 # up to -sum(log(y_i!))
      nb_prob   <- post_beta / (post_beta + 1)
      pred_mean <- post_alpha / post_beta
      pred_sd   <- sqrt(pred_mean * (1 + 1 / post_beta))
      data.frame(
        quantity = c("prior mean", "log marginal likelihood*", "posterior distribution",
                     "predictive distribution", "predictive mean", "predictive sd"),
        value = c(sprintf("%.3f", alpha / beta),
                  sprintf("%.3f", logmarg),
                  sprintf("Gamma(%.2f, %.2f)", post_alpha, post_beta),
                  sprintf("NegBin(%.2f, %.3f)", post_alpha, nb_prob),
                  sprintf("%.3f", pred_mean), sprintf("%.3f", pred_sd)))
    } else {
      mu0 <- input$mu0; kappa0 <- input$kappa0; sigma <- input$sigma_nn
      n <- input$n_nn; ybar <- input$ybar_nn
      post_kappa <- kappa0 + n
      post_mu <- (kappa0 * mu0 + n * ybar) / post_kappa
      post_sd <- sigma / sqrt(post_kappa)
      logmarg <- -n / 2 * log(2 * pi * sigma^2) + 0.5 * log(kappa0 / post_kappa) -
        kappa0 * n * (mu0 - ybar)^2 / (2 * sigma^2 * post_kappa)     # up to -SS/(2 sigma^2)
      pred_sd <- sqrt(post_sd^2 + sigma^2)
      data.frame(
        quantity = c("prior mean", "log marginal likelihood*", "posterior distribution",
                     "predictive distribution", "predictive mean", "predictive sd"),
        value = c(sprintf("%.3f", mu0),
                  sprintf("%.3f", logmarg),
                  sprintf("N(%.3f, %.3f^2)", post_mu, post_sd),
                  sprintf("N(%.3f, %.3f^2)", post_mu, pred_sd),
                  sprintf("%.3f", post_mu), sprintf("%.3f", pred_sd)))
    }
  }, colnames = FALSE, striped = TRUE)
}

      a1 <- input$a1; a0 <- input$a0; n <- input$n_bb; y <- round(input$mle_bb * input$n_bb)
      post_a1 <- a1 + y; post_a0 <- a0 + (n - y)
      xs <- seq(0, 1, length.out = 500)
      dpost <- dbeta(xs, post_a1, post_a0)       # y-limit from the posterior only: the prior may be unbounded (alpha < 1)
      ylim <- c(0, max(dpost[is.finite(dpost)]) * 1.1)
      curve(dbeta(x, a1, a0), 0, 1, lwd = 2, lty = 2, col = "gray40",
            xlab = expression(theta), ylab = "density", ylim = ylim)
      curve(dbeta(x, post_a1, post_a0), add = TRUE, lwd = 3, col = "steelblue")
      addlik(function(x) dbinom(y, n, x, log = TRUE), 0, 1, ylim, "forestgreen")
      abline(v = y / n, lty = 3)
      abline(v = post_a1 / (post_a1 + post_a0), lty = 1, lwd = 1.5, col = "steelblue")
      legend("topright", bty = "n", lwd = c(2, 3, 2, 1.5), lty = c(2, 1, 4, 1),
             col = c("gray40", "steelblue", "forestgreen", "steelblue"),
             legend = c("prior", "posterior", "likelihood (right axis)", "posterior mean"))
    } else if (input$model == "pg") {
      alpha <- 1 / input$disp_pg; beta <- alpha / input$mean_pg; n <- input$n_pg; S <- round(input$mle_pg * input$n_pg)
      post_alpha <- alpha + S; post_beta <- beta + n
      hi <- 18                                  # fixed x-axis: a little beyond the largest MLE the slider allows (15)
      xs <- seq(0, hi, length.out = 500)
      dpost <- dgamma(xs, post_alpha, post_beta)  # y-limit from the posterior only: the prior may be unbounded (alpha < 1)
      ylim <- c(0, max(dpost[is.finite(dpost)]) * 1.1)
      curve(dgamma(x, alpha, beta), 0, hi, lwd = 2, lty = 2, col = "gray40",
            xlab = expression(lambda), ylab = "density", ylim = ylim)
      curve(dgamma(x, post_alpha, post_beta), add = TRUE, lwd = 3, col = "firebrick")
      addlik(function(x) dpois(S, n * x, log = TRUE), 0, hi, ylim, "forestgreen")
      abline(v = S / n, lty = 3)
      abline(v = post_alpha / post_beta, lty = 1, lwd = 1.5, col = "firebrick")
      legend("topright", bty = "n", lwd = c(2, 3, 2, 1.5), lty = c(2, 1, 4, 1),
             col = c("gray40", "firebrick", "forestgreen", "firebrick"),
             legend = c("prior", "posterior", "likelihood (right axis)", "posterior mean"))
    } else {
      mu0 <- input$mu0; kappa0 <- input$kappa0; sigma <- input$sigma_nn
      n <- input$n_nn; ybar <- input$ybar_nn
      post_kappa <- kappa0 + n
      post_mu <- (kappa0 * mu0 + n * ybar) / post_kappa
      post_sd <- sigma / sqrt(post_kappa)
      prior_sd <- sigma / sqrt(kappa0)
      lo <- -6; hi <- 6                          # fixed x-axis: a little beyond the y-bar slider range (-5 to 5)
      xs <- seq(lo, hi, length.out = 500)
      ylim <- c(0, max(dnorm(xs, mu0, prior_sd), dnorm(xs, post_mu, post_sd)) * 1.1)
      curve(dnorm(x, mu0, prior_sd), lo, hi, lwd = 2, lty = 2, col = "gray40",
            xlab = expression(mu), ylab = "density", ylim = ylim)
      curve(dnorm(x, post_mu, post_sd), add = TRUE, lwd = 3, col = "darkorchid")
      addlik(function(x) dnorm(ybar, x, sigma / sqrt(n), log = TRUE), lo, hi, ylim, "forestgreen")
      abline(v = ybar, lty = 3)
      abline(v = post_mu, lty = 1, lwd = 1.5, col = "darkorchid")
      legend("topright", bty = "n", lwd = c(2, 3, 2, 1.5), lty = c(2, 1, 4, 1),
             col = c("gray40", "darkorchid", "forestgreen", "darkorchid"),
             legend = c("prior", "posterior", "likelihood (right axis)", "posterior mean"))
    }
  })

  ## MLE vs Bayesian: estimate, standard error, 95% interval
  output$cmptab <- renderTable({
    if (input$model == "bb") {
      a1 <- input$a1; a0 <- input$a0; n <- input$n_bb; y <- round(input$mle_bb * input$n_bb)
      post_a1 <- a1 + y; post_a0 <- a0 + (n - y)
      p <- y / n; se <- sqrt(p * (1 - p) / n)
      ci <- pmin(pmax(p + c(-1, 1) * qnorm(0.975) * se, 0), 1)
      pm <- post_a1 / (post_a1 + post_a0)
      psd <- sqrt(post_a1 * post_a0 / ((post_a1 + post_a0)^2 * (post_a1 + post_a0 + 1)))
      pci <- qbeta(c(0.025, 0.975), post_a1, post_a0)
    } else if (input$model == "pg") {
      alpha <- 1 / input$disp_pg; beta <- alpha / input$mean_pg; n <- input$n_pg; S <- round(input$mle_pg * input$n_pg)
      post_alpha <- alpha + S; post_beta <- beta + n
      p <- S / n; se <- sqrt(p / n)
      ci <- pmax(p + c(-1, 1) * qnorm(0.975) * se, 0)
      pm <- post_alpha / post_beta
      psd <- sqrt(post_alpha) / post_beta
      pci <- qgamma(c(0.025, 0.975), post_alpha, post_beta)
    } else {
      mu0 <- input$mu0; kappa0 <- input$kappa0; sigma <- input$sigma_nn
      n <- input$n_nn; ybar <- input$ybar_nn
      post_kappa <- kappa0 + n
      p <- ybar; se <- sigma / sqrt(n)
      ci <- p + c(-1, 1) * qnorm(0.975) * se
      pm <- (kappa0 * mu0 + n * ybar) / post_kappa
      psd <- sigma / sqrt(post_kappa)
      pci <- qnorm(c(0.025, 0.975), pm, psd)
    }
    data.frame(
      Method = c("MLE (Wald interval)", "Bayesian (posterior)"),
      Estimate = sprintf("%.3f", c(p, pm)),
      SE = sprintf("%.3f", c(se, psd)),
      `95% interval` = c(sprintf("(%.3f, %.3f)", ci[1], ci[2]),
                         sprintf("(%.3f, %.3f)", pci[1], pci[2])),
      check.names = FALSE)
  }, striped = TRUE)

  output$summtab <- renderTable({
    if (input$model == "bb") {
      a1 <- input$a1; a0 <- input$a0; n <- input$n_bb; y <- round(input$mle_bb * input$n_bb)
      post_a1 <- a1 + y; post_a0 <- a0 + (n - y)
      logmarg    <- lbeta(post_a1, post_a0) - lbeta(a1, a0)         # exact
      pred_mean  <- post_a1 / (post_a1 + post_a0)
      pred_sd    <- sqrt(pred_mean * (1 - pred_mean))
      data.frame(
        quantity = c("prior mean", "log marginal likelihood*", "posterior distribution",
                     "predictive distribution", "predictive mean", "predictive sd"),
        value = c(sprintf("%.3f", a1 / (a1 + a0)),
                  sprintf("%.3f", logmarg),
                  sprintf("Beta(%.2f, %.2f)", post_a1, post_a0),
                  sprintf("Bernoulli(%.3f)", pred_mean),
                  sprintf("%.3f", pred_mean), sprintf("%.3f", pred_sd)))
    } else if (input$model == "pg") {
      alpha <- 1 / input$disp_pg; beta <- alpha / input$mean_pg; n <- input$n_pg; S <- round(input$mle_pg * input$n_pg)
      post_alpha <- alpha + S; post_beta <- beta + n
      logmarg   <- alpha * log(beta) - lgamma(alpha) + lgamma(post_alpha) -
        post_alpha * log(post_beta)                                 # up to -sum(log(y_i!))
      nb_prob   <- post_beta / (post_beta + 1)
      pred_mean <- post_alpha / post_beta
      pred_sd   <- sqrt(pred_mean * (1 + 1 / post_beta))
      data.frame(
        quantity = c("prior mean", "log marginal likelihood*", "posterior distribution",
                     "predictive distribution", "predictive mean", "predictive sd"),
        value = c(sprintf("%.3f", alpha / beta),
                  sprintf("%.3f", logmarg),
                  sprintf("Gamma(%.2f, %.2f)", post_alpha, post_beta),
                  sprintf("NegBin(%.2f, %.3f)", post_alpha, nb_prob),
                  sprintf("%.3f", pred_mean), sprintf("%.3f", pred_sd)))
    } else {
      mu0 <- input$mu0; kappa0 <- input$kappa0; sigma <- input$sigma_nn
      n <- input$n_nn; ybar <- input$ybar_nn
      post_kappa <- kappa0 + n
      post_mu <- (kappa0 * mu0 + n * ybar) / post_kappa
      post_sd <- sigma / sqrt(post_kappa)
      logmarg <- -n / 2 * log(2 * pi * sigma^2) + 0.5 * log(kappa0 / post_kappa) -
        kappa0 * n * (mu0 - ybar)^2 / (2 * sigma^2 * post_kappa)     # up to -SS/(2 sigma^2)
      pred_sd <- sqrt(post_sd^2 + sigma^2)
      data.frame(
        quantity = c("prior mean", "log marginal likelihood*", "posterior distribution",
                     "predictive distribution", "predictive mean", "predictive sd"),
        value = c(sprintf("%.3f", mu0),
                  sprintf("%.3f", logmarg),
                  sprintf("N(%.3f, %.3f^2)", post_mu, post_sd),
                  sprintf("N(%.3f, %.3f^2)", post_mu, pred_sd),
                  sprintf("%.3f", post_mu), sprintf("%.3f", pred_sd)))
    }
  }, colnames = FALSE, striped = TRUE)
}

library(shiny)

### renderPlot replacement: Safari 27 (WebKit) cannot hold the call stack of
### shiny::renderPlot in webR ("Maximum call stack size exceeded"), so draw with
### renderImage instead, which nests about 45 fewer R calls
renderPlot <- function(expr, width = "auto", height = "auto", res = 72, ...,
                       env = parent.frame(), quoted = FALSE) {
    func <- shiny::exprToFunction(expr, env, quoted)
    shiny::renderImage({
        info <- shiny::getCurrentOutputInfo()
        w  <- if (is.numeric(width))  width  else info$width()
        h  <- if (is.numeric(height)) height else info$height()
        shiny::req(w > 0, h > 0)
        pr <- shiny::getDefaultReactiveDomain()$clientData$pixelratio
        if (is.null(pr)) pr <- 1
        f   <- tempfile(fileext = ".png")
        dev <- shiny:::startPNG(f, w * pr, h * pr, res = res * pr)
        on.exit(grDevices::dev.off(dev), add = TRUE)
        grDevices::dev.control(displaylist = "enable")
        v <- withVisible(func())
        if (v$visible) print(v$value)
        list(src = f, contentType = "image/png", width = w, height = h,
             coordmap = shiny:::getCoordmap(v$value, w * pr, h * pr, res * pr))
    }, deleteFile = TRUE)
}

log_g_gamma <- function(x, alpha) {
    (alpha - 1) * (log(alpha - 1) - 1) - log(1 + (x - (alpha - 1))^2 / (2 * alpha - 1))
}
g_gamma <- function(x, alpha) exp(log_g_gamma(x, alpha))

ui <- fluidPage(
    sidebarLayout(
        sidebarPanel(
            width = 3,
            sliderInput("alpha", "shape alpha (target: Gamma(alpha, 1))",
                        min = 1.1, max = 8, value = 3, step = 0.05),
            helpText("The envelope is only valid (g >= f everywhere) for ",
                     "alpha > 2. Below alpha = 2 the target pokes through ",
                     "the envelope near the mode, and the histogram falls ",
                     "slightly short of the true density there."),
            actionButton("resample", "draw new sample")
        ),
        mainPanel(
            width = 9,
            plotOutput("panels", height = "420px")
        )
    )
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {

    draws <- eventReactive(list(input$alpha, input$resample), {
        set.seed(input$resample + 1)
        a <- input$alpha; n <- 2000
        out <- numeric(0); tries <- 0; max_tries <- 2e6
        while (length(out) < n && tries < max_tries) {
            m <- n - length(out)
            x <- rcauchy(m) * sqrt(2 * a - 1) + (a - 1)
            tries <- tries + m
            keep <- log(runif(m)) < dgamma(x, a, log = TRUE) - log_g_gamma(x, a)
            out <- c(out, x[keep])
        }
        list(x = out[seq_len(min(n, length(out)))], accept = length(out) / tries)
    })

    output$panels <- renderPlot({
        d <- draws(); a <- input$alpha
        hi <- max(15, qgamma(0.999, a) * 1.3)
        xs <- seq(1e-3, hi, length.out = 500)
        ymax <- max(dgamma(xs, a), na.rm = TRUE) * 1.6   # scale to the target's
        # peak, not the envelope's: g touches f at the mode but can be much
        # looser far from it (especially for alpha far above 2), which would
        # otherwise blow up the y-axis and hide the interesting region

        par(mfrow = c(1, 2), mar = c(4, 4, 3, 1))

        plot(xs, g_gamma(xs, a), type = "l", lwd = 3, col = "steelblue",
             ylim = c(0, ymax), xlab = "x", ylab = "density",
             main = sprintf("target vs. envelope (alpha = %.2f)", a))
        lines(xs, dgamma(xs, a), lwd = 3, col = "firebrick")
        bad <- dgamma(xs, a) > g_gamma(xs, a)
        if (any(bad)) lines(xs[bad], dgamma(xs, a)[bad], col = "black", lwd = 5)
        legend("topright", bty = "n", lwd = c(3, 3, 5), col = c("firebrick", "steelblue", "black"),
               legend = c("target f", "envelope g", "f > g: invalid"))

        hist(d$x, breaks = 30, freq = FALSE, col = "steelblue", border = "white",
             xlim = c(0, hi), xlab = "x",
             main = sprintf("%d draws (accept rate %.1f%%)", length(d$x), 100 * d$accept))
        curve(dgamma(x, a), add = TRUE, lwd = 3, col = "firebrick")
        legend("topright", bty = "n", lwd = 3, col = "firebrick", legend = "true Gamma density")
    })
}

shinyApp(ui, server)

title: Rejection Sampling from a Gamma Density with a Cauchy Envelope
text:
About the app
Shows how the efficiency of rejection sampling for the Gamma distribution changes with the shape parameter while the draws remain exact. The app above shows the target \(f(x)=\text{Gamma}(\alpha,1)\) density against the Cauchy-based envelope \(g(x)=\exp(\texttt{log\_g\_gamma}(x,\alpha))\) as \(\alpha\) is dragged (left), and a histogram of 2000 fresh rejection-sampled draws against the true density (right) — an exact match whenever the envelope is valid.
Drag \(\alpha\) below \(2\) and the target pokes through the envelope, as in Table 10.2; the crossing is a modest one for this particular envelope, so the histogram only dips slightly short of the curve in the affected region rather than breaking outright, but the sampler is no longer drawing from the exact target.

## ---------------------------------------------------------------- objectives
mk <- function(label, fv, xlim, ylim, start, xstar) {
  force(fv)
  list(label = label, fv = fv, f = function(p) fv(p[1], p[2]),
       xlim = xlim, ylim = ylim, start = start,
       xstar = matrix(xstar, ncol = 2))
}

FNS <- list(
  quad = mk(
    "(a) Well-conditioned quadratic",
    function(x, y) 0.5 * (2 * (x - 1)^2 + 1.6 * (x - 1) * (y - 1) +
                          2 * (y - 1)^2),
    c(-3, 4), c(-3, 4), c(-2, 3), c(1, 1)
  ),
  banana = mk(
    "(b) Rosenbrock banana (narrow curved ridge)",
    function(x, y) (1 - x)^2 + 100 * (y - x^2)^2,
    c(-2, 2), c(-1, 3), c(-1.2, 1), c(1, 1)
  ),
  mix = mk(
    "(c) Highly correlated, two modes",
    function(x, y) {
      rho <- 0.9; den <- 1 - rho^2
      q <- function(u, v) (u^2 - 2 * rho * u * v + v^2) / den
      -log(exp(-0.5 * q(x - 1.2, y - 1.2)) +
           0.6 * exp(-0.5 * q(x + 1.5, y + 1.5) / 1.5) + 1e-12)
    },
    c(-4, 4), c(-4, 4), c(-3, -0.5), c(1.2, 1.2)
  ),
  himmel = mk(
    "(d) Himmelblau (four global minima)",
    function(x, y) (x^2 + y - 11)^2 + (x + y^2 - 7)^2,
    c(-5, 5), c(-5, 5), c(-4, 4),
    rbind(c(3, 2), c(-2.805118, 3.131312),
          c(-3.779310, -3.283186), c(3.584428, -1.848126))
  ),
  beale = mk(
    "(e) Beale (flat plateau, sharp valley)",
    function(x, y) (1.5 - x + x * y)^2 + (2.25 - x + x * y^2)^2 +
                   (2.625 - x + x * y^3)^2,
    c(-4.5, 4.5), c(-4.5, 4.5), c(-1, 1), c(3, 0.5)
  ),
  rastrigin = mk(
    "(f) Rastrigin (many local minima)",
    function(x, y) 20 + x^2 - 10 * cos(2 * pi * x) +
                        y^2 - 10 * cos(2 * pi * y),
    c(-5.12, 5.12), c(-5.12, 5.12), c(-3.1, 4.2), c(0, 0)
  )
)

## default learning rates for the momentum method: a fixed step has to suit
## the scale of each function (larger values diverge on (b), (d) and (e))
ETA <- c(quad = 0.1, banana = 0.002, mix = 0.03, himmel = 0.01,
         beale = 0.01, rastrigin = 0.003)

## ------------------------------------------------- numerical derivatives
num_grad <- function(f, x) {
  h <- 1e-5 * (1 + abs(x))
  g <- numeric(2)
  for (i in 1:2) {
    e <- numeric(2); e[i] <- h[i]
    g[i] <- (f(x + e) - f(x - e)) / (2 * h[i])
  }
  g
}

num_hess <- function(f, x) {
  h <- 1e-4 * (1 + abs(x))
  H <- matrix(0, 2, 2)
  for (i in 1:2) for (j in i:2) {
    ei <- numeric(2); ei[i] <- h[i]
    ej <- numeric(2); ej[j] <- h[j]
    H[i, j] <- (f(x + ei + ej) - f(x + ei - ej) -
                f(x - ei + ej) + f(x - ei - ej)) / (4 * h[i] * h[j])
    H[j, i] <- H[i, j]
  }
  H
}

## --------------------------------------------------- Wolfe line search
line_search <- function(f, g, x, d, a0 = 1, c1 = 1e-4, c2 = 0.9) {
  f0 <- f(x); gd0 <- sum(g * d)
  if (!is.finite(gd0) || gd0 >= 0) return(list(alpha = 0, ok = FALSE))
  lo <- 0; hi <- Inf; a <- a0
  for (it in 1:60) {
    fa <- f(x + a * d)
    if (!is.finite(fa) || fa > f0 + c1 * a * gd0) {
      hi <- a; a <- 0.5 * (lo + hi)
    } else {
      ga <- num_grad(f, x + a * d)
      if (sum(ga * d) < c2 * gd0) {
        lo <- a
        a <- if (is.finite(hi)) 0.5 * (lo + hi) else min(2 * a, 1e4)
      } else {
        return(list(alpha = a, ok = TRUE))
      }
    }
    if (a < 1e-14) return(list(alpha = 0, ok = FALSE))
  }
  list(alpha = a, ok = (a > 0))
}

## ------------------------------------------------------------- algorithms
run_alg <- function(alg, FN, x0, maxit = 60, tol = 1e-6,
                    eta = 0.01, beta = 0.9, alpha = 0.1, beta2 = 0.999) {
  f <- FN$f
  ## no line search: a fixed step needs many more iterations
  if (alg %in% c("mom", "adam")) maxit <- 200
  X <- matrix(NA_real_, maxit + 1, 2); G <- matrix(NA_real_, maxit + 1, 2)
  D <- matrix(NA_real_, maxit + 1, 2); Fv <- rep(NA_real_, maxit + 1)
  AL <- rep(NA_real_, maxit + 1)
  x <- x0; B <- diag(2)
  g_prev <- NULL; d_prev <- NULL; s_prev <- NULL; v <- c(0, 0)
  m <- c(0, 0); m2 <- c(0, 0)                  # Adam's averages of g and g^2
  n <- 0; note <- "maximum number of iterations reached"

  for (k in seq_len(maxit)) {
    if (any(!is.finite(x)) || max(abs(x)) > 1e6) { note <- "diverged"; break }
    g <- num_grad(f, x); gn <- sqrt(sum(g^2))
    X[k, ] <- x; G[k, ] <- g; Fv[k] <- f(x); n <- k
    if (!is.finite(gn)) { note <- "diverged"; break }
    if (gn < tol) { note <- "converged (||grad|| < 1e-6)"; break }

    if (alg == "mom") {
      ## heavy ball: the step keeps a fraction beta of the previous step;
      ## no line search, the learning rate eta is fixed
      v <- beta * v - eta * g
      D[k, ] <- v; AL[k] <- eta
      x <- x + v
      next
    }
    if (alg == "adam") {
      ## Adam: momentum on g, divided coordinate-wise by the root of a running
      ## average of g^2, so each coordinate moves about alpha per step
      ## whatever the scale of f; both averages are bias-corrected
      m  <- beta  * m  + (1 - beta)  * g
      m2 <- beta2 * m2 + (1 - beta2) * g^2
      v  <- -alpha * (m / (1 - beta^k)) / (sqrt(m2 / (1 - beta2^k)) + 1e-8)
      D[k, ] <- v; AL[k] <- alpha
      x <- x + v
      next
    }

    if (alg == "nr") {
      H <- num_hess(f, x); H <- (H + t(H)) / 2
      ev <- eigen(H, symmetric = TRUE, only.values = TRUE)$values
      delta <- 1e-3 * max(1, max(abs(ev)))
      tau <- max(0, delta - min(ev))
      d <- tryCatch(solve(H + tau * diag(2), -g), error = function(e) -g)
    } else if (alg == "gd") {
      d <- -g
    } else if (alg == "cg") {
      if (is.null(d_prev)) {
        d <- -g
      } else {
        y <- g - g_prev
        beta <- max(0, sum(g * y) / max(sum(g_prev^2), 1e-300))   # PR+
        d <- -g + beta * d_prev
      }
      if (sum(g * d) > -1e-12) d <- -g                            # restart
    } else {                                                      # BFGS
      if (!is.null(s_prev)) {
        y <- g - g_prev; sy <- sum(s_prev * y)
        if (sy > 1e-10) {
          rho <- 1 / sy
          V <- diag(2) - rho * outer(s_prev, y)
          B <- V %*% B %*% t(V) + rho * outer(s_prev, s_prev)
        }
      }
      d <- -as.vector(B %*% g)
      if (sum(g * d) > -1e-12) { B <- diag(2); d <- -g }
    }

    ls <- line_search(f, g, x, d)
    D[k, ] <- d; AL[k] <- ls$alpha
    if (ls$alpha <= 0) { note <- "line search failed (flat or non-descent)"; break }

    s_prev <- ls$alpha * d; g_prev <- g; d_prev <- d
    x <- x + s_prev
  }

  list(X = X[1:n, , drop = FALSE], G = G[1:n, , drop = FALSE],
       D = D[1:n, , drop = FALSE], F = Fv[1:n], A = AL[1:n],
       n = n, note = note)
}

ALGS <- c("Safeguarded Newton (modified Hessian + line search)" = "nr",
          "Gradient descent + line search"    = "gd",
          "Conjugate gradient (PR+)"          = "cg",
          "BFGS (quasi-Newton)"               = "bfgs",
          "Momentum (heavy ball, fixed step)" = "mom",
          "Adam (step scaled per coordinate)" = "adam")

## ---------------------------- widen the data box to the device aspect ratio
expand_box <- function(xlim, ylim, pin) {
  if (length(pin) != 2 || any(!is.finite(pin)) || any(pin <= 0))
    return(list(xlim = xlim, ylim = ylim))
  r <- pin[1] / pin[2]
  wd <- diff(xlim); ht <- diff(ylim)
  if (wd / ht < r) {
    w <- ht * r; m <- mean(xlim); xlim <- m + c(-0.5, 0.5) * w
  } else {
    h <- wd / r; m <- mean(ylim); ylim <- m + c(-0.5, 0.5) * h
  }
  list(xlim = xlim, ylim = ylim)
}

## ----------------------------------------------------------------- server
server <- function(input, output, session) {

  FN <- reactive(FNS[[input$fn]])
  playing <- reactiveVal(FALSE)
  play_ms <- 900

  set_start <- function(p) {
    updateNumericInput(session, "x1", value = round(p[1], 2))
    updateNumericInput(session, "x2", value = round(p[2], 2))
  }

  ## a new objective moves the start to its default; clicking the contour
  ## plot moves it to the clicked point
  observeEvent(input$fn, {
    set_start(FNS[[input$fn]]$start)
    updateNumericInput(session, "eta", value = ETA[[input$fn]])
  }, ignoreInit = TRUE)
  observeEvent(input$click, {
    p <- c(input$click$x, input$click$y)
    if (all(is.finite(p))) set_start(p)
  })

  start <- reactive({
    req(is.finite(input$x1), is.finite(input$x2))
    c(input$x1, input$x2)
  })

  ## settings of momentum and Adam (ignored by the others)
  mom_par <- reactive({
    eta <- if (is.finite(input$eta) && input$eta > 0) input$eta else ETA[[input$fn]]
    alpha <- if (is.finite(input$alpha) && input$alpha > 0) input$alpha else 0.1
    beta <- if (is.finite(input$beta)) min(max(input$beta, 0), 0.999) else 0.9
    list(eta = eta, beta = beta, alpha = alpha)
  })

  path <- reactive(run_alg(input$alg, FN(), start(),
                           eta = mom_par()$eta, beta = mom_par()$beta,
                           alpha = mom_par()$alpha))

  ## a second algorithm from the same start, shown for comparison
  ref <- reactive({
    if (input$compare == "none" || input$compare == input$alg) return(NULL)
    run_alg(input$compare, FN(), start(),
            eta = mom_par()$eta, beta = mom_par()$beta,
            alpha = mom_par()$alpha)
  })

  ## current iteration, clamped to the length of the path
  k <- reactive(min(as.integer(input$k), path()$n - 1))

  ## a new path restarts the display at iteration 0
  observeEvent(path(), {
    updateSliderInput(session, "k", max = max(1, path()$n - 1), value = 0)
    playing(isTRUE(input$autoplay) && path()$n > 1)
  })

  go_to <- function(i) {
    updateSliderInput(session, "k", value = max(0, min(i, path()$n - 1)))
  }

  observeEvent(input$play, {
    if (k() >= path()$n - 1) go_to(0)
    if (path()$n > 1) playing(TRUE)
  })
  observeEvent(input$pause, playing(FALSE))
  observeEvent(input$step,  { playing(FALSE); go_to(k() + 1) })
  observeEvent(input$back,  { playing(FALSE); go_to(k() - 1) })
  observeEvent(input$first, { playing(FALSE); go_to(0) })
  observeEvent(input$toend, { playing(FALSE); go_to(path()$n - 1) })

  observe({
    if (!isTRUE(playing())) return()
    kk <- isolate(k())
    if (kk >= isolate(path()$n) - 1) { playing(FALSE); return() }
    invalidateLater(play_ms, session)
    isolate(go_to(kk + 1))
  })

  output$contour <- renderPlot({
    FNc <- FN(); P <- path(); RP <- ref(); kk <- k() + 1L

    par(mar = c(7, 4, 2, 1))                 # room for the legend below
    plot.new()
    bx <- expand_box(FNc$xlim, FNc$ylim, par("pin"))
    plot.window(xlim = bx$xlim, ylim = bx$ylim, xaxs = "i", yaxs = "i")

    xs <- seq(bx$xlim[1], bx$xlim[2], length.out = 180)
    ys <- seq(bx$ylim[1], bx$ylim[2], length.out = 180)
    z  <- outer(xs, ys, FNc$fv)
    zf <- z[is.finite(z)]
    lv <- unique(quantile(zf, probs = seq(0, 1, length.out = 30)^1.7))
    contour(xs, ys, z, levels = lv, add = TRUE, col = "grey70",
            drawlabels = FALSE)
    axis(1); axis(2); box()
    title(main = paste0(names(ALGS)[ALGS == input$alg], " on ",
                        sub("^\\([a-f]\\) ", "", FNc$label)),
          xlab = expression(x[1]), ylab = expression(x[2]), cex.main = 1)
    points(FNc$xstar[, 1], FNc$xstar[, 2], pch = 3, col = "darkgreen",
           lwd = 2, cex = 1.2)

    ## the comparison path, drawn underneath
    if (!is.null(RP)) {
      Q <- RP$X[seq_len(min(kk, RP$n)), , drop = FALSE]
      if (nrow(Q) > 1) lines(Q[, 1], Q[, 2], col = "grey45", lwd = 2, lty = 2)
      points(Q[, 1], Q[, 2], pch = 21, bg = "grey85", col = "grey45",
             cex = 0.9)
    }

    X <- P$X
    if (kk > 1) lines(X[1:kk, 1], X[1:kk, 2], col = "steelblue", lwd = 2)
    points(X[1:kk, 1], X[1:kk, 2], pch = 21, bg = "steelblue", cex = 1.1)

    cur <- X[kk, ]
    inside <- cur[1] >= bx$xlim[1] && cur[1] <= bx$xlim[2] &&
              cur[2] >= bx$ylim[1] && cur[2] <= bx$ylim[2]
    if (inside) {
      ## Arrow along -grad f (steepest descent), of fixed length on screen.
      ## The gradient is a covector, so its on-screen components are obtained
      ## by multiplying by the units-per-inch factors; the box is widened to
      ## the device aspect ratio, so here the two factors agree anyway.
      g <- -P$G[kk, ]
      upi <- c(diff(par("usr")[1:2]) / par("pin")[1],
               diff(par("usr")[3:4]) / par("pin")[2])
      gs <- g * upi
      if (sqrt(sum(g^2)) > 1e-6 && sqrt(sum(gs^2)) > 0) {
        d <- 0.45 * gs / sqrt(sum(gs^2)) * upi              # 0.45 inch long
        arrows(cur[1], cur[2], cur[1] + d[1], cur[2] + d[2],
               col = "#E8820C", lwd = 3, length = 0.09)
      }
      points(cur[1], cur[2], pch = 21, bg = "firebrick", cex = 1.8)
    } else {
      mtext(sprintf("current iterate (%.3g, %.3g) is off the plotted region",
                    cur[1], cur[2]), side = 3, line = -1.5,
            col = "firebrick", cex = 0.9)
    }

    leg <- list(txt = c("current iterate", "minimum",
                        "steepest descent (direction)"),
                pch = c(21, 3, NA), bg = c("firebrick", NA, NA),
                lwd = c(NA, 2, 3), lty = c(NA, NA, 1),
                col = c("black", "darkgreen", "#E8820C"))
    if (!is.null(RP)) {
      leg$txt <- c(leg$txt, names(ALGS)[ALGS == input$compare])
      leg$pch <- c(leg$pch, NA); leg$bg <- c(leg$bg, NA)
      leg$lwd <- c(leg$lwd, 2);  leg$lty <- c(leg$lty, 2)
      leg$col <- c(leg$col, "grey45")
    }
    ## legend under the x axis label, so that it never covers the path
    y0 <- grconvertY(grconvertY(par("usr")[3], "user", "inches") -
                     3.2 * par("csi"), "inches", "user")
    legend(mean(par("usr")[1:2]), y0, xjust = 0.5, yjust = 1, xpd = NA,
           ncol = 2, bty = "n", cex = 0.85,
           pch = leg$pch, pt.bg = leg$bg, lwd = leg$lwd, lty = leg$lty,
           col = leg$col, legend = leg$txt)
  })

  ## compact numbers: fixed with three decimals, switching to scientific
  ## for very large or very small values
  f3 <- function(x) ifelse(!is.finite(x), "",
          ifelse(abs(x) >= 1e5 | (x != 0 & abs(x) < 1e-3),
                 formatC(x, format = "e", digits = 1),
                 formatC(x, format = "f", digits = 3)))

  ## why the run ended, shown as one line under the table
  output$note <- renderUI({
    P <- path(); RP <- ref()
    if (k() + 1 < P$n) return(NULL)
    HTML(paste0("<i>", P$note,
                if (!is.null(RP)) paste0("; ", names(ALGS)[ALGS == input$compare],
                                         ": ", RP$note, " after ", RP$n - 1,
                                         " iterations"),
                "</i>"))
  })

  output$tab <- renderTable({
    P <- path(); kk <- k() + 1L
    ## the step length that led to each iterate (none for the start)
    a_in <- c(NA, P$A)[seq_len(P$n)]
    i <- seq_len(kk)
    d <- data.frame(iteration = as.character(i - 1),
                    x1 = f3(P$X[i, 1]), x2 = f3(P$X[i, 2]),
                    f = f3(P$F[i]),
                    `||grad||` = f3(sqrt(rowSums(P$G[i, , drop = FALSE]^2))),
                    step = f3(a_in[i]),
                    check.names = FALSE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
    tail(d, 5)
  }, rownames = FALSE, align = "r", width = "100%")
}

shinyApp(ui, server)

title: Comparing Gradient Descent and Newton-Raphson Optimization Algorithms
text:
About the app
Lets you compare the paths that gradient descent, momentum, Adam, conjugate gradient, BFGS and safeguarded Newton take on the same objective, to see how curvature information affects speed and stability. Choose an objective and an algorithm, click a starting point, and step or play through the iterations, optionally with a second algorithm overlaid as a dashed grey path.
The app above runs safeguarded Newton, gradient descent, conjugate gradient, BFGS, momentum and Adam on six test functions, ranging from a well-conditioned quadratic to Rastrigin’s many local minima. Its controls match those of the safeguarded Newton–Raphson app (Safeguarded Newton-Raphson). Click in the contour plot (or type values) to choose a starting point, then use the playback buttons to step through the iterations or play the path as an animation. The orange arrow at the current iterate shows the direction of steepest descent, \(-\nabla f\). A second algorithm can be overlaid from the same start as a dashed grey path, and the latest iterations, with the gradient norm and the step length chosen by the line search (\(\eta\) for momentum, \(\alpha\) for Adam), are listed under the plot.
The momentum (heavy-ball) method is the generic optimizer behind much of machine learning: each step is \(v_{k+1} = \beta v_k - \eta \nabla f(x_k)\), \(x_{k+1} = x_k + v_{k+1}\), with a fixed learning rate \(\eta\) instead of a line search, so it needs many more iterations (up to 200) and diverges when \(\eta\) is too large for the function’s curvature. Its \(\eta\) and \(\beta\) can be set when it is chosen, and \(\eta\) resets to a default suited to each function.
Adam applies to any differentiable function in the same way, but rescales the step coordinate by coordinate. It keeps running averages of the gradient and of its square, \(m_{k} = \beta_1 m_{k-1} + (1-\beta_1) g_k\) and \(s_{k} = \beta_2 s_{k-1} + (1-\beta_2) g_k^2\), corrects both for starting at zero (\(\hat m_k = m_k/(1-\beta_1^k)\), \(\hat s_k = s_k/(1-\beta_2^k)\)), and steps \(x_{k+1} = x_k - \alpha\, \hat m_k / (\sqrt{\hat s_k} + \epsilon)\). Dividing by \(\sqrt{\hat s_k}\) makes each coordinate move roughly \(\alpha\) per step whatever the scale of \(f\), so one \(\alpha\) (default 0.1) works on all six functions, where momentum needs its own \(\eta\) for each; \(\beta_1\) is the shared \(\beta\) input and \(\beta_2 = 0.999\).
The app is built the same way as the Newton–Raphson divergence app earlier in this chapter (Safeguarded Newton-Raphson).






NoteR source for this app





library(shiny)

### renderPlot replacement: Safari 27 (WebKit) cannot hold the call stack of
### shiny::renderPlot in webR ("Maximum call stack size exceeded"), so draw with
### renderImage instead, which nests about 45 fewer R calls
renderPlot <- function(expr, width = "auto", height = "auto", res = 72, ...,
                       env = parent.frame(), quoted = FALSE) {
    func <- shiny::exprToFunction(expr, env, quoted)
    shiny::renderImage({
        info <- shiny::getCurrentOutputInfo()
        w  <- if (is.numeric(width))  width  else info$width()
        h  <- if (is.numeric(height)) height else info$height()
        shiny::req(w > 0, h > 0)
        pr <- shiny::getDefaultReactiveDomain()$clientData$pixelratio
        if (is.null(pr)) pr <- 1
        f   <- tempfile(fileext = ".png")
        dev <- shiny:::startPNG(f, w * pr, h * pr, res = res * pr)
        on.exit(grDevices::dev.off(dev), add = TRUE)
        grDevices::dev.control(displaylist = "enable")
        v <- withVisible(func())
        if (v$visible) print(v$value)
        list(src = f, contentType = "image/png", width = w, height = h,
             coordmap = shiny:::getCoordmap(v$value, w * pr, h * pr, res * pr))
    }, deleteFile = TRUE)
}

## ---------------------------------------------------------------- objectives
mk <- function(label, fv, xlim, ylim, start, xstar) {
  force(fv)
  list(label = label, fv = fv, f = function(p) fv(p[1], p[2]),
       xlim = xlim, ylim = ylim, start = start,
       xstar = matrix(xstar, ncol = 2))
}

FNS <- list(
  quad = mk(
    "(a) Well-conditioned quadratic",
    function(x, y) 0.5 * (2 * (x - 1)^2 + 1.6 * (x - 1) * (y - 1) +
                          2 * (y - 1)^2),
    c(-3, 4), c(-3, 4), c(-2, 3), c(1, 1)
  ),
  banana = mk(
    "(b) Rosenbrock banana (narrow curved ridge)",
    function(x, y) (1 - x)^2 + 100 * (y - x^2)^2,
    c(-2, 2), c(-1, 3), c(-1.2, 1), c(1, 1)
  ),
  mix = mk(
    "(c) Highly correlated, two modes",
    function(x, y) {
      rho <- 0.9; den <- 1 - rho^2
      q <- function(u, v) (u^2 - 2 * rho * u * v + v^2) / den
      -log(exp(-0.5 * q(x - 1.2, y - 1.2)) +
           0.6 * exp(-0.5 * q(x + 1.5, y + 1.5) / 1.5) + 1e-12)
    },
    c(-4, 4), c(-4, 4), c(-3, -0.5), c(1.2, 1.2)
  ),
  himmel = mk(
    "(d) Himmelblau (four global minima)",
    function(x, y) (x^2 + y - 11)^2 + (x + y^2 - 7)^2,
    c(-5, 5), c(-5, 5), c(-4, 4),
    rbind(c(3, 2), c(-2.805118, 3.131312),
          c(-3.779310, -3.283186), c(3.584428, -1.848126))
  ),
  beale = mk(
    "(e) Beale (flat plateau, sharp valley)",
    function(x, y) (1.5 - x + x * y)^2 + (2.25 - x + x * y^2)^2 +
                   (2.625 - x + x * y^3)^2,
    c(-4.5, 4.5), c(-4.5, 4.5), c(-1, 1), c(3, 0.5)
  ),
  rastrigin = mk(
    "(f) Rastrigin (many local minima)",
    function(x, y) 20 + x^2 - 10 * cos(2 * pi * x) +
                        y^2 - 10 * cos(2 * pi * y),
    c(-5.12, 5.12), c(-5.12, 5.12), c(-3.1, 4.2), c(0, 0)
  )
)

## default learning rates for the momentum method: a fixed step has to suit
## the scale of each function (larger values diverge on (b), (d) and (e))
ETA <- c(quad = 0.1, banana = 0.002, mix = 0.03, himmel = 0.01,
         beale = 0.01, rastrigin = 0.003)

## ------------------------------------------------- numerical derivatives
num_grad <- function(f, x) {
  h <- 1e-5 * (1 + abs(x))
  g <- numeric(2)
  for (i in 1:2) {
    e <- numeric(2); e[i] <- h[i]
    g[i] <- (f(x + e) - f(x - e)) / (2 * h[i])
  }
  g
}

num_hess <- function(f, x) {
  h <- 1e-4 * (1 + abs(x))
  H <- matrix(0, 2, 2)
  for (i in 1:2) for (j in i:2) {
    ei <- numeric(2); ei[i] <- h[i]
    ej <- numeric(2); ej[j] <- h[j]
    H[i, j] <- (f(x + ei + ej) - f(x + ei - ej) -
                f(x - ei + ej) + f(x - ei - ej)) / (4 * h[i] * h[j])
    H[j, i] <- H[i, j]
  }
  H
}

## --------------------------------------------------- Wolfe line search
line_search <- function(f, g, x, d, a0 = 1, c1 = 1e-4, c2 = 0.9) {
  f0 <- f(x); gd0 <- sum(g * d)
  if (!is.finite(gd0) || gd0 >= 0) return(list(alpha = 0, ok = FALSE))
  lo <- 0; hi <- Inf; a <- a0
  for (it in 1:60) {
    fa <- f(x + a * d)
    if (!is.finite(fa) || fa > f0 + c1 * a * gd0) {
      hi <- a; a <- 0.5 * (lo + hi)
    } else {
      ga <- num_grad(f, x + a * d)
      if (sum(ga * d) < c2 * gd0) {
        lo <- a
        a <- if (is.finite(hi)) 0.5 * (lo + hi) else min(2 * a, 1e4)
      } else {
        return(list(alpha = a, ok = TRUE))
      }
    }
    if (a < 1e-14) return(list(alpha = 0, ok = FALSE))
  }
  list(alpha = a, ok = (a > 0))
}

## ------------------------------------------------------------- algorithms
run_alg <- function(alg, FN, x0, maxit = 60, tol = 1e-6,
                    eta = 0.01, beta = 0.9, alpha = 0.1, beta2 = 0.999) {
  f <- FN$f
  ## no line search: a fixed step needs many more iterations
  if (alg %in% c("mom", "adam")) maxit <- 200
  X <- matrix(NA_real_, maxit + 1, 2); G <- matrix(NA_real_, maxit + 1, 2)
  D <- matrix(NA_real_, maxit + 1, 2); Fv <- rep(NA_real_, maxit + 1)
  AL <- rep(NA_real_, maxit + 1)
  x <- x0; B <- diag(2)
  g_prev <- NULL; d_prev <- NULL; s_prev <- NULL; v <- c(0, 0)
  m <- c(0, 0); m2 <- c(0, 0)                  # Adam's averages of g and g^2
  n <- 0; note <- "maximum number of iterations reached"

  for (k in seq_len(maxit)) {
    if (any(!is.finite(x)) || max(abs(x)) > 1e6) { note <- "diverged"; break }
    g <- num_grad(f, x); gn <- sqrt(sum(g^2))
    X[k, ] <- x; G[k, ] <- g; Fv[k] <- f(x); n <- k
    if (!is.finite(gn)) { note <- "diverged"; break }
    if (gn < tol) { note <- "converged (||grad|| < 1e-6)"; break }

    if (alg == "mom") {
      ## heavy ball: the step keeps a fraction beta of the previous step;
      ## no line search, the learning rate eta is fixed
      v <- beta * v - eta * g
      D[k, ] <- v; AL[k] <- eta
      x <- x + v
      next
    }
    if (alg == "adam") {
      ## Adam: momentum on g, divided coordinate-wise by the root of a running
      ## average of g^2, so each coordinate moves about alpha per step
      ## whatever the scale of f; both averages are bias-corrected
      m  <- beta  * m  + (1 - beta)  * g
      m2 <- beta2 * m2 + (1 - beta2) * g^2
      v  <- -alpha * (m / (1 - beta^k)) / (sqrt(m2 / (1 - beta2^k)) + 1e-8)
      D[k, ] <- v; AL[k] <- alpha
      x <- x + v
      next
    }

    if (alg == "nr") {
      H <- num_hess(f, x); H <- (H + t(H)) / 2
      ev <- eigen(H, symmetric = TRUE, only.values = TRUE)$values
      delta <- 1e-3 * max(1, max(abs(ev)))
      tau <- max(0, delta - min(ev))
      d <- tryCatch(solve(H + tau * diag(2), -g), error = function(e) -g)
    } else if (alg == "gd") {
      d <- -g
    } else if (alg == "cg") {
      if (is.null(d_prev)) {
        d <- -g
      } else {
        y <- g - g_prev
        beta <- max(0, sum(g * y) / max(sum(g_prev^2), 1e-300))   # PR+
        d <- -g + beta * d_prev
      }
      if (sum(g * d) > -1e-12) d <- -g                            # restart
    } else {                                                      # BFGS
      if (!is.null(s_prev)) {
        y <- g - g_prev; sy <- sum(s_prev * y)
        if (sy > 1e-10) {
          rho <- 1 / sy
          V <- diag(2) - rho * outer(s_prev, y)
          B <- V %*% B %*% t(V) + rho * outer(s_prev, s_prev)
        }
      }
      d <- -as.vector(B %*% g)
      if (sum(g * d) > -1e-12) { B <- diag(2); d <- -g }
    }

    ls <- line_search(f, g, x, d)
    D[k, ] <- d; AL[k] <- ls$alpha
    if (ls$alpha <= 0) { note <- "line search failed (flat or non-descent)"; break }

    s_prev <- ls$alpha * d; g_prev <- g; d_prev <- d
    x <- x + s_prev
  }

  list(X = X[1:n, , drop = FALSE], G = G[1:n, , drop = FALSE],
       D = D[1:n, , drop = FALSE], F = Fv[1:n], A = AL[1:n],
       n = n, note = note)
}

ALGS <- c("Safeguarded Newton (modified Hessian + line search)" = "nr",
          "Gradient descent + line search"    = "gd",
          "Conjugate gradient (PR+)"          = "cg",
          "BFGS (quasi-Newton)"               = "bfgs",
          "Momentum (heavy ball, fixed step)" = "mom",
          "Adam (step scaled per coordinate)" = "adam")

## ---------------------------- widen the data box to the device aspect ratio
expand_box <- function(xlim, ylim, pin) {
  if (length(pin) != 2 || any(!is.finite(pin)) || any(pin <= 0))
    return(list(xlim = xlim, ylim = ylim))
  r <- pin[1] / pin[2]
  wd <- diff(xlim); ht <- diff(ylim)
  if (wd / ht < r) {
    w <- ht * r; m <- mean(xlim); xlim <- m + c(-0.5, 0.5) * w
  } else {
    h <- wd / r; m <- mean(ylim); ylim <- m + c(-0.5, 0.5) * h
  }
  list(xlim = xlim, ylim = ylim)
}

## ----------------------------------------------------------------- server
server <- function(input, output, session) {

  FN <- reactive(FNS[[input$fn]])
  playing <- reactiveVal(FALSE)
  play_ms <- 900

  set_start <- function(p) {
    updateNumericInput(session, "x1", value = round(p[1], 2))
    updateNumericInput(session, "x2", value = round(p[2], 2))
  }

  ## a new objective moves the start to its default; clicking the contour
  ## plot moves it to the clicked point
  observeEvent(input$fn, {
    set_start(FNS[[input$fn]]$start)
    updateNumericInput(session, "eta", value = ETA[[input$fn]])
  }, ignoreInit = TRUE)
  observeEvent(input$click, {
    p <- c(input$click$x, input$click$y)
    if (all(is.finite(p))) set_start(p)
  })

  start <- reactive({
    req(is.finite(input$x1), is.finite(input$x2))
    c(input$x1, input$x2)
  })

  ## settings of momentum and Adam (ignored by the others)
  mom_par <- reactive({
    eta <- if (is.finite(input$eta) && input$eta > 0) input$eta else ETA[[input$fn]]
    alpha <- if (is.finite(input$alpha) && input$alpha > 0) input$alpha else 0.1
    beta <- if (is.finite(input$beta)) min(max(input$beta, 0), 0.999) else 0.9
    list(eta = eta, beta = beta, alpha = alpha)
  })

  path <- reactive(run_alg(input$alg, FN(), start(),
                           eta = mom_par()$eta, beta = mom_par()$beta,
                           alpha = mom_par()$alpha))

  ## a second algorithm from the same start, shown for comparison
  ref <- reactive({
    if (input$compare == "none" || input$compare == input$alg) return(NULL)
    run_alg(input$compare, FN(), start(),
            eta = mom_par()$eta, beta = mom_par()$beta,
            alpha = mom_par()$alpha)
  })

  ## current iteration, clamped to the length of the path
  k <- reactive(min(as.integer(input$k), path()$n - 1))

  ## a new path restarts the display at iteration 0
  observeEvent(path(), {
    updateSliderInput(session, "k", max = max(1, path()$n - 1), value = 0)
    playing(isTRUE(input$autoplay) && path()$n > 1)
  })

  go_to <- function(i) {
    updateSliderInput(session, "k", value = max(0, min(i, path()$n - 1)))
  }

  observeEvent(input$play, {
    if (k() >= path()$n - 1) go_to(0)
    if (path()$n > 1) playing(TRUE)
  })
  observeEvent(input$pause, playing(FALSE))
  observeEvent(input$step,  { playing(FALSE); go_to(k() + 1) })
  observeEvent(input$back,  { playing(FALSE); go_to(k() - 1) })
  observeEvent(input$first, { playing(FALSE); go_to(0) })
  observeEvent(input$toend, { playing(FALSE); go_to(path()$n - 1) })

  observe({
    if (!isTRUE(playing())) return()
    kk <- isolate(k())
    if (kk >= isolate(path()$n) - 1) { playing(FALSE); return() }
    invalidateLater(play_ms, session)
    isolate(go_to(kk + 1))
  })

  output$contour <- renderPlot({
    FNc <- FN(); P <- path(); RP <- ref(); kk <- k() + 1L

    par(mar = c(7, 4, 2, 1))                 # room for the legend below
    plot.new()
    bx <- expand_box(FNc$xlim, FNc$ylim, par("pin"))
    plot.window(xlim = bx$xlim, ylim = bx$ylim, xaxs = "i", yaxs = "i")

    xs <- seq(bx$xlim[1], bx$xlim[2], length.out = 180)
    ys <- seq(bx$ylim[1], bx$ylim[2], length.out = 180)
    z  <- outer(xs, ys, FNc$fv)
    zf <- z[is.finite(z)]
    lv <- unique(quantile(zf, probs = seq(0, 1, length.out = 30)^1.7))
    contour(xs, ys, z, levels = lv, add = TRUE, col = "grey70",
            drawlabels = FALSE)
    axis(1); axis(2); box()
    title(main = paste0(names(ALGS)[ALGS == input$alg], " on ",
                        sub("^\\([a-f]\\) ", "", FNc$label)),
          xlab = expression(x[1]), ylab = expression(x[2]), cex.main = 1)
    points(FNc$xstar[, 1], FNc$xstar[, 2], pch = 3, col = "darkgreen",
           lwd = 2, cex = 1.2)

    ## the comparison path, drawn underneath
    if (!is.null(RP)) {
      Q <- RP$X[seq_len(min(kk, RP$n)), , drop = FALSE]
      if (nrow(Q) > 1) lines(Q[, 1], Q[, 2], col = "grey45", lwd = 2, lty = 2)
      points(Q[, 1], Q[, 2], pch = 21, bg = "grey85", col = "grey45",
             cex = 0.9)
    }

    X <- P$X
    if (kk > 1) lines(X[1:kk, 1], X[1:kk, 2], col = "steelblue", lwd = 2)
    points(X[1:kk, 1], X[1:kk, 2], pch = 21, bg = "steelblue", cex = 1.1)

    cur <- X[kk, ]
    inside <- cur[1] >= bx$xlim[1] && cur[1] <= bx$xlim[2] &&
              cur[2] >= bx$ylim[1] && cur[2] <= bx$ylim[2]
    if (inside) {
      ## Arrow along -grad f (steepest descent), of fixed length on screen.
      ## The gradient is a covector, so its on-screen components are obtained
      ## by multiplying by the units-per-inch factors; the box is widened to
      ## the device aspect ratio, so here the two factors agree anyway.
      g <- -P$G[kk, ]
      upi <- c(diff(par("usr")[1:2]) / par("pin")[1],
               diff(par("usr")[3:4]) / par("pin")[2])
      gs <- g * upi
      if (sqrt(sum(g^2)) > 1e-6 && sqrt(sum(gs^2)) > 0) {
        d <- 0.45 * gs / sqrt(sum(gs^2)) * upi              # 0.45 inch long
        arrows(cur[1], cur[2], cur[1] + d[1], cur[2] + d[2],
               col = "#E8820C", lwd = 3, length = 0.09)
      }
      points(cur[1], cur[2], pch = 21, bg = "firebrick", cex = 1.8)
    } else {
      mtext(sprintf("current iterate (%.3g, %.3g) is off the plotted region",
                    cur[1], cur[2]), side = 3, line = -1.5,
            col = "firebrick", cex = 0.9)
    }

    leg <- list(txt = c("current iterate", "minimum",
                        "steepest descent (direction)"),
                pch = c(21, 3, NA), bg = c("firebrick", NA, NA),
                lwd = c(NA, 2, 3), lty = c(NA, NA, 1),
                col = c("black", "darkgreen", "#E8820C"))
    if (!is.null(RP)) {
      leg$txt <- c(leg$txt, names(ALGS)[ALGS == input$compare])
      leg$pch <- c(leg$pch, NA); leg$bg <- c(leg$bg, NA)
      leg$lwd <- c(leg$lwd, 2);  leg$lty <- c(leg$lty, 2)
      leg$col <- c(leg$col, "grey45")
    }
    ## legend under the x axis label, so that it never covers the path
    y0 <- grconvertY(grconvertY(par("usr")[3], "user", "inches") -
                     3.2 * par("csi"), "inches", "user")
    legend(mean(par("usr")[1:2]), y0, xjust = 0.5, yjust = 1, xpd = NA,
           ncol = 2, bty = "n", cex = 0.85,
           pch = leg$pch, pt.bg = leg$bg, lwd = leg$lwd, lty = leg$lty,
           col = leg$col, legend = leg$txt)
  })

  ## compact numbers: fixed with three decimals, switching to scientific
  ## for very large or very small values
  f3 <- function(x) ifelse(!is.finite(x), "",
          ifelse(abs(x) >= 1e5 | (x != 0 & abs(x) < 1e-3),
                 formatC(x, format = "e", digits = 1),
                 formatC(x, format = "f", digits = 3)))

  ## why the run ended, shown as one line under the table
  output$note <- renderUI({
    P <- path(); RP <- ref()
    if (k() + 1 < P$n) return(NULL)
    HTML(paste0("<i>", P$note,
                if (!is.null(RP)) paste0("; ", names(ALGS)[ALGS == input$compare],
                                         ": ", RP$note, " after ", RP$n - 1,
                                         " iterations"),
                "</i>"))
  })

  output$tab <- renderTable({
    P <- path(); kk <- k() + 1L
    ## the step length that led to each iterate (none for the start)
    a_in <- c(NA, P$A)[seq_len(P$n)]
    i <- seq_len(kk)
    d <- data.frame(iteration = as.character(i - 1),
                    x1 = f3(P$X[i, 1]), x2 = f3(P$X[i, 2]),
                    f = f3(P$F[i]),
                    `||grad||` = f3(sqrt(rowSums(P$G[i, , drop = FALSE]^2))),
                    step = f3(a_in[i]),
                    check.names = FALSE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
    tail(d, 5)
  }, rownames = FALSE, align = "r", width = "100%")
}

shinyApp(ui, server)

### renderPlot replacement: Safari 27 (WebKit) cannot hold the call stack of
### shiny::renderPlot in webR ("Maximum call stack size exceeded"), so draw with
### renderImage instead, which nests about 45 fewer R calls
renderPlot <- function(expr, width = "auto", height = "auto", res = 72, ...,
                       env = parent.frame(), quoted = FALSE) {
    func <- shiny::exprToFunction(expr, env, quoted)
    shiny::renderImage({
        info <- shiny::getCurrentOutputInfo()
        w  <- if (is.numeric(width))  width  else info$width()
        h  <- if (is.numeric(height)) height else info$height()
        shiny::req(w > 0, h > 0)
        pr <- shiny::getDefaultReactiveDomain()$clientData$pixelratio
        if (is.null(pr)) pr <- 1
        f   <- tempfile(fileext = ".png")
        dev <- shiny:::startPNG(f, w * pr, h * pr, res = res * pr)
        on.exit(grDevices::dev.off(dev), add = TRUE)
        grDevices::dev.control(displaylist = "enable")
        v <- withVisible(func())
        if (v$visible) print(v$value)
        list(src = f, contentType = "image/png", width = w, height = h,
             coordmap = shiny:::getCoordmap(v$value, w * pr, h * pr, res * pr))
    }, deleteFile = TRUE)
}

## ---- distribution definitions -------------------------------------------
## Each constructor takes the parameters of a target distribution and returns
## its CDF, inverse CDF, plotting range, support of the density, and a routine
## that draws the true density (or pmf).

## Gamma(shape a, rate b); a = 1 gives the exponential distribution.  The
## inverse CDF has no closed form except for a = 1, so qgamma() inverts the
## CDF numerically.
gamma_dist <- function(a, b) list(
  discrete = FALSE,
  xlim    = c(0, qgamma(0.995, a, b)),   # plotting range
  support = c(0, Inf),                   # known range of the density
  ## maximum of the true density (at the mode (a - 1)/b for a >= 1; the
  ## density is unbounded at 0 for a < 1, so its value at the median is used)
  fmax    = if (a >= 1) dgamma((a - 1) / b, a, b)
            else dgamma(qgamma(0.5, a, b), a, b),
  ## cap on the vertical range of the x histogram, so that the spike at 0
  ## of an unbounded density does not flatten the rest of the plot
  ycap    = if (a >= 1) Inf else 4 * dgamma(qgamma(0.5, a, b), a, b),
  p    = function(x) pgamma(x, a, b),
  qinv = function(u) qgamma(u, a, b),
  dens = function() curve(dgamma(x, a, b), add = TRUE, col = "steelblue",
                          lwd = 2.5, n = 400),
  hist_breaks = function() 30,
  mean = a / b
)

## Piecewise-constant density on [0, 1] with three equal pieces whose
## heights are proportional to h = (h1, h2, h3).  Normalising,
## (c/3)(h1 + h2 + h3) = 1 gives densities 3h / sum(h); the CDF is piecewise
## linear through the cumulative masses at 0, 1/3, 2/3, 1.
pw_dist <- function(h) {
  hh <- 3 * h / sum(h)            # densities on the three pieces
  bb <- c(0, 1/3, 2/3, 1)         # piece boundaries
  Fb <- cumsum(c(0, hh / 3))      # CDF at the boundaries
  list(
    discrete = FALSE,
    xlim    = c(0, 1),
    support = c(0, 1),
    fmax    = max(hh),
    p    = function(x) approx(bb, Fb, xout = pmin(pmax(x, 0), 1))$y,
    ## invert piece by piece: u in [Fb[k], Fb[k+1]) lies on piece k, where
    ## F rises linearly with slope hh[k]; findInterval() skips pieces of
    ## zero height, whose flat parts of the CDF receive no u
    qinv = function(u) {
      k <- findInterval(u, Fb, rightmost.closed = TRUE)
      k <- pmin(pmax(k, 1), 3)
      bb[k] + (u - Fb[k]) / hh[k]
    },
    dens = function() {
      segments(bb[-4], hh, bb[-1], hh, col = "steelblue", lwd = 2.5)
      segments(bb[2:3], hh[1:2], bb[2:3], hh[2:3],
               col = "steelblue", lwd = 2.5, lty = 3)
    },
    hist_breaks = function() seq(0, 1, length.out = 31),
    mean = sum(hh / 3 * (bb[-4] + bb[-1]) / 2)
  )
}

## Binomial(m, p); the inverse CDF of a discrete distribution is the
## generalised inverse F^{-1}(u) = min{x : F(x) >= u}, computed by qbinom().
binom_dist <- function(m, p) list(
  discrete = TRUE,
  xlim    = c(-0.5, m + 0.5),
  support = c(0, m),
  fmax    = max(dbinom(0:m, m, p)),
  p    = function(x) pbinom(x, m, p),
  qinv = function(u) qbinom(u, m, p),
  dens = function() {
    xs <- 0:m
    segments(xs, 0, xs, dbinom(xs, m, p), col = "steelblue", lwd = 2.5)

           cex = if (m <= 30) 1.2 else 0.6)

  mean = m * p

## ---- server --------------------------------------------------------------
server <- function(input, output, session) {

  rv <- reactiveValues(x = numeric(0), u = numeric(0),
                       u_last = numeric(0), x_last = numeric(0))
  playing <- reactiveVal(FALSE)

  ok <- function(v) !is.null(v) && length(v) == 1 && is.finite(v)

  ## the selected target, built from its parameter boxes; invalid parameters
  ## stop everything downstream with a message shown in the plot
  D <- reactive({
    req(input$dist)
    switch(input$dist,
      gamma = {
        a <- input$g_a; b <- input$g_b
        validate(need(ok(a) && ok(b) && a > 0 && b > 0,
                      "Gamma: a and b must be positive."))
        gamma_dist(a, b)
      },
      pw = {
        h <- c(input$pw_h1, input$pw_h2, input$pw_h3)
        validate(need(length(h) == 3 && all(is.finite(h)) && all(h >= 0) &&
                        sum(h) > 0,
                      "Piecewise constant: heights must be >= 0, not all 0."))
        pw_dist(h)
      },
      binom = {
        m <- input$b_m; p <- input$b_p
        validate(need(ok(m) && ok(p) && m >= 1 && m <= 100 && m == round(m) &&
                        p >= 0 && p <= 1,
                      "Binomial: m must be an integer in 1..100 and p in [0, 1]."))
        binom_dist(m, p)
      })
  })
  grid <- reactive(seq(D()$xlim[1], D()$xlim[2], length.out = 400))

  clear <- function() {
    rv$x <- numeric(0); rv$u <- numeric(0)
    rv$u_last <- numeric(0); rv$x_last <- numeric(0)
  }

  stop_play <- function() playing(FALSE)

  N_total <- function() {
    N <- input$N
    if (!ok(N) || N < 1) 1000 else round(N)
  }
  remaining <- function() max(0, N_total() - length(rv$x))

  ## draw m points (default: one step of n, capped by the remaining budget)
  draw_step <- function(m = min(input$n, remaining())) {
    if (m <= 0) { stop_play(); return(invisible()) }
    u  <- runif(m)
    ## sampling via the survival function draws x = S^{-1}(u); since
    ## S(x) = 1 - F(x), this is just F^{-1}(1 - u), and S(x) = u exactly,
    ## so u_last can still be plotted directly against the survival curve.
    xs <- if (input$use_surv) D()$qinv(1 - u) else D()$qinv(u)
    rv$u_last <- u
    rv$x_last <- xs
    rv$x      <- c(rv$x, xs)
    rv$u      <- c(rv$u, u)
    if (remaining() == 0) stop_play()
  }

  observeEvent(input$draw, draw_step())

  ## switching the target, changing its parameters, or toggling CDF/survival
  ## restarts the sampling, since old draws would be shown against a new curve
  observeEvent(D(), { stop_play(); clear() }, ignoreInit = TRUE)
  observeEvent(input$use_surv, { stop_play(); clear() }, ignoreInit = TRUE)

  observeEvent(input$play,  if (remaining() > 0) playing(TRUE))
  observeEvent(input$pause, stop_play())

  ## "To the End": draw all remaining samples at once, skipping the
  ## step-by-step display of the individual draws
  observeEvent(input$toend, {
    stop_play()
    draw_step(remaining())
    rv$u_last <- numeric(0); rv$x_last <- numeric(0)
  })

  observeEvent(input$reset, { stop_play(); clear() })

  observe({
    if (playing()) {
      invalidateLater(play_ms, session)
      isolate(draw_step())
    }
  })

  output$count <- renderText(paste0("Total draws: ", length(rv$x), " / ", N_total()))

  output$moments <- renderText({
    if (length(rv$x) < 2) return("")
    sprintf("sample mean = %.3f  (true = %.3f)", mean(rv$x), D()$mean)
  })

  ## kernel density estimate restricted to the known support [lo, hi]:
  ## the sample is reflected about each finite boundary, so that no mass
  ## leaks outside the support and the estimate is not biased down near it
  kde_bounded <- function(x, lo, hi, xl) {
    bw <- bw.nrd0(x)
    xx <- c(x, if (is.finite(lo)) 2 * lo - x, if (is.finite(hi)) 2 * hi - x)
    d  <- density(xx, bw = bw, from = max(lo, xl[1]), to = min(hi, xl[2]), n = 512)
    d$y <- d$y * length(xx) / length(x)
    d
  }

  ## One figure with three aligned panels:
  ##   top-left : histogram of all U_i on the margin of the u axis
  ##   top-right: the CDF (or survival function) transformation
  ##   bottom-right: histogram of all X_i, upside down and attached to the
  ##                 x axis of the transformation plot (same x range)
  ##   bottom-left: legend
  output$mainPlot <- renderPlot({
    xl <- D()$xlim; g <- grid()
    disc   <- D()$discrete
    use_s  <- input$use_surv
    yvals  <- if (use_s) 1 - D()$p(g) else D()$p(g)
    ylab   <- if (use_s) "u = S(x) = 1 - F(x)" else "u = F(x)"
    main   <- if (use_s) "Draw u on the vertical axis, read x off the survival function"
              else "Draw u on the vertical axis, read x off the CDF"

    layout(matrix(c(1, 2, 4, 3), nrow = 2, byrow = TRUE),
           widths = c(1.2, 5), heights = c(1, 1))

    ## (1) histogram of U, attached to the left edge of the transformation
    ## plot (same u range), bars growing leftwards
    brk_u <- seq(0, 1, length.out = 21)
    par(mar = c(0, 0.5, 3, 0))
    dmax <- 1.5
    if (length(rv$u) > 0) {
      hu <- hist(rv$u, breaks = brk_u, plot = FALSE)
      dmax <- max(dmax, hu$density)
    }
    plot.new(); plot.window(xlim = c(dmax, 0), ylim = c(0, 1), xaxs = "i")
    if (length(rv$u) > 0)
      rect(hu$density, brk_u[-length(brk_u)], 0, brk_u[-1],
           col = "grey80", border = "white")
    abline(v = 1, col = "steelblue", lty = 2)
    mtext("hist of U", side = 3, line = 1.2, cex = 0.8)
    mtext("1", side = 3, at = 1, line = 0.1, cex = 0.7, col = "steelblue")

    ## (2) transformation plot; no bottom or left margin, so the X histogram
    ## hangs directly from its x axis and the U histogram from its left
    ## edge; the u axis is drawn on the right
    par(mar = c(0, 0, 3, 4))
    plot(g, yvals, type = "n", xlim = xl, ylim = c(0, 1), xaxt = "n",
         yaxt = "n", xlab = "", ylab = "", main = main)
    axis(1, labels = FALSE); axis(4)
    mtext(ylab, side = 4, line = 2.5)
    u <- rv$u_last; x <- rv$x_last
    if (length(u) > 0) {
      xc <- pmin(x, xl[2])
      segments(xl[1], u, xc, u, col = "grey65")
      inside <- x <= xl[2]
      segments(x[inside], u[inside], x[inside], par("usr")[3], col = "grey65")
    }
    lines(g, yvals, col = "steelblue", lwd = 2.5,
          type = if (disc) "s" else "l")
    if (length(u) > 0) {
      points(xc, u, pch = 16, col = "firebrick", cex = 1.1)
      points(rep(xl[1], length(u)), u, pch = 16, col = "grey35", cex = 0.8)
    }

    ## (3) histogram of X, upside down, sharing the x range of panel (2)
    par(mar = c(4, 0, 0, 4))
    ylab_x <- if (disc) "proportion" else "density"
    if (length(rv$x) < 2) {
      plot.new(); plot.window(xlim = xl, ylim = c(1, 0))
      box(); axis(1); title(xlab = "x"); mtext(ylab_x, side = 4, line = 2.5)
      text(mean(xl), 0.5, "Draw some samples to see the histogram of x", col = "grey40")
    } else {
      hx   <- hist(rv$x, breaks = D()$hist_breaks(), plot = FALSE)
      kde  <- if (!disc) kde_bounded(rv$x, D()$support[1], D()$support[2], xl)
      ymax <- 1.05 * max(hx$density, if (!disc) kde$y, D()$fmax)
      if (!is.null(D()$ycap)) ymax <- min(ymax, D()$ycap)
      plot.new(); plot.window(xlim = xl, ylim = c(ymax, 0), yaxs = "i")
      rect(hx$breaks[-length(hx$breaks)], 0, hx$breaks[-1], hx$density,
           col = "grey85", border = "white")
      D()$dens()
      if (!disc) lines(kde, col = "darkorange", lwd = 2)
      abline(v = mean(rv$x), col = "firebrick", lwd = 2, lty = 2)
      ## omit the 0 label, which would collide with the u = 0 label above
      at <- pretty(c(0, ymax)); at <- at[at > 0 & at <= ymax]
      box(); axis(1); axis(4, at = at)
      title(xlab = "x"); mtext(ylab_x, side = 4, line = 2.5)
    }

    ## (4) legend in the empty bottom-left cell
    par(mar = c(4, 0.5, 0, 0))
    plot.new()
    legend("center", bty = "n", cex = 0.85, lwd = 2, seg.len = 1.5,
           lty = if (disc) c(1, 2) else c(1, 1, 2),
           col = if (disc) c("steelblue", "firebrick")
                 else c("steelblue", "darkorange", "firebrick"),
           legend = if (disc) c("true pmf", "sample\nmean")
                    else c("true\ndensity", "kernel\ndensity", "sample\nmean"),
           y.intersp = 1.6)
  })
}

title: The Inverse CDF Method
text:
About the app
Demonstrates the inverse-CDF method for generating random numbers from a target distribution by transforming uniform draws. The target and its parameters are set in the panel at the top: \(\text{Gamma}(a, b)\) with shape \(a\) and rate \(b\) (the default \(a = b = 1\) is \(\text{Exp}(1)\); for other shapes the inverse CDF has no closed form and is computed numerically); a piecewise-constant density on \([0,1]\) with three equal pieces of relative heights \(h_1 : h_2 : h_3\) (default \(1:5:10\)), whose piecewise-linear CDF shows most clearly that steep parts of the CDF receive more draws; and the discrete \(\text{Binomial}(m, p)\). The playback buttons draw one step of \(n\) samples, play, pause, skip to the end (drawing all remaining samples at once without the animation), and reset; sampling stops at the total sample size \(N\). The top panel of the plot shows how each uniform draw \(u\) maps through the CDF (or the survival function \(S = 1 - F\)) to a sample \(x\), with a histogram of all \(U_i\) attached to the \(u\) axis. Hanging upside down from the \(x\) axis, the bottom panel shows how the draws accumulate into a histogram against the true density, together with a kernel density estimate of \(X\) restricted to the known support of the density (by reflection at its boundaries).
