library(shiny)

### renderPlot replacement: Safari 27 (WebKit) cannot hold the call stack of
### shiny::renderPlot in webR ("Maximum call stack size exceeded"), so draw with
### renderImage instead, which nests about 45 fewer R calls
renderPlot <- function(expr, width = "auto", height = "auto", res = 72, ...,
                       env = parent.frame(), quoted = FALSE) {
    func <- shiny::exprToFunction(expr, env, quoted)
    shiny::renderImage({
        info <- shiny::getCurrentOutputInfo()
        w  <- if (is.numeric(width))  width  else info$width()
        h  <- if (is.numeric(height)) height else info$height()
        shiny::req(w > 0, h > 0)
        pr <- shiny::getDefaultReactiveDomain()$clientData$pixelratio
        if (is.null(pr)) pr <- 1
        f   <- tempfile(fileext = ".png")
        dev <- shiny:::startPNG(f, w * pr, h * pr, res = res * pr)
        on.exit(grDevices::dev.off(dev), add = TRUE)
        grDevices::dev.control(displaylist = "enable")
        v <- withVisible(func())
        if (v$visible) print(v$value)
        list(src = f, contentType = "image/png", width = w, height = h,
             coordmap = shiny:::getCoordmap(v$value, w * pr, h * pr, res * pr))
    }, deleteFile = TRUE)
}

## ---- distribution definitions -------------------------------------------
## Each constructor takes the parameters of a target distribution and returns
## its CDF, inverse CDF, plotting range, support of the density, and a routine
## that draws the true density (or pmf).

## Gamma(shape a, rate b); a = 1 gives the exponential distribution.  The
## inverse CDF has no closed form except for a = 1, so qgamma() inverts the
## CDF numerically.
gamma_dist <- function(a, b) list(
  discrete = FALSE,
  xlim    = c(0, qgamma(0.995, a, b)),   # plotting range
  support = c(0, Inf),                   # known range of the density
  ## maximum of the true density (at the mode (a - 1)/b for a >= 1; the
  ## density is unbounded at 0 for a < 1, so its value at the median is used)
  fmax    = if (a >= 1) dgamma((a - 1) / b, a, b)
            else dgamma(qgamma(0.5, a, b), a, b),
  ## cap on the vertical range of the x histogram, so that the spike at 0
  ## of an unbounded density does not flatten the rest of the plot
  ycap    = if (a >= 1) Inf else 4 * dgamma(qgamma(0.5, a, b), a, b),
  p    = function(x) pgamma(x, a, b),
  qinv = function(u) qgamma(u, a, b),
  dens = function() curve(dgamma(x, a, b), add = TRUE, col = "steelblue",
                          lwd = 2.5, n = 400),
  hist_breaks = function() 30,
  mean = a / b
)

## Piecewise-constant density on [0, 1] with three equal pieces whose
## heights are proportional to h = (h1, h2, h3).  Normalising,
## (c/3)(h1 + h2 + h3) = 1 gives densities 3h / sum(h); the CDF is piecewise
## linear through the cumulative masses at 0, 1/3, 2/3, 1.
pw_dist <- function(h) {
  hh <- 3 * h / sum(h)            # densities on the three pieces
  bb <- c(0, 1/3, 2/3, 1)         # piece boundaries
  Fb <- cumsum(c(0, hh / 3))      # CDF at the boundaries
  list(
    discrete = FALSE,
    xlim    = c(0, 1),
    support = c(0, 1),
    fmax    = max(hh),
    p    = function(x) approx(bb, Fb, xout = pmin(pmax(x, 0), 1))$y,
    ## invert piece by piece: u in [Fb[k], Fb[k+1]) lies on piece k, where
    ## F rises linearly with slope hh[k]; findInterval() skips pieces of
    ## zero height, whose flat parts of the CDF receive no u
    qinv = function(u) {
      k <- findInterval(u, Fb, rightmost.closed = TRUE)
      k <- pmin(pmax(k, 1), 3)
      bb[k] + (u - Fb[k]) / hh[k]
    },
    dens = function() {
      segments(bb[-4], hh, bb[-1], hh, col = "steelblue", lwd = 2.5)
      segments(bb[2:3], hh[1:2], bb[2:3], hh[2:3],
               col = "steelblue", lwd = 2.5, lty = 3)
    },
    hist_breaks = function() seq(0, 1, length.out = 31),
    mean = sum(hh / 3 * (bb[-4] + bb[-1]) / 2)
  )
}

## Binomial(m, p); the inverse CDF of a discrete distribution is the
## generalised inverse F^{-1}(u) = min{x : F(x) >= u}, computed by qbinom().
binom_dist <- function(m, p) list(
  discrete = TRUE,
  xlim    = c(-0.5, m + 0.5),
  support = c(0, m),
  fmax    = max(dbinom(0:m, m, p)),
  p    = function(x) pbinom(x, m, p),
  qinv = function(u) qbinom(u, m, p),
  dens = function() {
    xs <- 0:m
    segments(xs, 0, xs, dbinom(xs, m, p), col = "steelblue", lwd = 2.5)
    points(xs, dbinom(xs, m, p), pch = 16, col = "steelblue",
           cex = if (m <= 30) 1.2 else 0.6)
  },
  hist_breaks = function() seq(-0.5, m + 0.5, by = 1),
  mean = m * p
)

                       u_last = numeric(0), x_last = numeric(0))
  playing <- reactiveVal(FALSE)

  ok <- function(v) !is.null(v) && length(v) == 1 && is.finite(v)

  ## stop everything downstream with a message shown in the plot

    switch(input$dist,
      gamma = {
        a <- input$g_a; b <- input$g_b
        validate(need(ok(a) && ok(b) && a > 0 && b > 0,
                      "Gamma: a and b must be positive."))
        gamma_dist(a, b)
      },
      pw = {
        h <- c(input$pw_h1, input$pw_h2, input$pw_h3)
        validate(need(length(h) == 3 && all(is.finite(h)) && all(h >= 0) &&
                        sum(h) > 0,
                      "Piecewise constant: heights must be >= 0, not all 0."))
        pw_dist(h)
      },
      binom = {
        m <- input$b_m; p <- input$b_p
        validate(need(ok(m) && ok(p) && m >= 1 && m <= 100 && m == round(m) &&
                        p >= 0 && p <= 1,
                      "Binomial: m must be an integer in 1..100 and p in [0, 1]."))
        binom_dist(m, p)
      })
  })
  grid <- reactive(seq(D()$xlim[1], D()$xlim[2], length.out = 400))

  clear <- function() {
    rv$x <- numeric(0); rv$u <- numeric(0)
    rv$u_last <- numeric(0); rv$x_last <- numeric(0)
  }

  stop_play <- function() playing(FALSE)

  N_total <- function() {
    N <- input$N
    if (!ok(N) || N < 1) 1000 else round(N)
  }
  remaining <- function() max(0, N_total() - length(rv$x))

  ## draw m points (default: one step of n, capped by the remaining budget)
  draw_step <- function(m = min(input$n, remaining())) {
    if (m <= 0) { stop_play(); return(invisible()) }
    u  <- runif(m)
    ## sampling via the survival function draws x = S^{-1}(u); since
    ## S(x) = 1 - F(x), this is just F^{-1}(1 - u), and S(x) = u exactly,
    ## so u_last can still be plotted directly against the survival curve.
    xs <- if (input$use_surv) D()$qinv(1 - u) else D()$qinv(u)
    rv$u_last <- u
    rv$x_last <- xs
    rv$x      <- c(rv$x, xs)
    rv$u      <- c(rv$u, u)

  }

  observeEvent(input$draw, draw_step())

  ## switching the target, changing its parameters, or toggling CDF/survival
  ## restarts the sampling, since old draws would be shown against a new curve
  observeEvent(D(), { stop_play(); clear() }, ignoreInit = TRUE)
  observeEvent(input$use_surv, { stop_play(); clear() }, ignoreInit = TRUE)

  observeEvent(input$play,  if (remaining() > 0) playing(TRUE))
  observeEvent(input$pause, stop_play())

  ## "To the End": draw all remaining samples at once, skipping the
  ## step-by-step display of the individual draws
  observeEvent(input$toend, {
    stop_play()
    draw_step(remaining())
    rv$u_last <- numeric(0); rv$x_last <- numeric(0)
  })

  observeEvent(input$reset, { stop_play(); clear() })

  observe({
    if (playing()) {
      invalidateLater(play_ms, session)
      isolate(draw_step())
    }
  })

  output$count <- renderText(paste0("Total draws: ", length(rv$x), " / ", N_total()))

  output$moments <- renderText({
    if (length(rv$x) < 2) return("")
    sprintf("sample mean = %.3f  (true = %.3f)", mean(rv$x), D()$mean)
  })

  ## kernel density estimate restricted to the known support [lo, hi]:
  ## the sample is reflected about each finite boundary, so that no mass
  ## leaks outside the support and the estimate is not biased down near it
  kde_bounded <- function(x, lo, hi, xl) {
    bw <- bw.nrd0(x)
    xx <- c(x, if (is.finite(lo)) 2 * lo - x, if (is.finite(hi)) 2 * hi - x)
    d  <- density(xx, bw = bw, from = max(lo, xl[1]), to = min(hi, xl[2]), n = 512)
    d$y <- d$y * length(xx) / length(x)
    d
  }

  ## One figure with three aligned panels:
  ##   top-left : histogram of all U_i on the margin of the u axis
  ##   top-right: the CDF (or survival function) transformation
  ##   bottom-right: histogram of all X_i, upside down and attached to the
  ##                 x axis of the transformation plot (same x range)
  ##   bottom-left: legend
  output$mainPlot <- renderPlot({
    xl <- D()$xlim; g <- grid()
    disc   <- D()$discrete
    use_s  <- input$use_surv
    yvals  <- if (use_s) 1 - D()$p(g) else D()$p(g)
    ylab   <- if (use_s) "u = S(x) = 1 - F(x)" else "u = F(x)"
    main   <- if (use_s) "Draw u on the vertical axis, read x off the survival function"
              else "Draw u on the vertical axis, read x off the CDF"

    layout(matrix(c(1, 2, 4, 3), nrow = 2, byrow = TRUE),
           widths = c(1.2, 5), heights = c(1, 1))

    ## (1) histogram of U, attached to the left edge of the transformation
    ## plot (same u range), bars growing leftwards
    brk_u <- seq(0, 1, length.out = 21)
    par(mar = c(0, 0.5, 3, 0))
    dmax <- 1.5
    if (length(rv$u) > 0) {
      hu <- hist(rv$u, breaks = brk_u, plot = FALSE)
      dmax <- max(dmax, hu$density)
    }
    plot.new(); plot.window(xlim = c(dmax, 0), ylim = c(0, 1), xaxs = "i")
    if (length(rv$u) > 0)
      rect(hu$density, brk_u[-length(brk_u)], 0, brk_u[-1],
           col = "grey80", border = "white")
    abline(v = 1, col = "steelblue", lty = 2)
    mtext("hist of U", side = 3, line = 1.2, cex = 0.8)
    mtext("1", side = 3, at = 1, line = 0.1, cex = 0.7, col = "steelblue")

    ## (2) transformation plot; no bottom or left margin, so the X histogram
    ## hangs directly from its x axis and the U histogram from its left
    ## edge; the u axis is drawn on the right
    par(mar = c(0, 0, 3, 4))
    plot(g, yvals, type = "n", xlim = xl, ylim = c(0, 1), xaxt = "n",
         yaxt = "n", xlab = "", ylab = "", main = main)
    axis(1, labels = FALSE); axis(4)
    mtext(ylab, side = 4, line = 2.5)
    u <- rv$u_last; x <- rv$x_last
    if (length(u) > 0) {
      xc <- pmin(x, xl[2])
      segments(xl[1], u, xc, u, col = "grey65")
      inside <- x <= xl[2]
      segments(x[inside], u[inside], x[inside], par("usr")[3], col = "grey65")
    }
    lines(g, yvals, col = "steelblue", lwd = 2.5,
          type = if (disc) "s" else "l")
    if (length(u) > 0) {
      points(xc, u, pch = 16, col = "firebrick", cex = 1.1)
      points(rep(xl[1], length(u)), u, pch = 16, col = "grey35", cex = 0.8)
    }

    ## (3) histogram of X, upside down, sharing the x range of panel (2)
    par(mar = c(4, 0, 0, 4))
    ylab_x <- if (disc) "proportion" else "density"
    if (length(rv$x) < 2) {
      plot.new(); plot.window(xlim = xl, ylim = c(1, 0))
      box(); axis(1); title(xlab = "x"); mtext(ylab_x, side = 4, line = 2.5)
      text(mean(xl), 0.5, "Draw some samples to see the histogram of x", col = "grey40")
    } else {
      hx   <- hist(rv$x, breaks = D()$hist_breaks(), plot = FALSE)
      kde  <- if (!disc) kde_bounded(rv$x, D()$support[1], D()$support[2], xl)
      ymax <- 1.05 * max(hx$density, if (!disc) kde$y, D()$fmax)
      if (!is.null(D()$ycap)) ymax <- min(ymax, D()$ycap)
      plot.new(); plot.window(xlim = xl, ylim = c(ymax, 0), yaxs = "i")
      rect(hx$breaks[-length(hx$breaks)], 0, hx$breaks[-1], hx$density,
           col = "grey85", border = "white")
      D()$dens()
      if (!disc) lines(kde, col = "darkorange", lwd = 2)
      abline(v = mean(rv$x), col = "firebrick", lwd = 2, lty = 2)
      ## omit the 0 label, which would collide with the u = 0 label above
      at <- pretty(c(0, ymax)); at <- at[at > 0 & at <= ymax]
      box(); axis(1); axis(4, at = at)
      title(xlab = "x"); mtext(ylab_x, side = 4, line = 2.5)
    }

    ## (4) legend in the empty bottom-left cell
    par(mar = c(4, 0.5, 0, 0))
    plot.new()
    legend("center", bty = "n", cex = 0.85, lwd = 2, seg.len = 1.5,
           lty = if (disc) c(1, 2) else c(1, 1, 2),
           col = if (disc) c("steelblue", "firebrick")
                 else c("steelblue", "darkorange", "firebrick"),
           legend = if (disc) c("true pmf", "sample\nmean")
                    else c("true\ndensity", "kernel\ndensity", "sample\nmean"),
           y.intersp = 1.6)
  })
}

library(latex2exp)

d <- 5

log_f <- function(th, d) {
    a <- dnorm(th, -d, log = TRUE); b <- dnorm(th, d, log = TRUE)
    m <- pmax(a, b)
    m + log(exp(a - m) + exp(b - m)) - log(2)
}

log_Ew2 <- function(d, sg) {
    A <- 2 - 1 / sg^2
    if (A <= 0) return(Inf)
    lterm <- function(a, b) {
        m <- (a + b) / 2
        B <- 2 * m + d / sg^2
        C <- 2 * m^2 - d^2 / sg^2
        dnorm(a, b, sqrt(2), log = TRUE) + log(sg) + 0.5 * log(2) +
            0.5 * log(2 * pi / A) - 0.5 * (C - B^2 / A)
    }
    lv <- c(lterm(-d, -d), log(2) + lterm(-d, d), lterm(d, d))
    m  <- max(lv)
    m + log(sum(exp(lv - m))) - log(4)
}

ui <- fluidPage(
    wellPanel(
        fluidRow(
            column(4, sliderInput("sg", HTML("proposal sd σ"), min = 0.25, max = 8,
                                  value = 1, step = 0.05)),
            column(4, sliderInput("S", "sample size  S", min = 100, max = 20000,
                                  value = 2000, step = 100)),
            column(2, numericInput("seed", "seed", value = 11, min = 1, step = 1)),
            column(2, br(), actionButton("new", "New sample")))
    ),
    fluidRow(
        column(8, plotOutput("panels", height = "600px")),
        column(4,
            tags$style("#tab td, #tab th { white-space: nowrap; }"),
            h5("Estimates"),
            tableOutput("tab"))
    )
)

server <- function(input, output) {

    sim <- reactive({
        S  <- as.integer(input$S); sg <- input$sg
        set.seed(input$seed + 1000 * input$new)

        th   <- rnorm(S, -d, sg)
        logw <- log_f(th, d) - dnorm(th, -d, sg, log = TRUE)
        mx   <- max(logw); v <- exp(logw - mx)
        wn   <- v / sum(v)

        list(th = th, wn = wn, S = S, sg = sg,
             Chat = mean(v) * exp(mx),
             se   = sd(v) / sqrt(S) * exp(mx),
             ess  = 1 / sum(wn^2),
             Ehat = sum(wn * th),
             lsum = mx + log(sum(v)),
             ess_x = 100 * exp(-log_Ew2(d, sg)))
    })

    output$panels <- renderPlot({
        s  <- sim(); th <- s$th; sg <- s$sg
        xr <- c(-15, 15)                                  # fixed x-axis
        xs <- seq(xr[1], xr[2], length.out = 1000)
        fx <- exp(log_f(xs, d)); gx <- dnorm(xs, -d, sg)
        lwc <- log_f(xs, d) - dnorm(xs, -d, sg, log = TRUE) - s$lsum

        layout(matrix(1:2, 2), heights = c(3, 2))

        par(mar = c(0.4, 5, 3, 1))
        plot(xs, fx, type = "n", ylim = c(0, max(fx, gx) * 1.1), xlim = xr, xaxt = "n",
             xlab = "", ylab = "density",
             main = "bimodal target and a proposal centred on one mode")
        lines(xs, fx, lwd = 4, col = "red")
        lines(xs, gx, lwd = 3, col = "grey60")
        rug(th, col = adjustcolor("grey45", 0.35))
        legend("top", bty = "n", cex = 1.05, text.col = "navy",
               lwd = c(4, 3), col = c("red", "grey60"),
               legend = TeX(c(
                   r"(target $f$)",
                   sprintf(r"(proposal $g$, sd $= %.2f$)", sg))))

        par(mar = c(4.5, 5, 0.4, 1))
        wn <- s$wn
        wl <- c(min(wn) / 5, max(wn) * 5)
        plot(th, wn, type = "n", log = "y", ylim = wl, xlim = xr,
             xlab = expression(theta), ylab = "normalized weight (log scale)")
        lines(xs, exp(pmin(lwc, 700)), lwd = 2, col = "grey25")
        segments(th, wl[1], th, wn, col = adjustcolor("grey45", 0.5))
        abline(h = 1 / s$S, lty = 2, col = "grey55", lwd = 2)
        legend("bottomright", bty = "n", cex = 1.05, text.col = "navy",
               lty = c(2, 1), lwd = c(2, 2), col = c("grey55", "grey25"),
               legend = TeX(c(r"($1/S$)", r"(normalized weight function)")))
    })

    output$tab <- renderTable({
        s <- sim()
        data.frame(
            Quantity = c("C_f / C_g", "95% CI for C_f / C_g", "E_f(theta)", "observed ESS (% of S)",
                         "exact ESS (% of S)", "Var_f(w)"),
            True = c("1", "", "0", "", "", ""),
            Estimate = c(sprintf("%.4f", s$Chat),
                         sprintf("(%.4f, %.4f)", s$Chat - 1.96 * s$se, s$Chat + 1.96 * s$se),
                         sprintf("%.4f", s$Ehat),
                         sprintf("%.4g", 100 * s$ess / s$S),
                         sprintf("%.4g", s$ess_x),
                         if (s$sg <= 1 / sqrt(2)) "infinite" else "finite"))
    }, striped = TRUE, align = "lrr", width = "100%")
}

title: The Failure of Importance Sampling
text:
About the app
Illustrates how importance sampling can fail without warning when the proposal is too narrow to cover the target. The proposal’s standard deviation \(\sigma\) is under slider control and both panels are redrawn for each setting. For \(\sigma \le 1/\sqrt{2}\) the weight variance is infinite; near \(\sigma = 1\) the failure is silent, with the observed effective sample size close to \(S\) while the estimate of \(C_f/C_g\) sits at one half; past \(\sigma \approx 4\) the proposal reaches the second mode, the observed effective sample size falls, and the estimate moves onto the truth.
The target \(f\) and the proposal \(g\). The target is a normalized, equally weighted mixture of two unit-variance normals, with the modes at \(\pm d\) and \(d=5\), \[f(\theta)=\tfrac12\,N(\theta\mid -d,\,1)+\tfrac12\,N(\theta\mid d,\,1),\] and the proposal is a single normal centred on one of the modes, with the standard deviation \(\sigma\) set by the slider, \[g(\theta)=N(\theta\mid -d,\,\sigma^2).\] Draw \(\theta_1,\ldots,\theta_S\sim g\) and form the importance weights \(w_s=f(\theta_s)/g(\theta_s)\). Because both densities are normalized, \(C_f/C_g=1\), and \[\widehat{C_f/C_g}=\frac1S\sum_{s=1}^S w_s,\qquad \widehat{E_f(\theta)}=\frac{\sum_s w_s\theta_s}{\sum_s w_s},\] with true values \(1\) and \(0\). The 95% interval for \(C_f/C_g\) is \(\hat C\pm1.96\,s_w/\sqrt S\), where \(s_w\) is the sample standard deviation of the weights. The quality of the draws is summarized by the effective sample size \(S_{\text{eff}}=1/\sum_s\tilde w_s^2\) with \(\tilde w_s=w_s/\sum_j w_j\), reported as a percentage of \(S\) (“observed”), and by its exact value \(S/E_g(w^2)\). The second moment \(E_g(w^2)=\int f^2/g\) is finite only when \(\sigma>1/\sqrt2\), so for smaller \(\sigma\) the weight variance is infinite. The sample size \(S\), the seed and a new sample are set in the control panel at the top; the estimates are listed in a table to the right of the plots, and the horizontal axis of both plots is fixed at \([-15,15]\). The top plot shows \(f\) and \(g\) on the density scale, and the bottom plot the normalized weights of the draws (log scale), with the dashed line at \(1/S\) marking perfectly balanced weights.
The app above varies \(\sigma\) with everything else held fixed. Three regimes appear. Below \(\sigma=1/\sqrt{2}\) the variance is infinite and the exact effective fraction is reported as zero. Between there and roughly \(\sigma=3\) the failure is silent in the sense above: observed \(S_{\text{eff}}\) near \(S\), estimate near \(\tfrac12\). Past \(\sigma\approx4\) the proposal is over-dispersed enough to place draws near \(+d\); the observed \(S_{\text{eff}}\) then drops, which looks like deterioration and is in fact the diagnostic finally working, and the estimate moves onto the truth. The cure for a missed mode is a proposal that is too diffuse rather than too well matched.

log_sum_exp <- function(lx) { mx <- max(lx); mx + log(sum(exp(lx - mx))) }

log_like_obs <- function(theta, Y) {
    A <- cbind(log(theta[1])     + dnorm(Y, theta[2], 1, log = TRUE),
               log(1 - theta[1]) + dnorm(Y, theta[3], 1, log = TRUE))
    sum(apply(A, 1, log_sum_exp))
}

e_step <- function(theta, Y) {
    l1 <- dnorm(Y, theta[2], 1, log = TRUE) + log(theta[1])
    l0 <- dnorm(Y, theta[3], 1, log = TRUE) + log(1 - theta[1])
    exp(l1 - apply(cbind(l1, l0), 1, log_sum_exp))
}

m_step <- function(w, Y) {
    c(mean(w), sum(Y * w) / sum(w), sum(Y * (1 - w)) / sum(1 - w))
}

em_path <- function(theta0, Y, no_iters) {
    out <- matrix(NA_real_, no_iters + 1, 4,
                  dimnames = list(NULL, c("p", "mu1", "mu0", "log_lik")))
    th <- theta0
    out[1, ] <- c(th, log_like_obs(th, Y))
    for (i in seq_len(no_iters)) {
        th <- m_step(e_step(th, Y), Y)
        if (any(!is.finite(th))) break
        out[i + 1, ] <- c(th, log_like_obs(th, Y))
    }
    out
}

### ---------- server -----------------------------------------------------------
server <- function(input, output, session) {

    seed <- reactiveVal(812)
    observeEvent(input$newdata, seed(seed() + 1))

    Y <- reactive({
        req(input$n)
        s <- datasets[[input$dataset]]
        set.seed(seed())
        Z <- rbinom(input$n, 1, s[1])
        rnorm(input$n, mean = ifelse(Z == 1, s[2], s[3]), sd = 1)
    })

    ## vertical jitter for the points drawn along the bottom of the plot (fixed for a data set)
    jit <- reactive({
        n <- length(Y())
        set.seed(seed() + 1000)
        runif(n, 0.01, 0.07)
    })

    ## preset -> fill the three boxes
    ## "Regenerate starting value" draws a new random-labels start
    observeEvent(input$newstart, {
        if (input$preset != "random labels")
            updateSelectInput(session, "preset", selected = "random labels")
    })

    observeEvent(list(input$preset, input$dataset, input$n, seed(), input$newstart), {
        pr <- presets[[input$preset]]
        if (is.null(pr)) return(invisible(NULL))          # manual entry
        if (length(pr) == 1 && is.na(pr)) {               # random labels
            y <- Y()
            set.seed(NULL)                                # Y() fixes the seed; draw a fresh start
            repeat {
                lab <- rbinom(length(y), 1, 0.5)
                if (any(lab == 1) && any(lab == 0)) break
            }
            pr <- c(0.5, mean(y[lab == 1]), mean(y[lab == 0]))
        }
        updateNumericInput(session, "p0",   value = round(pr[1], 3))
        updateNumericInput(session, "mu10", value = round(pr[2], 3))
        updateNumericInput(session, "mu00", value = round(pr[3], 3))
    }, ignoreInit = FALSE)

    ## ---- iteration state driven by the three buttons ----------------------
    t_cur   <- reactiveVal(0)      # iteration currently displayed
    playing <- reactiveVal(FALSE)

    stop_play <- function() {
        playing(FALSE)
        updateActionButton(session, "play", label = "Play")
    }

    ## any change to the data or the starting value restarts the fit
    observeEvent(list(input$dataset, input$n, seed(), input$maxit,
                      input$p0, input$mu10, input$mu00), {
        t_cur(0)
        stop_play()
    })

    observeEvent(input$nxt, {
        stop_play()
        t_cur(min(t_cur() + 1, input$maxit))
    })

    observeEvent(input$prv, {
        stop_play()
        t_cur(max(t_cur() - 1, 0))
    })

    observeEvent(input$play, {
        if (playing()) {
            stop_play()
        } else {
            if (t_cur() >= input$maxit) t_cur(0)   # replay from the start
            playing(TRUE)
            updateActionButton(session, "play", label = "Pause")
        }
    })

    ## the timer: advances one iteration per tick while playing
    observe({
        if (!playing()) return(NULL)
        invalidateLater(700, session)
        isolate({
            if (t_cur() >= input$maxit) stop_play() else t_cur(t_cur() + 1)
        })
    })

    output$stepLabel <- renderText(
        sprintf("Iteration %d of %d", t_cur(), input$maxit)
    )

    theta0 <- reactive({
        p <- input$p0
        validate(need(is.finite(p) && p > 0 && p < 1, "p must lie strictly between 0 and 1"),
                 need(is.finite(input$mu10) && is.finite(input$mu00),
                      "both means must be numeric"))
        c(p, input$mu10, input$mu00)
    })

    path <- reactive({
        req(input$maxit)
        em_path(theta0(), Y(), input$maxit)
    })

    output$fit <- renderPlot({
        y <- Y(); P <- path()
        k  <- min(t_cur() + 1, nrow(P))
        th <- P[k, 1:3]
        validate(need(all(is.finite(th)), "the iteration broke down numerically"))
        w  <- e_step(th, y)
        cw <- cm.colors(100)

        xr <- range(y, th[2:3]) + c(-2, 2)
        xg <- seq(xr[1], xr[2], length.out = 400)
        d1 <- dnorm(xg, th[2]) * th[1]
        d0 <- dnorm(xg, th[3]) * (1 - th[1])

        par(mar = c(4, 4, 3, 1))
        plot(xg, d1, type = "l", lwd = 2, col = cw[100],
             ylim = c(0, max(0.42, d1 + d0)), xlab = "y", ylab = "weighted density",
             main = sprintf("step %d:  p = %.2f,  mu1 = %.2f,  mu0 = %.2f,  loglik = %.1f",
                            k - 1, th[1], th[2], th[3], P[k, 4]))
        lines(xg, d0, lwd = 2, col = cw[1])
        lines(xg, d1 + d0, lwd = 2, col = "black")
        points(y, jit(), col = cw[pmax(1, ceiling(w * 100))], pch = 19,
               cex = 0.7)
        if (k < nrow(P) && all(is.finite(P[k + 1, 1:3]))) {
            arrows(th[2], 0.09, P[k + 1, 2], 0.09, length = 0.08, lwd = 2, col = cw[100])
            arrows(th[3], 0.09, P[k + 1, 3], 0.09, length = 0.08, lwd = 2, col = cw[1])
        }
        legend("topright", bty = "n", lwd = 2, col = c(cw[100], cw[1], "black"),
               legend = c(expression(hat(p) * phi(y * "|" * hat(mu)[1])),
                          expression((1 - hat(p)) * phi(y * "|" * hat(mu)[0])),
                          "mixture density"))
    })

    output$trace <- renderPlot({
        P <- path(); k <- min(t_cur() + 1, nrow(P))
        par(mfrow = c(1, 2), mar = c(4, 4, 2, 1))
        it <- 0:(nrow(P) - 1)
        plot(it, P[, 4], type = "n", xlab = "iteration",
             ylab = "observed log-likelihood", main = "must never decrease")
        lines(it[1:k], P[1:k, 4], type = "b", pch = 19, col = "firebrick")
        yl <- range(P[, 2:3], na.rm = TRUE)
        plot(it, P[, 2], type = "n", ylim = yl, xlab = "iteration",
             ylab = "component means", main = "parameter paths")
        lines(it[1:k], P[1:k, 2], type = "b", pch = 19, col = "firebrick")
        lines(it[1:k], P[1:k, 3], type = "b", pch = 19, col = "steelblue")
        legend("right", bty = "n", lwd = 2, col = c("firebrick", "steelblue"),
               legend = c(expression(hat(mu)[1]), expression(hat(mu)[0])))
    })

    output$tab <- renderTable({
        P <- path(); k <- min(t_cur() + 1, nrow(P))
        d <- as.data.frame(P[seq_len(k), , drop = FALSE])
        d$iter <- seq_len(k) - 1
        tail(d[, c("iter", "p", "mu1", "mu0", "log_lik")], 5)
    }, digits = 4, rownames = FALSE)
}

title: The EM Algorithm for a Normal Mixture
text:
About the app
Lets you watch the EM algorithm fit a two-component normal mixture, showing how the estimates and the likelihood evolve from iteration to iteration. The app above replaces the frame-by-frame animation of earlier versions of this chapter.
Choose a data set and a starting value — either from the presets in the left panel or by typing your own — then step through the fit with Prev and Next, or press Play to run it automatically. Regenerate data draws a fresh sample from the same model, which is the quickest way to see how much of the algorithm’s behaviour is a property of the model and how much is an accident of one data set. Changing the data, the sample size or any starting value resets the display to iteration 0.
Upper panel: the two weighted component densities, with each observation coloured by its current responsibility \(\hat p_i^{(t)}\) and arrows showing where the M-step moves the two means. Lower panel: the observed log-likelihood, which must never decrease.
Four behaviours are worth producing deliberately.
Slow drift from a distant start. With \((0.5, -10, 5)\) both means begin far outside the data. The early iterations move them very little, because every observation is assigned almost the same responsibility; progress accelerates only once one mean reaches the data.
Label switching. The starts \((0.5, 0, 3)\) and \((0.5, 3, 0)\) converge to the same fitted mixture with the roles of the two components exchanged. The likelihood is invariant to this relabelling, so the fitted density is identical while the parameter estimates differ — a genuine identifiability problem for the model, not a defect of the algorithm.
Stalling at a symmetric point. With \(\mu_1^{(0)} = 0.1\) and \(\mu_0^{(0)} = 0.2\) the two components are nearly indistinguishable, every responsibility is close to \(\hat p^{(0)}\), and the algorithm creeps away from the one-component solution very slowly. That configuration is close to a saddle point of \(\ell_{\text{obs}}\).
Separation and speed. Switch the data set from \(\mu = (1.5, 0)\) to \(\mu = (5, 0)\). Well-separated components make the responsibilities nearly \(0\) or \(1\), the E-step becomes almost a hard classification, and convergence takes a handful of iterations rather than dozens. This is the practical face of the general result that EM’s linear convergence rate is governed by the fraction of missing information.

library(shiny)

### renderPlot replacement: Safari 27 (WebKit) cannot hold the call stack of
### shiny::renderPlot in webR ("Maximum call stack size exceeded"), so draw with
### renderImage instead, which nests about 45 fewer R calls
renderPlot <- function(expr, width = "auto", height = "auto", res = 72, ...,
                       env = parent.frame(), quoted = FALSE) {
    func <- shiny::exprToFunction(expr, env, quoted)
    shiny::renderImage({
        info <- shiny::getCurrentOutputInfo()
        w  <- if (is.numeric(width))  width  else info$width()
        h  <- if (is.numeric(height)) height else info$height()
        shiny::req(w > 0, h > 0)
        pr <- shiny::getDefaultReactiveDomain()$clientData$pixelratio
        if (is.null(pr)) pr <- 1
        f   <- tempfile(fileext = ".png")
        dev <- shiny:::startPNG(f, w * pr, h * pr, res = res * pr)
        on.exit(grDevices::dev.off(dev), add = TRUE)
        grDevices::dev.control(displaylist = "enable")
        v <- withVisible(func())
        if (v$visible) print(v$value)
        list(src = f, contentType = "image/png", width = w, height = h,
             coordmap = shiny:::getCoordmap(v$value, w * pr, h * pr, res * pr))
    }, deleteFile = TRUE)
}

               cex = 0.7)
        if (k < nrow(P) && all(is.finite(P[k + 1, 1:3]))) {
            arrows(th[2], 0.09, P[k + 1, 2], 0.09, length = 0.08, lwd = 2, col = cw[100])
            arrows(th[3], 0.09, P[k + 1, 3], 0.09, length = 0.08, lwd = 2, col = cw[1])
        }
        legend("topright", bty = "n", lwd = 2, col = c(cw[100], cw[1], "black"),
               legend = c(expression(hat(p) * phi(y * "|" * hat(mu)[1])),
                          expression((1 - hat(p)) * phi(y * "|" * hat(mu)[0])),
                          "mixture density"))
    })

    output$trace <- renderPlot({
        P <- path(); k <- min(t_cur() + 1, nrow(P))
        par(mfrow = c(1, 2), mar = c(4, 4, 2, 1))
        it <- 0:(nrow(P) - 1)
        plot(it, P[, 4], type = "n", xlab = "iteration",
             ylab = "observed log-likelihood", main = "must never decrease")
        lines(it[1:k], P[1:k, 4], type = "b", pch = 19, col = "firebrick")
        yl <- range(P[, 2:3], na.rm = TRUE)
        plot(it, P[, 2], type = "n", ylim = yl, xlab = "iteration",
             ylab = "component means", main = "parameter paths")
        lines(it[1:k], P[1:k, 2], type = "b", pch = 19, col = "firebrick")
        lines(it[1:k], P[1:k, 3], type = "b", pch = 19, col = "steelblue")
        legend("right", bty = "n", lwd = 2, col = c("firebrick", "steelblue"),
               legend = c(expression(hat(mu)[1]), expression(hat(mu)[0])))
    })

    output$tab <- renderTable({
        P <- path(); k <- min(t_cur() + 1, nrow(P))
        d <- as.data.frame(P[seq_len(k), , drop = FALSE])
        d$iter <- seq_len(k) - 1
        tail(d[, c("iter", "p", "mu1", "mu0", "log_lik")], 5)
    }, digits = 4, rownames = FALSE)
}

### renderPlot replacement: Safari 27 (WebKit) cannot hold the call stack of
### shiny::renderPlot in webR ("Maximum call stack size exceeded"), so draw with
### renderImage instead, which nests about 45 fewer R calls
renderPlot <- function(expr, width = "auto", height = "auto", res = 72, ...,
                       env = parent.frame(), quoted = FALSE) {
    func <- shiny::exprToFunction(expr, env, quoted)
    shiny::renderImage({
        info <- shiny::getCurrentOutputInfo()
        w  <- if (is.numeric(width))  width  else info$width()
        h  <- if (is.numeric(height)) height else info$height()
        shiny::req(w > 0, h > 0)
        pr <- shiny::getDefaultReactiveDomain()$clientData$pixelratio
        if (is.null(pr)) pr <- 1
        f   <- tempfile(fileext = ".png")
        dev <- shiny:::startPNG(f, w * pr, h * pr, res = res * pr)
        on.exit(grDevices::dev.off(dev), add = TRUE)
        grDevices::dev.control(displaylist = "enable")
        v <- withVisible(func())
        if (v$visible) print(v$value)
        list(src = f, contentType = "image/png", width = w, height = h,
             coordmap = shiny:::getCoordmap(v$value, w * pr, h * pr, res * pr))
    }, deleteFile = TRUE)
}

## ------------------------------------------------------------------- model
## One covariate x, four tanh hidden units, log link, Poisson counts:
##   a_j = w_j1 x + w_j0,  h_j = tanh(a_j),  eta = v_0 + sum_j v_j h_j,
##   lambda = exp(eta).
## The data come from four units; the fitted network has J >= 4 units (chosen in the app).
## theta = (w11..wJ1,  w10..wJ0,  v1..vJ,  v0), so p = 3 J + 1 weights
nunits <- function(th) (length(th) - 1) %/% 3
## two bumps in the mean: units 1, 2 switch on and off over (-2.2, -0.8),
## units 3, 4 over (0.8, 2.2), so lambda(x) has two modes
TRUE_THETA <- c(2.5, 2.5, 2.5, 2.5,   5.5, 2, -2, -5.5,   1.2, -1.2, 1.0, -1.0,   -0.5)

## the same function as a network of J units: units 5 to J get output weight 0, and
## fixed random input weights (with zero input weights too they could never move)
embed_theta <- function(th4, J) {
  if (J <= 4) return(th4)
  set.seed(77); e <- J - 4
  c(th4[1:4], rnorm(e), th4[5:8], rnorm(e), th4[9:12], rep(0, e), th4[13])
}

fwd <- function(th, x) {
  J <- nunits(th)
  H <- tanh(outer(x, th[1:J]) + rep(th[J + 1:J], each = length(x)))
  list(H = H, eta = as.vector(th[3 * J + 1] + H %*% th[2 * J + 1:J]))
}
lambda_fun <- function(th, x) exp(fwd(th, x)$eta)

## the scaled units v_j h_j(x), one column per hidden unit
unit_terms <- function(th, x) { J <- nunits(th); sweep(fwd(th, x)$H, 2, th[2 * J + 1:J], "*") }

## average Poisson negative log-likelihood, with the log y! term: it does not depend on
## the weights, but without it the training and test losses would differ by a constant
nll <- function(th, x, y) {
  e <- fwd(th, x)$eta
  v <- mean(exp(e) - y * e + lfactorial(y))
  if (is.finite(v)) v else Inf
}

## its gradient by backpropagation:  delta_eta -> delta_a -> weights
nll_grad <- function(th, x, y) {
  J <- nunits(th)
  E <- fwd(th, x)
  d_eta <- exp(E$eta) - y                                   # n
  d_a   <- (1 - E$H^2) * outer(d_eta, th[2 * J + 1:J])      # n x J
  c(colSums(d_a * x),                                       # w_j1
    colSums(d_a),                                           # w_j0
    as.vector(crossprod(E$H, d_eta)),                       # v_j
    sum(d_eta)) / length(x)                                 # v_0
}

## the L1 penalty lambda * sum |w| applies to the weights w_j1 and v_j, not to the intercepts
pen_mask <- function(th) { J <- nunits(th); r <- rep(1, length(th)); r[c(J + 1:J, 3 * J + 1)] <- 0; r }

make_data <- function(n, seed) {
  set.seed(100 + seed)
  x <- runif(n, -3, 3)
  y <- rpois(n, lambda_fun(TRUE_THETA, x))
  ## a fixed vertical offset, drawn once with the data, so the points stay put
  list(x = x, y = y, yj = y + runif(n, -0.12, 0.12))
}

## random starting weights: the output weights v_j have sd 2 / sqrt(J), so the
## starting curve has about the same size whatever the number of units
rand_start <- function(seed, J) {
  set.seed(2000 + seed)
  c(rnorm(2 * J), rnorm(J, 0, 2 / sqrt(J)), 0)
}

## ------------------------------------------------------- Wolfe line search
line_search <- function(f, g, x, d, a0 = 1, c1 = 1e-4, c2 = 0.9) {
  f0 <- f(x); gd0 <- sum(g(x) * d)
  if (!is.finite(gd0) || gd0 >= 0) return(list(alpha = 0, ok = FALSE))
  lo <- 0; hi <- Inf; a <- a0
  for (it in 1:60) {
    fa <- f(x + a * d)
    if (!is.finite(fa) || fa > f0 + c1 * a * gd0) {
      hi <- a; a <- 0.5 * (lo + hi)
    } else {
      if (sum(g(x + a * d) * d) < c2 * gd0) {
        lo <- a
        a <- if (is.finite(hi)) 0.5 * (lo + hi) else min(2 * a, 1e4)
      } else {
        return(list(alpha = a, ok = TRUE))
      }
    }
    if (a < 1e-14) return(list(alpha = 0, ok = FALSE))
  }
  list(alpha = a, ok = (a > 0))
}

## ------------------------------------------------------------- algorithms
## the methods that step through mini-batches: one iteration is one epoch
MINIBATCH <- c("sgdls", "sgdls2", "mom", "adam")
## Row k of P (the weights), and element k of F (the objective), L (the loss
## without the penalty) and GN (the gradient norm), is the state after k - 1 steps;
## A[k] is the step length that led to it. The objective is the loss plus the L1
## penalty lam * sum |w|, whose gradient is taken as lam * sign(w) (a subgradient).
run_alg <- function(alg, th0, x, y, maxit, lr = 0.1, mom = 0.9, m = 20,
                    tol = 1e-6, patience = Inf, rtol = 1e-5, lmem = 10, lam = 0) {
  p <- length(th0)
  pm <- lam * pen_mask(th0)
  f <- function(th) nll(th, x, y) + sum(pm * abs(th))
  g <- function(th) nll_grad(th, x, y) + pm * sign(th)
  n <- 0; note <- "maximum number of iterations reached"
  if (alg == "bfgs" && p > 2000) {           # B alone would take p^2 numbers
    return(list(P = matrix(th0, 1), F = f(th0), L = nll(th0, x, y),
                GN = sqrt(sum(g(th0)^2)), A = NA_real_, n = 1,
                note = paste0("BFGS not run: its p x p matrix would hold ",
                              format(p^2, big.mark = ","), " numbers (p = ", p,
                              "); use L-BFGS")))
  }
  ## state for the fixed-rate rules
  n_obs <- length(x); m <- max(1, min(m, n_obs))
  capped <- FALSE
  if (alg %in% MINIBATCH) {                  # keep the number of mini-batch steps in check
    cap <- max(1, floor(100000 / ceiling(n_obs / m)))
    if (maxit > cap) { maxit <- cap; capped <- TRUE }
  }
  stored <- FALSE                            # keep the stored path to 4 million numbers
  if ((maxit + 1) * p > 4e6) { maxit <- floor(4e6 / p) - 1; stored <- TRUE }
  P <- matrix(NA_real_, maxit + 1, p)
  Fv <- Lv <- GN <- AL <- rep(NA_real_, maxit + 1)
  th <- th0; B <- if (alg == "bfgs") diag(p) else NULL
  g_prev <- d_prev <- s_prev <- NULL
  Sh <- Yh <- list()                          # the stored pairs of L-BFGS
  best_f <- Inf; best_k <- 1                  # the best loss so far, and when it was reached
  vel <- m1 <- m2 <- numeric(p)              # momentum velocity; Adam moments
  a_prev <- lr / 2; nrej <- 0; nsteps <- 0     # the independent-batch line search
  tt <- 0                                    # mini-batch updates so far (Adam)
  if (alg %in% MINIBATCH) set.seed(11)

  for (k in 1:(maxit + 1)) {
    gk <- g(th); lk <- nll(th, x, y); fk <- lk + sum(pm * abs(th))
    P[k, ] <- th; GN[k] <- sqrt(sum(gk^2)); Fv[k] <- fk; Lv[k] <- lk; n <- k
    if (!is.finite(fk) || !all(is.finite(gk))) { note <- "diverged"; break }
    if (tol > 0 && sqrt(sum(gk^2)) < tol) {
      note <- paste0("converged: gradient norm < ", format(tol)); break
    }
    ## no stopping rule can be exact for a noisy method, so every method also stops when the
    ## full-data loss has not improved by a fraction rtol for `patience` iterations
    if (k == 1 || fk < best_f - rtol * abs(best_f)) { best_f <- fk; best_k <- k }
    if (k - best_k >= patience) {
      note <- paste0("stopped: the loss has not improved by ", 100 * rtol, "% in ",
                     patience, " iterations"); break
    }
    if (k > maxit) break

    if (alg == "gdfix") {                    # full-batch gradient, fixed learning rate
      AL[k + 1] <- lr
      th <- th - lr * gk
      next
    }

    if (alg %in% MINIBATCH) {                # one iteration is one epoch: a shuffled pass
      perm <- sample.int(n_obs)              # of mini-batch steps over all the data, so
      al <- numeric(0)                       # it costs about one full-batch gradient
      for (s0 in seq(1, n_obs, by = m)) {
        idx <- perm[s0:min(s0 + m - 1, n_obs)]
        xb <- x[idx]; yb <- y[idx]
        gb <- nll_grad(th, xb, yb) + pm * sign(th)   # the gradient of mini-batch B_k
        if (alg == "sgdls") {                # backtracking line search on the batch objective
          fb <- nll(th, xb, yb) + sum(pm * abs(th)); a <- lr; gg <- sum(gb^2)
          for (j in 1:30) {
            fa <- nll(th - a * gb, xb, yb) + sum(pm * abs(th - a * gb))
            if (is.finite(fa) && fa <= fb - 1e-4 * a * gg) break
            a <- a / 2
          }
          al <- c(al, a)
          th <- th - a * gb
        } else if (alg == "sgdls2") {          # the same search, judged on an independent batch C:
          ic <- sample.int(n_obs, length(idx))  # the step is checked on cases it was not fitted to,
          xc <- x[ic]; yc <- y[ic]              # with the same cases at both points (a paired estimate)
          fc <- nll(th, xc, yc) + sum(pm * abs(th)); gg <- sum(gb^2)
          a <- min(2 * a_prev, 1e3); ok <- FALSE  # start from twice the last accepted step
          for (j in 1:30) {
            fa <- nll(th - a * gb, xc, yc) + sum(pm * abs(th - a * gb))
            if (is.finite(fa) && fa <= fc - 1e-4 * a * gg) { ok <- TRUE; break }
            a <- a / 2
          }
          nsteps <- nsteps + 1
          if (ok) { th <- th - a * gb; a_prev <- a; al <- c(al, a) } else nrej <- nrej + 1
        } else if (alg == "mom") {           # heavy ball on the batch gradient
          vel <- mom * vel - lr * gb
          th <- th + vel
        } else {                             # Adam on the batch gradient
          tt <- tt + 1
          m1 <- 0.9 * m1 + 0.1 * gb
          m2 <- 0.999 * m2 + 0.001 * gb^2
          th <- th - lr * (m1 / (1 - 0.9^tt)) / (sqrt(m2 / (1 - 0.999^tt)) + 1e-8)
        }
      }
      AL[k + 1] <- if (alg %in% c("sgdls", "sgdls2")) (if (length(al)) mean(al) else 0) else lr
      next
    }

    if (alg == "gd") {
      d <- -gk
    } else if (alg == "cg") {
      if (is.null(d_prev)) {
        d <- -gk
      } else {
        yk <- gk - g_prev
        beta <- max(0, sum(gk * yk) / max(sum(g_prev^2), 1e-300))   # PR+
        d <- -gk + beta * d_prev
      }
      if (sum(gk * d) > -1e-12) d <- -gk                           # restart
    } else if (alg == "lbfgs") {                                   # L-BFGS: two-loop recursion
      if (!is.null(s_prev)) {
        yk <- gk - g_prev; sy <- sum(s_prev * yk)
        if (sy > 1e-10) {
          Sh <- c(Sh, list(s_prev)); Yh <- c(Yh, list(yk))
          if (length(Sh) > lmem) { Sh <- Sh[-1]; Yh <- Yh[-1] }
        }
      }
      q <- gk; nh <- length(Sh); al <- numeric(nh)
      for (i in rev(seq_len(nh))) {
        al[i] <- sum(Sh[[i]] * q) / sum(Yh[[i]] * Sh[[i]])
        q <- q - al[i] * Yh[[i]]
      }
      if (nh > 0) q <- q * sum(Sh[[nh]] * Yh[[nh]]) / sum(Yh[[nh]]^2)   # initial scaling
      for (i in seq_len(nh)) {
        be <- sum(Yh[[i]] * q) / sum(Yh[[i]] * Sh[[i]])
        q <- q + Sh[[i]] * (al[i] - be)
      }
      d <- -q
      if (sum(gk * d) > -1e-12) { Sh <- Yh <- list(); d <- -gk }
    } else {                                                       # BFGS
      if (!is.null(s_prev)) {
        yk <- gk - g_prev; sy <- sum(s_prev * yk)
        if (sy > 1e-10) {
          if (k == 2) B <- (sy / sum(yk^2)) * diag(p)    # scale the first B
          ## B <- (I - rho s y') B (I - rho y s') + rho s s', in O(p^2) operations
          rho <- 1 / sy; By <- as.vector(B %*% yk)
          B <- B + (rho^2 * (sy + sum(yk * By))) * outer(s_prev, s_prev) -
            rho * (outer(By, s_prev) + outer(s_prev, By))
        }
      }
      d <- -as.vector(B %*% gk)
      if (sum(gk * d) > -1e-12) { B <- diag(p); d <- -gk }
    }

    a0 <- if (alg %in% c("bfgs", "lbfgs") && k > 1) 1 else min(1, 1 / sqrt(sum(d^2)))
    ls <- line_search(f, g, th, d, a0)
    if (!ls$ok && alg != "gd") {             # restart from steepest descent before giving up
      d <- -gk; if (alg == "bfgs") B <- diag(p)
      d_prev <- s_prev <- g_prev <- NULL; Sh <- Yh <- list()
      ls <- line_search(f, g, th, d, min(1, 1 / sqrt(sum(d^2))))
    }
    if (!ls$ok) { note <- "line search failed"; break }
    AL[k + 1] <- ls$alpha
    s_prev <- ls$alpha * d; g_prev <- gk; d_prev <- d
    th <- th + s_prev
  }
  if (capped && grepl("^maximum", note))
    note <- paste0("stopped after ", maxit, " epochs (100000 mini-batch steps)")
  if (stored && grepl("^maximum", note))
    note <- paste0("stopped after ", maxit, " iterations, to keep the stored path of the ",
                   p, " weights within 4 million numbers")
  if (alg == "sgdls2" && nsteps > 0)
    note <- paste0(note, "; ", round(100 * nrej / nsteps), "% of the mini-batch steps were not ",
                   "taken (no sufficient decrease on the check batch)")
  i <- seq_len(n)
  list(P = P[i, , drop = FALSE], F = Fv[i], L = Lv[i], GN = GN[i],
       A = AL[i], n = n, note = note)
}

ALGS <- c("Gradient descent, fixed learning rate"     = "gdfix",
          "Gradient descent + line search"            = "gd",
          "Conjugate gradient (Polak-Ribiere+)"       = "cg",
          "BFGS (quasi-Newton)"                       = "bfgs",
          "L-BFGS (limited memory)"                   = "lbfgs",
          "SGD + line search (on each mini-batch)"    = "sgdls",
          "SGD + line search (on an independent batch)" = "sgdls2",
          "SGD + momentum"                            = "mom",
          "SGD + Adam"                                = "adam")

alg_name <- function(a) if (a == "none") "none" else names(ALGS)[ALGS == a]

## --------------------------------------------------------- network layout
## Weights sit on the edges; each intercept is a node of its own, a box with
## the value and its arrows, hung on the neuron it shifts. Only the first JS = 4
## hidden units are drawn, with vertical dots below them for any others. A slot is
## one drawn weight; show_idx(J) gives the position of each slot in theta.
JS <- 4
NPS <- 3 * JS + 1                                   # weights drawn
NAMES <- c(paste0("w", 1:JS, "1"), paste0("w", 1:JS, "0"), paste0("v", 1:JS), "v0")
BIASIDX <- c(JS + 1:JS, NPS)                        # the intercept slots
show_idx <- function(J) c(1:JS, J + 1:JS, 2 * J + 1:JS, 3 * J + 1)
NX <- c(0.07, 0.50)                                 # (x, y) of the input node
YH <- seq(0.88, 0.12, length.out = JS); XH <- 0.60  # hidden nodes
NO <- c(1.13, 0.50)                                 # output node
at <- function(p, q, f) p + f * (q - p)             # a point along an edge
## hidden intercepts hang above the upper half of the hidden nodes and below the rest
YB <- YH + rep(c(0.14, -0.14), each = JS / 2)
BIAS <- c(rep(0.56, JS), 1.00)                      # x of the intercept boxes
BIASY <- c(YB, 0.17)                                # y of the intercept boxes
## where each weight's value and arrows sit
ADJ <- local({
  hj <- lapply(1:JS, function(j) c(XH, YH[j]))
  pos <- c(lapply(1:JS, function(j) at(NX, hj[[j]], 0.50)),    # w_j1: x -> h_j
           lapply(1:JS, function(j) c(BIAS[j], BIASY[j])),     # w_j0: box on h_j
           lapply(1:JS, function(j) at(hj[[j]], NO, 0.50)),    # v_j: h_j -> out
           list(c(BIAS[JS + 1], BIASY[JS + 1])))              # v_0: box on output
  data.frame(idx = 1:NPS, sym = NAMES,
             x = sapply(pos, `[`, 1), y = sapply(pos, `[`, 2),
             stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
})
## the arrows beside each value (also the click targets): up / down beside an
## edge weight, left / right beside an intercept box
AX <- 0.104                                  # arrow offset from the value
isb <- ADJ$idx %in% BIASIDX
ARROWS <- rbind(
  data.frame(idx = ADJ$idx, dir = +1, horiz = isb,
             ax = ifelse(isb, ADJ$x + AX, ADJ$x + AX),
             ay = ifelse(isb, ADJ$y, ADJ$y + 0.028)),
  data.frame(idx = ADJ$idx, dir = -1, horiz = isb,
             ax = ifelse(isb, ADJ$x - AX, ADJ$x + AX),
             ay = ifelse(isb, ADJ$y, ADJ$y - 0.028)))

## ---------------------------------------------------------------- colours
## Diverging ramp: blue = negative, red = positive, depth by magnitude.
DIV <- colorRampPalette(c("#08306B", "#2171B5", "#6BAED6", "#DEEBF7",
                          "#F7F7F7",
                          "#FEE0D2", "#FC9272", "#CB181D", "#67000D"))(201)

## compander: maps v in [-vmax, vmax] to [-1, 1], boosting small values
tone <- function(v, vmax, k) {
  u <- pmax(-1, pmin(1, v / vmax))
  sign(u) * log1p(k * abs(u)) / log1p(k)
}
hcol <- function(v, vmax, k) DIV[round((tone(v, vmax, k) + 1) * 100) + 1]

## th is the full weight vector; the first JS units and v0 are drawn, and the
## other units, if any, are marked by vertical dots below unit JS
draw_net <- function(th, vmax, k, main, arrows = TRUE, digits = 2) {
  J <- nunits(th); more <- J - JS; v <- th[show_idx(J)]
  col <- hcol(v, vmax, k); lw <- 0.8 + 6 * abs(tone(v, vmax, k))
  yb <- if (more > 0) -0.17 else 0                  # the colour bar moves down for the dots
  plot.new(); plot.window(c(0, 1.2), c(-0.25 + yb, 1.08))
  title(main = main, cex.main = 1.05)
  H <- cbind(XH, YH)
  if (more > 0) {                                   # the units not drawn: faint edges and dots
    yd <- -0.14
    segments(NX[1], NX[2], XH, yd + 0.04, col = "grey75", lty = 2)
    segments(XH, yd + 0.04, NO[1], NO[2], col = "grey75", lty = 2)
    points(rep(XH, 3), yd + c(0.03, -0.01, -0.05), pch = 19, cex = 0.7)
    text(XH + 0.05, yd - 0.01, adj = 0, cex = 0.8, col = "grey25",
         sprintf("units %d to %d not shown (%d more)", JS + 1, J, more))
  }
  ## edges, each carrying one weight: x -> h_j (w_j1), h_j -> output (v_j)
  for (j in 1:JS) {
    segments(NX[1], NX[2], H[j, 1], H[j, 2], col = col[j],     lwd = lw[j],     lend = 1)
    segments(H[j, 1], H[j, 2], NO[1], NO[2], col = col[2 * JS + j], lwd = lw[2 * JS + j], lend = 1)
  }
  ## intercept nodes: a thin arrow from each box to the neuron it shifts
  tgt <- rbind(H, NO)
  for (i in seq_along(BIASIDX)) {
    b <- ADJ[BIASIDX[i], ]
    dy <- sign(tgt[i, 2] - b$y)
    if (i == JS + 1) arrows(b$x, b$y + 0.03, NO[1] - 0.03, NO[2] - 0.03, length = 0.08,
                       col = "grey45", lwd = 1.4)
    else arrows(b$x, b$y + dy * 0.035, tgt[i, 1], tgt[i, 2] - dy * 0.035,
                length = 0.08, col = "grey45", lwd = 1.4)
  }
  ## nodes
  points(rbind(NX, H, NO), pch = 21, cex = 3.2, bg = "white", lwd = 1.6)
  text(NX[1], NX[2], "x", font = 2)
  text(H[, 1], H[, 2], paste0("h", 1:JS), cex = 0.8)
  text(NO[1], NO[2], expression(lambda), cex = 1.1)
  ## values: an intercept is a box coloured by its value; an edge weight is
  ## plain text on a white patch so the edge does not strike through it
  for (i in 1:NPS) {
    b <- ADJ[i, ]; isb <- i %in% BIASIDX
    if (isb) rect(b$x - 0.075, b$y - 0.036, b$x + 0.075, b$y + 0.036,
                  col = col[i], border = "grey35")
    else rect(b$x - 0.072, b$y - 0.028, b$x + 0.072, b$y + 0.028,
              col = adjustcolor("white", 0.8), border = NA)
    dark <- abs(tone(v[i], vmax, k)) > 0.62
    text(b$x, b$y, sprintf(paste0("%s=%.", digits, "f"), b$sym, v[i]),
         cex = 0.85, font = if (isb) 1 else 2,
         col = if (isb) { if (dark) "white" else "black" }
               else if (dark) col[i] else "grey20")
  }
  if (arrows) for (r in seq_len(nrow(ARROWS))) {
    a <- ARROWS[r, ]
    if (a$horiz)                                   # left / right: -, +
      polygon(a$ax + a$dir * c(-0.013, -0.013, 0.015),
              a$ay + c(-0.033, 0.033, 0), col = "grey30", border = NA)
    else                                           # down / up: -, +
      polygon(a$ax + c(-0.026, 0.026, 0), a$ay + a$dir * c(-0.016, -0.016, 0.02),
              col = "grey30", border = NA)
  }
  ## signed colour bar
  xs <- seq(0.12, 1.08, length.out = 201)
  rect(xs, -0.24 + yb, xs + diff(xs)[1], -0.19 + yb, col = DIV, border = NA)
  lab <- formatC(vmax, format = "g", digits = 2)
  text(c(0.12, 0.60, 1.08), -0.16 + yb, c(paste0("-", lab), "0", paste0("+", lab)),
       cex = 0.72)
}

                            selected = 20, width = "100%"))))),
      conditionalPanel(paste0(a, " == 'lbfgs'"),

            helpText("The step length comes from a Wolfe line search."))))
  )
}
